readings.title: Dazi—a New Way to Team up
readings.text: When Ne Zha 2 was on general release in cinemas in 2025, numerous youths turned to the Internet to look for "movie dazi". Serving as a fresh and hassle-free approach to making friends, this trend enables them to find like-minded partners without being burdened by the heavy lifting of maintaining the relationship. A 24-year-old office worker in Chengdu, who posted a message on social media three days ahead of the movie's release, conveying her hope of finding a companion to share the touching experience, succeeded in locating a girl from the same neighbourhood within half an hour. She said that she bought some ice cream in advance and received tissues from her companion when she was moved to tears, and they talked about the plot enthusiastically on their way home, even holding the same opinions about the story. She emphasized that without this dazi, she would have just returned home in silence instead of having such an enjoyable time. A 30-year-old mother, who prefers a "playground dazi", connected with a mum with a baby of the same age online last month. They took turns looking after the babies, shared a family meal, and even planned to go to the zoo next week, despite not knowing each other's full names. She mentioned that she didn't have to brainstorm topics for casual conversation, which gave her an additional thirty minutes to play football with her child. However, every coin has two sides. Seeking a dazi can be a double-edged sword. Friends you meet online who like the same things may have bad plans in reality. So it is vital to think twice when finding a dazi.
readings.translation: 当《哪吒2》于2025年在电影院公映时，众多的年轻人涌向互联网寻找"电影搭子"。作为一种新的且省心的交友方式，这一趋势使他们能够找到志同道合的伙伴，而无需承受维护关系所带来的沉重负担。成都一名24岁上班族在电影上映三天前在社交媒体上发布消息，表达了她想找个搭子一起分享感人观影体验的期望，结果在半个小时内就成功找到一个同街区的女孩。她说，她提前买了些冰淇淋，并在感动得落泪时收到了同伴递来的纸巾，然后，她们在回家的路上热烈地讨论影片情节，甚至对故事的看法也不谋而合。她还强调，如果没有这个搭子，她原本只会沉默地返回家中，而不是度过如此令人愉快的一段时光。一位30岁的母亲更喜欢"娃搭子"，上个月，她在网上与一位有着同龄宝宝的妈妈取得了联系。她们轮流照看孩子，一起家庭聚餐，甚至还计划下个星期一起去动物园，尽管她们连彼此的全名都不知道。她提到，自己不必再为闲聊头脑风暴找话题，这给了她额外的三十分钟可以陪孩子踢足球。然而，正如每枚硬币都有两面。寻找搭子也可能是一把双刃剑。网上志同道合的伙伴现实中可能别有意图。因此，找搭子时再三考虑至关重要。

readings.title: A Colour Walk
readings.text: What do you usually focus on while taking a walk outdoors? If you often find your mind wandering to past regrets or future anxieties and wish to stay grounded in the moment, a colour walk is absolutely a wonderful practice worth trying. A colour walk refers to a slow, mindful stroll outdoors that helps us free ourselves from messy thoughts and connect with the world around us. To start this little activity, all you need to do is to pick a colour you like, such as bright yellow, gentle blue or fresh green. As you walk along the street, keep your eyes open and try to spot everything that matches your chosen colour. You might come across a bright yellow wall, a passer-by wearing a yellow sweater, or a yellow outdoor chair beside a quiet cafe. To turn it into a healthy lifestyle, you can select a different colour every time you head out for a walk, which makes the whole experience feel like an interesting and refreshing game. Numerous scientific studies have shown that colour walks bring remarkable benefits to our mental health. They can effectively calm our nervous system, ease tension and reduce feelings of stress and anxiety. By engaging our senses, colour walks pull our attention back to the present moment, preventing us from being trapped in negative emotions. This trend has even reached several Chinese cities, where local authorities have designed tours with special colour themes. In Zhengzhou, the local officials have designed a pink-themed trip, guiding people to the city zoo, local gardens, and Fuxi Mountain to enjoy peach blossoms. Meanwhile, in Nanjing, the government mapped out a green-themed tour, inviting walkers to view willow trees at Yuyuan Garden, taste springtime qingtuan, and stroll through tea plantations. Pick a colour and go for a colour walk today!
readings.translation: 你在户外散步时，通常会关注些什么？如果你总是走神，沉溺于过去的遗憾或是对未来的焦虑，想要静下心活在当下，那么色彩漫步绝对是一个值得尝试的好方式。色彩漫步指的是一种缓慢、在户外的静心漫步方式，它能帮我们摆脱杂乱的想法并与我们周围的世界建立联结。想要开启这项小活动，你所要做的就是挑选一种你喜欢的颜色，比如明亮的黄色、柔和的蓝色或是清新的绿色。当你沿街行走时，静大双眼，尽力发现所有和你所选的颜色一致的事物。你可能会偶然发现一面明黄色的墙、一位穿着黄色毛衣的路人，或是一把在安静的咖啡馆旁边的黄色户外座椅。若想把它转变成健康的生活方式，每次出门散步你都可以选择一种不同的颜色，整个过程就会变得像一场趣味十足、别具一格的小游戏。大量科学研究表明，色彩漫步对我们的心理健康有显著的益处。它能有效地平复我们的神经系统、缓解紧张并减轻压力与焦虑。通过感官吸引，色彩漫步能将我们的注意力拉回到当下，防止我们被负面情绪困住。这一风潮也蔓延至中国多座城市，地方政府设计了特色的色彩主题游览路线。在郑州，当地政府打造了粉色主题路线，带领市民逛市动物园、游当地花园、登伏羲山赏桃花。与此同时，在南京，政府则规划了绿色主题路线，邀请游人观赏垂柳、品尝春日青团，漫步穿行于茶园之间。挑选一种颜色，今天就来一场色彩漫步吧！

readings.title: From Writing to Empathy-
readings.text: In my ninth-grade writing class last year, I met a diverse cast of characters created by my students brave cowboy who rescued his town and a demanding father who insisted on outstanding school-work. More than once, I couldn't help wondering how my students, the creators of these characters, had such a thorough understanding of their subjects. However, things were totally different for their first writing. The essay prompt was “Why is writing important?" Most of the papers were less than a page long, and very few contained a clear thesis statement. I was shocked. It soon became clear to me that the issue was with the question itself. While they might have written many volumes about the necessity of computers, the act of writing itself simply did not seem significant to them. Clearly, this perspective needed to change. When a new unit began, I asked everyone to compose a persuasive piece on a health-related topic of their choice. This time, they found the task much more interesting. For the following two -a personal narrative unit followed assignments- by a creative writing works hopI simply required that their work meet the type requirements and include a thesis. The results were astonishing. The students explored various topics and submitted stories, each ranging from 10 to 20 pages, shaping characters that broadened my view and touched my heart. I had entered the classroom believing that writing was important primarily as atool for communication. However, my students demonstrated something far more profound. When the final bell rang in June, I left with a yearbook full of messages revealing writing's most powerful significance-the ability to connect people, to allow us to walk in another's shoes, and to teach us what it truly means to be human. -ment
readings.translation: 去年在九年级（grade）写作（writing）课（class）上，我逼见（meet）了学生们（student）塑造的形形色色的（diverse）人物形象（cast of character）位拯教了（rescue）自己小镇的勇敢的（brave）牛仔（cowboy）和一位坚持要求（insist on）让孩子学业拔尖的严苛的（demanding）父亲。不止一次，我恐不住想知道（wonder）：我的学生们，作为这些人物的创造者，怎么会对自已笔下的角色有如此透彻的（thorough）理解（understanding）？然而，他们的第一次写作时的表现截然不同。那篇作文题目（essay prompt）是“为什么写作很重要？”大多数文章的篇幅都少于一页，而且几乎没有几篇能包含清晰的（clear）中心论点（thesis statement）。我很震惊。但很快我就明白了，问题出在题目本身。尽管他们或许能长篇大论地阐述（write many volumes）电脑的必要性（necessity），但写作这个行为（act）本身在他们看来似乎一点都不重要。显然，这种观点（perspective）需要改变。当一个新的单元（unit）开始时，我让每个人都围绕自己选择的健康相关话题撰写（compose）一篇有说服力的（persuasive）文章。这一次，他们觉得这项任务有趣（interesting）多了。在接下来的（following）两项任务（assignment）中一先是个人（personal）叙述单元，然后是创意写作工坊（workshop）一一我只要求他们的作品满足文章类型（type）要求（requirement），并且包含一个论点。结果令人惊诉（astonishing）。学生们探讨了各种各样的话题，提交（submit）的故事每篇都有10到20页，塑造（shape）的人物拓宽了我的视野（view），也触动（touch）了我的心（heart）。我走进教室（classroom）时，曾认为（believe）写作的重要性主要就是作为一种交流（communication）工具（tool）。然而，我的学生们向我展示（demonstrate）了远比这更为深刻的（profound）东西。六月最后的（final）铃声响起（ring）时，我带着一本写满留言的毕业纪念册离开了。这些留言揭示了写作最强大的意义（significance）-一它能联结人与人，让我们换位思考，也教会我们生而为人真正意味着（mean）什么。

readings.title: Discover the Magic of Reading
readings.text: Many professors have noticed a worrying trend students are struggling with reading more than ever. This isn't just about choosing phones over books. It gradually hurts their studies and future careers. In a world where short videos catch our attention all the time, long articles often feel like boring work rather than a pleasure. There are several signs of the decline in students' reading skills. First, students focus too much on small facts but miss the main point. Second, they are so used to short social media posts that thick books seem scary. Some students even doubt the value of reading, thinking it is out of date and choosing video content or AI summaries instead. The results are severe. Students who find reading difficult often can't understand complex ideas in their studies. They also can't express their thoughts clearly in writing. Besides schoolwork, they miss out on the hidden benefits of reading, such as stronger empathy and sharper critical thinking. So, what is deep reading? It trains your brain to follow long arguments and notice small details. It builds focus and independent judgment. It actually strengthens the connections in your brain related to language and logic. These are skills that skimming or AI summaries cannot give you. To improve reading skills, students can use active reading methods, like underlining key points and putting away their phones to avoid distractions. They should slowly build up their reading “muscles" by reading a little bit more each day. Teachers can found book clubs where students can share ideas. Schools should build a school culture that truly celebrates reading. Improving reading skills isn't about complaining about technology or giving students more books. It is about lighting the fire of deep reading again. By diving into a good book, we prepare ourselves not just for exams, but for a complex world that needs clear thinkers and kind hearts.
readings.translation: 许多教授都注意到（notice）了一个令人担忧的（worrying）趋势（trend）一一学生们的阅读变得比以往更加吃力（struggle）。这不仅仅是学生们更倾向于选择（choose）手机而不是书籍这么简单。这逐渐（gradually）还会对他们的学业和未来的职业生涯（career）有不良影响（hurt）。在一个短（short）视频总是吸引我们注意力的世界里，长篇文章（article）读起来如同乏味的（boring）任务，而不是一种乐趣。学生们阅读能力下降（decline）有以下几个迹象。首先，他们过于关注（focus）细枝末节，却忽略了文章主旨。其次，他们早已习惯简短的社交（social）媒体（media）帖子，以至于厚的（thick）书籍看起来令人畏惧。有些学生甚至怀疑（doubt）阅读的价值（value），认为它已经过时，转而选择视频内容（content）或人工智能摘要（summary）来代替（instead）。其结果是十分严重的（severe）。那些觉得阅读困难的学生往往无法理解学习中的复杂概念。他们在写作中也无法清晰地表达（express）自己的想法（thought）。除了学业之外（besides），他们还错失了阅读所带来的潜在好处（benefit），比如更强的共鸣（empathy）能力和更敏锐的（sharp）批判性思维。那么，什么是深度阅读呢？它能训练（train）大脑去跟随穴长的论述（argument）并注意到微小的细节（detail）。它能培养专注力和独立的（independent）判断力（judgment）。实际上，它还会加强你大脑中与语言和逻辑（logic）相关的（related）神经联结。这些技能是略读（skim）或人工智能摘要无法给予你的。想要提高阅读能力，学生可以采用主动（active）阅读法，比如在文中画出（underline）关键点，并且收好手机避免（avoid）分心（distraction）。他们应该通过每天多读一点儿（a little bit）的方式逐步增强自己的阅读“肌肉”（muscle）。教师可以成立（found）读书俱乐部（club）供学生们分享（share）想法。学校应该营造一种真正（truly）颂扬（celebrate）阅读的校园文化（culture）。提高阅读能力并不是抱怨（complain）科技或者给学生多提供一些书籍。而是重新点燃深度阅读的热情（fire）。通过沉浸（dive）到一本好书中，我们不仅能为考试做好准备（prepare），还能为复杂的世界做好准备一一这个世界需要思路清晰（thinker）、内心善良的人。

sentences.en: Many professors have noticed a worrying trend students are struggling with reading more than ever.
sentences.cn: 许多教授都注意到（notice）了一个令人担忧的（worrying）趋势（trend）一一学生们的阅读变得比以往更加吃力（struggle）。

sentences.en: This isn't just about choosing phones over books.
sentences.cn: 这不仅仅是学生们更倾向于选择（choose）手机而不是书籍这么简单。

sentences.en: It gradually hurts their studies and future careers.
sentences.cn: 这逐渐（gradually）还会对他们的学业和未来的职业生涯（career）有不良影响（hurt）。

sentences.en: In a world where short videos catch our attention all the time, long articles often feel like boring work rather than a pleasure.
sentences.cn: 在一个短（short）视频总是吸引我们注意力的世界里，长篇文章（article）读起来如同乏味的（boring）任务，而不是一种乐趣。

sentences.en: There are several signs of the decline in students' reading skills.
sentences.cn: 学生们阅读能力下降（decline）有以下几个迹象。

sentences.en: First, students focus too much on small facts but miss the main point.
sentences.cn: 首先，他们过于关注（focus）细枝末节，却忽略了文章主旨。

sentences.en: Second, they are so used to short social media posts that thick books seem scary.
sentences.cn: 其次，他们早已习惯简短的社交（social）媒体（media）帖子，以至于厚的（thick）书籍看起来令人畏惧。

sentences.en: Some students even doubt the value of reading, thinking it is out of date and choosing video content or AI summaries instead.
sentences.cn: 有些学生甚至怀疑（doubt）阅读的价值（value），认为它已经过时，转而选择视频内容（content）或人工智能摘要（summary）来代替（instead）。

sentences.en: The results are severe.
sentences.cn: 其结果是十分严重的（severe）。

sentences.en: Students who find reading difficult often can't understand complex ideas in their studies.
sentences.cn: 那些觉得阅读困难的学生往往无法理解学习中的复杂概念。

sentences.en: They also can't express their thoughts clearly in writing.
sentences.cn: 他们在写作中也无法清晰地表达（express）自己的想法（thought）。

sentences.en: Besides schoolwork, they miss out on the hidden benefits of reading, such as stronger empathy and sharper critical thinking.
sentences.cn: 除了学业之外（besides），他们还错失了阅读所带来的潜在好处（benefit），比如更强的共鸣（empathy）能力和更敏锐的（sharp）批判性思维。

sentences.en: So, what is deep reading?
sentences.cn: 那么，什么是深度阅读呢？

sentences.en: It trains your brain to follow long arguments and notice small details.
sentences.cn: 它能训练（train）大脑去跟随穴长的论述（argument）并注意到微小的细节（detail）。

sentences.en: It builds focus and independent judgment.
sentences.cn: 它能培养专注力和独立的（independent）判断力（judgment）。

sentences.en: It actually strengthens the connections in your brain related to language and logic.
sentences.cn: 实际上，它还会加强你大脑中与语言和逻辑（logic）相关的（related）神经联结。

sentences.en: These are skills that skimming or AI summaries cannot give you.
sentences.cn: 这些技能是略读（skim）或人工智能摘要无法给予你的。

sentences.en: To improve reading skills, students can use active reading methods, like underlining key points and putting away their phones to avoid distractions.
sentences.cn: 想要提高阅读能力，学生可以采用主动（active）阅读法，比如在文中画出（underline）关键点，并且收好手机避免（avoid）分心（distraction）。

sentences.en: They should slowly build up their reading “muscles" by reading a little bit more each day.
sentences.cn: 他们应该通过每天多读一点儿（a little bit）的方式逐步增强自己的阅读“肌肉”（muscle）。

sentences.en: Teachers can found book clubs where students can share ideas.
sentences.cn: 教师可以成立（found）读书俱乐部（club）供学生们分享（share）想法。

sentences.en: Schools should build a school culture that truly celebrates reading.
sentences.cn: 学校应该营造一种真正（truly）颂扬（celebrate）阅读的校园文化（culture）。

sentences.en: Improving reading skills isn't about complaining about technology or giving students more books.
sentences.cn: 提高阅读能力并不是抱怨（complain）科技或者给学生多提供一些书籍。

sentences.en: It is about lighting the fire of deep reading again.
sentences.cn: 而是重新点燃深度阅读的热情（fire）。

sentences.en: By diving into a good book, we prepare ourselves not just for exams, but for a complex world that needs clear thinkers and kind hearts.
sentences.cn: 通过沉浸（dive）到一本好书中，我们不仅能为考试做好准备（prepare），还能为复杂的世界做好准备一一这个世界需要思路清晰（thinker）、内心善良的人。

readings.title: Broken Bed, Better Body
readings.text: My name is Jack, and I still vividly recall the first day of my middle school life. I walked into my newly assigned dormitory and sat down on the wooden bed that belonged to me. Suddenly, the bed broke in half, which was a great surprise! As my new roommate stared at me in complete shock, my face instantly turned red with shame. What an embarrassing moment that was! Clearly, the accident happened not because the bed was of poor quality, but simply because I was overweight. Nowadays, more and more people are struggling with being overweight, which has become a growing concern. Some individuals claim that they are far too occupied with their work or daily routines to spare any time for physical exercise. Moreover, having no time to cook at home, they often choose to eat out or order take aways as a convenient alternative. Actually, you don't need a large amount of free time in order to stay healthy. After I broke that poor bed, my dad advised me to lose weight and stay energetic in my daily life. I accepted his suggestion, which has benefited me greatly. I rode my bike ten kilometers home, or got off one stop early to cover the rest of the distance. Besides, I also cut down on junk food and ate more vegetables and fruit. Daily exercise and a healthy diet proved very helpful for me, as I am now 21 kilograms lighter than before. Some of my health problems have also improved as a result. Looking back, that embarrassing incident turned out to be a turning point in my life. It made me realize the importance of a healthy weight and good living habits. Since then, I've decided to change and stick to it. You certainly don't have to break a bed to start your own health path. To keep fit, take timely measures. Even small changes will make a significant difference! badminton baseball volleyball sit-up ice hockey rope skipping jogging yoga
readings.translation: 我叫杰克，我仍然（still）能清晰地（vividly）回想起（recall）我的中学（middle school）生活（life）的第一天。那天我走进新分配（assign）的宿舍（dormitory），坐在属于（belong to）我的那张木制的（wooden）床（bed）上。突然间，床折断（break）成了两半，着实是意外之事（surprise）！我的新室友（roommate）万分震惊（incomplete shock）地町着（star eat）我看，我顿时（instantly）差愧（shame）得满脸通红（red）。那是多么令人难堪的（embarrassing）瞬间（moment）！显然，这件事并不是因为床的质量差（poor）才发生（happen）的，仅仅是因为我超重（overweight）了。现在（nowadays），越来越多的人受超重问题围扰，这也成了人们愈发关注的事（concern）。有些人声称（claim）自己平日忙于（be occupied with）工作和日常生活（daily routine），根本留（spare）不出时间锻炼身体。此外（moreover）由于没时间在家做饭，他们常常选择外出就餐（eat out）或点（order）外卖（takeaway），作为一种方便的（convenient）备选方案（alternative）。其实，为了保持健康（healthy），你并不需要大量的空闲时间。自从我压坏了那张可怜的床后，我爸爸就建议（advise）我减重（lose weight），并在日常生活中保持精力充沛（energetic）。我接受（accept）了他的建议（suggestion），也因此受益匪浅。我骑行十公里回家，或是提前一站下车，步行走完（cover）剩下的路程（distance）。此外，我还减少吃垃圾食品，并且多吃蔬菜和水果。日常锻炼和健康的饮食（diet）对我很有帮助，现在我比以前轻（light）了21公斤，一些健康问题也因此有所改善。回首过往，那件令人难堪的事件（incident）竞成了我人生的转折点。它让我意识到健康体重和良好生活习惯（habit）的重要性。从那以后，我下定决心改变自己并一直坚持（stick to）。你当然不必压坏一张床才开启自己的健康之路（path）。想要保持健康（keep fit），就要及时采取措施（measure）。即使是微小的改变，也能带来显著的（significant）不同（difference）！

sentences.en: My name is Jack, and I still vividly recall the first day of my middle school life.
sentences.cn: 我叫杰克，我仍然（still）能清晰地（vividly）回想起（recall）我的中学（middle school）生活（life）的第一天。

sentences.en: I walked into my newly assigned dormitory and sat down on the wooden bed that belonged to me.
sentences.cn: 那天我走进新分配（assign）的宿舍（dormitory），坐在属于（belong to）我的那张木制的（wooden）床（bed）上。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the bed broke in half, which was a great surprise!
sentences.cn: 突然间，床折断（break）成了两半，着实是意外之事（surprise）！

sentences.en: As my new roommate stared at me in complete shock, my face instantly turned red with shame.
sentences.cn: 我的新室友（roommate）万分震惊（incomplete shock）地町着（star eat）我看，我顿时（instantly）差愧（shame）得满脸通红（red）。

sentences.en: What an embarrassing moment that was!
sentences.cn: 那是多么令人难堪的（embarrassing）瞬间（moment）！

sentences.en: Clearly, the accident happened not because the bed was of poor quality, but simply because I was overweight.
sentences.cn: 显然，这件事并不是因为床的质量差（poor）才发生（happen）的，仅仅是因为我超重（overweight）了。

sentences.en: Nowadays, more and more people are struggling with being overweight, which has become a growing concern.
sentences.cn: 现在（nowadays），越来越多的人受超重问题围扰，这也成了人们愈发关注的事（concern）。

sentences.en: Some individuals claim that they are far too occupied with their work or daily routines to spare any time for physical exercise.
sentences.cn: 有些人声称（claim）自己平日忙于（be occupied with）工作和日常生活（daily routine），根本留（spare）不出时间锻炼身体。

sentences.en: Moreover, having no time to cook at home, they often choose to eat out or order take aways as a convenient alternative.
sentences.cn: 此外（moreover）由于没时间在家做饭，他们常常选择外出就餐（eat out）或点（order）外卖（takeaway），作为一种方便的（convenient）备选方案（alternative）。

sentences.en: Actually, you don't need a large amount of free time in order to stay healthy.
sentences.cn: 其实，为了保持健康（healthy），你并不需要大量的空闲时间。

sentences.en: After I broke that poor bed, my dad advised me to lose weight and stay energetic in my daily life.
sentences.cn: 自从我压坏了那张可怜的床后，我爸爸就建议（advise）我减重（lose weight），并在日常生活中保持精力充沛（energetic）。

sentences.en: I accepted his suggestion, which has benefited me greatly.
sentences.cn: 我接受（accept）了他的建议（suggestion），也因此受益匪浅。

sentences.en: I rode my bike ten kilometers home, or got off one stop early to cover the rest of the distance.
sentences.cn: 我骑行十公里回家，或是提前一站下车，步行走完（cover）剩下的路程（distance）。

sentences.en: Besides, I also cut down on junk food and ate more vegetables and fruit.
sentences.cn: 此外，我还减少吃垃圾食品，并且多吃蔬菜和水果。

sentences.en: Daily exercise and a healthy diet proved very helpful for me, as I am now 21 kilograms lighter than before. Some of my health problems have also improved as a result.
sentences.cn: 日常锻炼和健康的饮食（diet）对我很有帮助，现在我比以前轻（light）了21公斤，一些健康问题也因此有所改善。

sentences.en: Looking back, that embarrassing incident turned out to be a turning point in my life.
sentences.cn: 回首过往，那件令人难堪的事件（incident）竞成了我人生的转折点。

sentences.en: It made me realize the importance of a healthy weight and good living habits.
sentences.cn: 它让我意识到健康体重和良好生活习惯（habit）的重要性。

readings.title: Sound Baths-a Nice Way to Relax
readings.text: The relaxing power of sound is something we all recognize in our daily lives. When your favourite song comes on, the stress of the day seems to fade away. Or consider the peace that washes over you when you hear raindrops tapping softly against the leaves. These sounds have a natural ability to calm our racing minds. Sound baths take this basic idea and turn it into a more structured experience. Do not be cheated by the word “bath"-this activity does not require you to get wet at all. Rather, a sound bath is an event where you find yourself completely surrounded by peaceful tones. So what exactly makes these sounds? They come from special instruments played by practitioners, not tapes. Common tools include gongs, bells, tuning forks, and especially singing bowls-metal or crystal vessels that make deep, soothing tones. They can be struck for a clear ring or rubbed to create a continuous, space-filling vibration. During a session, you lie comfortably on a mat and listen. The practitioner creates an ever-changing landscape of sound. Sometimes the tones are low and rumbling; other times they are clear and high. People naturally enter a meditative state, with a quiet mind and a relaxed body. Sound baths have ancient roots in traditional Chinese medicine and Indian wellness practices. Both suggest that the vibrations produced by these instruments can help clear blockages in the body's flow of energy, thereby restoring a sense of balance and health. Modern science offers another angle- these low-frequency sounds and steady rhythms may shift our brainwave patterns. Instead of staying in an alert state, the brain may move toward slower, more relaxed rhythms associated with deep rest. Despite the fact that experts agree more studies are necessary to understand the medical effects, many people continue to share positive stories. They frequently mention feeling less overwhelmed by stress and enjoying a much better sleep after attending a session. wisdom or modern Whether seen through ancient science, sound baths offer a break from daily noise and make you refreshed and ready to face life again.
readings.translation: 声音（sound）的放松功效（power）是我们日常生活中都认可（recognize）的。当你听到自己喜爱的歌曲时，一天的精神压力（stress）似乎就会逐渐消失（fadeaway）。或者细想（consider）当你听到雨滴轻柔地敲打（tap）树叶时所涌上心头的那种宁静。这些声音具有让我们思绪纷乱的头脑平静下来（calm）的自然的（natural）能力（ability）。音浴（bath）沿用这一基本（basic）理念并将其转变为一种更为结构化的体验。不要被“洗澡”这个字眼所骗（cheat），这项活动一点也不需要你弄湿自己。更确切地说（rather），音浴是一种会让你发现自己完全（completely）被宁静的音调（tone）包围（surround）的活动。那么，这些声音究竞（exactly）是什么产生的呢？它们来自于从业者们演奏的特殊乐器（instrument），而非录音带（tape）。常见的（common）工具包括锣、铃（bell）、音叉（tuning fork），尤其（especially）是颂钵金属（metal）或水晶制成的器皿，能发出深沉、舒缓的音调。它们可以被敲击（strike）发出清亮的回响或被摩擦产生（create）持续的、充满空间的振动（vibration）。在一个疗程（session）中，你舒适地躺在垫子（mat）上聆听。从业者会创造出不断变化的声音景观（landscape）。有时音调低沉浑厚，有时它们则清亮高亢。人们自然而然地进入想状态（state），思绪宁静，身体放松（relaxed）音浴起源于（have ancient root sin）中国传统医学（medicine）和印度养生技法（practice）。这两种体系都认为，这些乐器产生（produce）的振动可以帮助清除身体能量流动中的淤堵，从而（thereby）恢复（restore）平衡（balance）与健康感。现代科学提供了另一种视角（angle）一一这些低频声音和平稳的（steady）节奏（rhythm）可能会改变我们的脑电波模式。大脑不再停留在警觉的状态，而是可能转向与深度休息相关的（associate with）更慢、更放松的节奏。尽管（despite）专家们认为进行更多的研究来了解其医学效果（effect）是必需的（necessary），但许多人仍持续（continue）分享积极的体验。他们经常提到（mention），在参加（attend）一个疗程后感觉不再被压力压倒（overwhelmed），并且睡眠也改善了。无论是从古老的智慧（wisdom）还是现代科学来看，音浴都能让你从日常的喧置中解脱出来，使你精神振作（refreshed），准备好再次面对生活。

sentences.en: The relaxing power of sound is something we all recognize in our daily lives.
sentences.cn: 声音（sound）的放松功效（power）是我们日常生活中都认可（recognize）的。

sentences.en: When your favourite song comes on, the stress of the day seems to fade away.
sentences.cn: 当你听到自己喜爱的歌曲时，一天的精神压力（stress）似乎就会逐渐消失（fadeaway）。

sentences.en: Or consider the peace that washes over you when you hear raindrops tapping softly against the leaves.
sentences.cn: 或者细想（consider）当你听到雨滴轻柔地敲打（tap）树叶时所涌上心头的那种宁静。

sentences.en: These sounds have a natural ability to calm our racing minds.
sentences.cn: 这些声音具有让我们思绪纷乱的头脑平静下来（calm）的自然的（natural）能力（ability）。

sentences.en: Sound baths take this basic idea and turn it into a more structured experience.
sentences.cn: 音浴（bath）沿用这一基本（basic）理念并将其转变为一种更为结构化的体验。

sentences.en: Do not be cheated by the word “bath"-this activity does not require you to get wet at all.
sentences.cn: 不要被“洗澡”这个字眼所骗（cheat），这项活动一点也不需要你弄湿自己。

sentences.en: Rather, a sound bath is an event where you find yourself completely surrounded by peaceful tones.
sentences.cn: 更确切地说（rather），音浴是一种会让你发现自己完全（completely）被宁静的音调（tone）包围（surround）的活动。

sentences.en: So what exactly makes these sounds?
sentences.cn: 那么，这些声音究竞（exactly）是什么产生的呢？

sentences.en: They come from special instruments played by practitioners, not tapes.
sentences.cn: 它们来自于从业者们演奏的特殊乐器（instrument），而非录音带（tape）。

sentences.en: Common tools include gongs, bells, tuning forks, and especially singing bowls-metal or crystal vessels that make deep, soothing tones.
sentences.cn: 常见的（common）工具包括锣、铃（bell）、音叉（tuning fork），尤其（especially）是颂钵金属（metal）或水晶制成的器皿，能发出深沉、舒缓的音调。

sentences.en: They can be struck for a clear ring or rubbed to create a continuous, space-filling vibration.
sentences.cn: 它们可以被敲击（strike）发出清亮的回响或被摩擦产生（create）持续的、充满空间的振动（vibration）。

sentences.en: During a session, you lie comfortably on a mat and listen.
sentences.cn: 在一个疗程（session）中，你舒适地躺在垫子（mat）上聆听。

sentences.en: The practitioner creates an ever-changing landscape of sound.
sentences.cn: 从业者会创造出不断变化的声音景观（landscape）。

sentences.en: Sometimes the tones are low and rumbling; other times they are clear and high.
sentences.cn: 有时音调低沉浑厚，有时它们则清亮高亢。

sentences.en: People naturally enter a meditative state, with a quiet mind and a relaxed body. Sound baths have ancient roots in traditional Chinese medicine and Indian wellness practices.
sentences.cn: 人们自然而然地进入想状态（state），思绪宁静，身体放松（relaxed）音浴起源于（have ancient root sin）中国传统医学（medicine）和印度养生技法（practice）。

sentences.en: Both suggest that the vibrations produced by these instruments can help clear blockages in the body's flow of energy, thereby restoring a sense of balance and health.
sentences.cn: 这两种体系都认为，这些乐器产生（produce）的振动可以帮助清除身体能量流动中的淤堵，从而（thereby）恢复（restore）平衡（balance）与健康感。

sentences.en: Modern science offers another angle- these low-frequency sounds and steady rhythms may shift our brainwave patterns.
sentences.cn: 现代科学提供了另一种视角（angle）一一这些低频声音和平稳的（steady）节奏（rhythm）可能会改变我们的脑电波模式。

sentences.en: Instead of staying in an alert state, the brain may move toward slower, more relaxed rhythms associated with deep rest.
sentences.cn: 大脑不再停留在警觉的状态，而是可能转向与深度休息相关的（associate with）更慢、更放松的节奏。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that experts agree more studies are necessary to understand the medical effects, many people continue to share positive stories.
sentences.cn: 尽管（despite）专家们认为进行更多的研究来了解其医学效果（effect）是必需的（necessary），但许多人仍持续（continue）分享积极的体验。

sentences.en: They frequently mention feeling less overwhelmed by stress and enjoying a much better sleep after attending a session.
sentences.cn: 他们经常提到（mention），在参加（attend）一个疗程后感觉不再被压力压倒（overwhelmed），并且睡眠也改善了。

sentences.en: wisdom or modern Whether seen through ancient science, sound baths offer a break from daily noise and make you refreshed and ready to face life again.
sentences.cn: 无论是从古老的智慧（wisdom）还是现代科学来看，音浴都能让你从日常的喧置中解脱出来，使你精神振作（refreshed），准备好再次面对生活。

readings.title: Say No to Smoking
readings.text: Smoking brings heavy financial and health burdens to individuals and society, becoming a serious problem that needs urgent attention. Financially, the cost of cigarettes is significant, and daily purchases add up to a large monthly expense, which wastes money that could be used for other activities. As pointed out by the Health Commission of Shenzhen Municipality, the financial pressure becomes much worse when smoking causes illnesses- expensive medical fees, costly medicines and is much larger than the price of cigarettes. Shenzhen takes the lead in the national “smoke- free city" activity to protect non-smokers. Second- hand smoke, a harmful mixture of more than 7, o00 chemicals including at least 69 proven cancer- causing substances, is a silent killer. It poses a great threat to public health and violates the rights of innocent bystanders. The terrible smell fills closed spaces and cars, causing great dislike, bringing on bad headaches and increasing the risk of heart disease and lung cancer in non-smokers. That is why smoking is banned in all indoor public areas in Shenzhen, like train stations and even some outdoor places like metro entrances. Most importantly, smoking causes serious damage to the body. Smokers often suffer from long- term coughing and serious shortness of breath, which get worse when they exercise or have diseases like asthma. Tobacco smoke badly harms lung tissue. It also puts more pressure on the heart, speeds up skin aging and is linked to dozens of diseases, greatly increasing the risk of early death. The WHO says tobacco kills more than 8 million people every year, including 1.2 million non-smokers. Giving up smoking is the most effective way to protect your health. Shenzhen's “15-Minute Smoking Cessation Circle" in 933 community health centers provides easy access to help. Refuse the temptation of tobacco, and work together to build a healthier, better smoke-free future for everyone. cigarette money health debt high cost long-term medical
readings.translation: 吸烟给个人（individual）和社会（society）带来了沉况重的（heavy）财政（financial）和健康负担（burden），已成为一个需要迫切（urgent）关注的严重问题。从经济层面来看，香烟（cigarette）的花费是不容小靓的，日常购买（purchase）的开销合计起来，每月（monthly）就是一笔巨大的开支（expense），浪费了本可以用于其他活动的钱（money）。正如深圳市卫生健康委员会所指出（point out）的那样，当吸烟引发（cause）疾病（illness）的时候，财政的压力（pressure）会变得更加严重一一昂责的（expensive）医疗费用（fee）、高价的药物以及频繁的（frequent）就医会形成一笔远远超过香烟价格的况重的“健康债务（debt）”深圳在全国“无烟城市”活动中率先（take the lead）开展行动，以保护非吸烟者。二手烟是一种包含超过7000种化学物质的有害混合物（mixture），其中包括（include）至少（at least）69种已被证实的致癌物质，是一个况默的（silent）杀手。它对公众健康构成巨大威胁（threat），并侵犯（violate）了无率的（innocent）旁观者的权利（right）。这种糟糕的（terrible）气味充斥于封闭空间和车辆内，造成人们极度的反感（dislike），导致严重的头痛（headache），并增加非吸烟者患心脏病（heart disease）和肺癌（cancer）的风险。这就是为什么在深圳，所有室内公共场所都禁止（ban）吸烟，比如火车站（station），甚至一些户外场所，如地铁入口处（entrance）。最重要的是，吸烟会对身体造成严重损害（damage）。吸烟者往往遭受（suffer from）长期咳嗽（cough）和严重气短的困扰，尤其是在锻炼（exercise）时或有哮喘等疾病时情况会更严重。烟草（tobacco）烟雾会严重损伤（harm）肺组织（tissue）。它还会增加心脏负担，加速皮肤（skin）老化，并与几十种不同的疾病有关，极大增加了早逝（death）的风险。世界卫生组织表示，烟草每年杀死（kil）超过800万人，其中包括120万非吸烟者。成烟是保护健康最有效的（effective）方法。深圳在933个社区（community）健康服务中心推出的“15分钟戒烟图（circle）”提供（provide）了便捷获得帮助的机会（access）。拒绝（refiuse）烟草的诱感（temptation），共同努力为每个人创造一个更健康、更无烟的未来。

sentences.en: Smoking brings heavy financial and health burdens to individuals and society, becoming a serious problem that needs urgent attention.
sentences.cn: 吸烟给个人（individual）和社会（society）带来了沉况重的（heavy）财政（financial）和健康负担（burden），已成为一个需要迫切（urgent）关注的严重问题。

sentences.en: Financially, the cost of cigarettes is significant, and daily purchases add up to a large monthly expense, which wastes money that could be used for other activities.
sentences.cn: 从经济层面来看，香烟（cigarette）的花费是不容小靓的，日常购买（purchase）的开销合计起来，每月（monthly）就是一笔巨大的开支（expense），浪费了本可以用于其他活动的钱（money）。

sentences.en: As pointed out by the Health Commission of Shenzhen Municipality, the financial pressure becomes much worse when smoking causes illnesses- expensive medical fees, costly medicines and is much larger than the price of cigarettes. Shenzhen takes the lead in the national “smoke- free city" activity to protect non-smokers.
sentences.cn: 正如深圳市卫生健康委员会所指出（point out）的那样，当吸烟引发（cause）疾病（illness）的时候，财政的压力（pressure）会变得更加严重一一昂责的（expensive）医疗费用（fee）、高价的药物以及频繁的（frequent）就医会形成一笔远远超过香烟价格的况重的“健康债务（debt）”深圳在全国“无烟城市”活动中率先（take the lead）开展行动，以保护非吸烟者。

sentences.en: Second- hand smoke, a harmful mixture of more than 7, o00 chemicals including at least 69 proven cancer- causing substances, is a silent killer.
sentences.cn: 二手烟是一种包含超过7000种化学物质的有害混合物（mixture），其中包括（include）至少（at least）69种已被证实的致癌物质，是一个况默的（silent）杀手。

sentences.en: It poses a great threat to public health and violates the rights of innocent bystanders.
sentences.cn: 它对公众健康构成巨大威胁（threat），并侵犯（violate）了无率的（innocent）旁观者的权利（right）。

sentences.en: The terrible smell fills closed spaces and cars, causing great dislike, bringing on bad headaches and increasing the risk of heart disease and lung cancer in non-smokers.
sentences.cn: 这种糟糕的（terrible）气味充斥于封闭空间和车辆内，造成人们极度的反感（dislike），导致严重的头痛（headache），并增加非吸烟者患心脏病（heart disease）和肺癌（cancer）的风险。

sentences.en: That is why smoking is banned in all indoor public areas in Shenzhen, like train stations and even some outdoor places like metro entrances.
sentences.cn: 这就是为什么在深圳，所有室内公共场所都禁止（ban）吸烟，比如火车站（station），甚至一些户外场所，如地铁入口处（entrance）。

sentences.en: Most importantly, smoking causes serious damage to the body.
sentences.cn: 最重要的是，吸烟会对身体造成严重损害（damage）。

sentences.en: Smokers often suffer from long- term coughing and serious shortness of breath, which get worse when they exercise or have diseases like asthma.
sentences.cn: 吸烟者往往遭受（suffer from）长期咳嗽（cough）和严重气短的困扰，尤其是在锻炼（exercise）时或有哮喘等疾病时情况会更严重。

sentences.en: Tobacco smoke badly harms lung tissue.
sentences.cn: 烟草（tobacco）烟雾会严重损伤（harm）肺组织（tissue）。

sentences.en: It also puts more pressure on the heart, speeds up skin aging and is linked to dozens of diseases, greatly increasing the risk of early death.
sentences.cn: 它还会增加心脏负担，加速皮肤（skin）老化，并与几十种不同的疾病有关，极大增加了早逝（death）的风险。

sentences.en: The WHO says tobacco kills more than 8 million people every year, including 1. 2 million non-smokers.
sentences.cn: 世界卫生组织表示，烟草每年杀死（kil）超过800万人，其中包括120万非吸烟者。

sentences.en: Giving up smoking is the most effective way to protect your health.
sentences.cn: 成烟是保护健康最有效的（effective）方法。

sentences.en: Shenzhen's “15-Minute Smoking Cessation Circle" in 933 community health centers provides easy access to help.
sentences.cn: 深圳在933个社区（community）健康服务中心推出的“15分钟戒烟图（circle）”提供（provide）了便捷获得帮助的机会（access）。

sentences.en: Refuse the temptation of tobacco, and work together to build a healthier, better smoke-free future for everyone.
sentences.cn: 拒绝（refiuse）烟草的诱感（temptation），共同努力为每个人创造一个更健康、更无烟的未来。

readings.title: Courage to Pick up the Brush Again
readings.text: When I was a little girl, I had a passion for drawing, freely and joyously making marks on the walls at home. In primary school, I learned to write with chalk. Writing seemed to be another form of drawing. I shaped individual letters into repeating lines, which were abstract, delightful but meaningless patterns. In secondary school, art was my favourite subject. I spent all my leisure time exploring the beauty of art. Because I loved it so much, I was convinced I had a talent for it. For the art O-level exam, I had to present an oil painting. I found it challenging, but still expected to pass. I failed, with a low grade. I'd been overly confident. This failure hit me deeply and made me upset. I'd been declared talentless. But other channels of creativity stayed open- I went on writing poems and stories. Still, I often went to exhibitions. I continued my habitual drawing, which I now regarded as childish doodling. In my 30s, creativity ity I made friends with painters and gained a totally new understanding of art. However, I lacked the courage to let myself have a go at actually doing it. Though my acquaintances were abstract painters, printmakers or sculptors, I took oil painting as the taboo high form I dared not practise. One night in my early 40s, I dreamed that a big woman in red walked towards me, handed me a bag of paints, and encouraged me to start painting. I woke up immediately with strong inspiration. The dream was so powerful that it shook me. It was a form of energy, bringing back something I'd lost. Accordingly, I started by experimenting with watercolours. Finally, I bought some oil paints for drawing. Although I took delight in breaking my decades- long taboo about working with oil paints, I have discovered I now prefer chalk and ink. I let my line drawings turn into cartoons and send to friends. Instead of being anxious, I can accept my weaknesses but keep going this time. I enjoy complete freedom and peace of mind. Becoming a successful painter requires great determination. I realized I was always afraid of wanting too much. These fears once stopped me from making any progress. That dream reminded me that those fears and desires could motivate me to take risks and do experiments. Now I truly understand that growth matters more than success.
readings.translation: 当我还是一个小女孩时，我酷爱（havea passion for）绘画（drawing），自由自在、开心地在家中的墙上涂画。在小学（primary school），我学习（leam）用粉笔（chalk）写字。写字仿佛是画画的另一种（another）形式。我把单个字母（letter）塑造（shape）成重复的线条，这些线条是抽象的（abstract）、令人愉悦但（but）毫无意义的图案。中学时期，美术是我最喜欢的（favourite）学科（subject）。我把所有闲暇（leisure）时间都用来探寻艺术之美（beauty）。因为我十分热爱（love）它，我坚信（convinced）自己拥有艺术天赋。美术基础考试（exam）中，我必须提交（present）幅油画。我觉得这件事很具有挑战性（challenging），但依旧期待（expect）能够通过。最终我没能通过，成绩很差。我之前太过自信（confident）。这次失败（failure）深深打击了我，让我十分沮丧（upset）。我被宣告（declare）毫无艺术天赋。但仍有其他创作（creativity）途径（channel）-一我继续创作诗（poem）和故事。我也时常去看展览（exhibition）。我保持着平日里画画的习惯，只是如今我把它看待（regard）成幼稚的涂鸦。三十多岁时，我结识了画家朋友们，对艺术获得（gain）了完全（totally）薪新的理解。然而，我缺少让我自已（myself）真正（actually）动手尝试创作的勇气（courage）。虽然（though）我的熟人（acquaintance）有抽象画家、版画家或是雕刻家（sculptor），我却把油画视作高不可攀的禁区而不敢（dare）尝试。四十岁出头的一个夜晚，我梦见（dream）一位身形高大的红衣女子向（towards）我走来，递给（hand）我一袋颜料，并鼓励（encourage）我开始作画。我立刻醒来（wake），心中涌起强烈的灵感（inspiration）。这个梦非常有力量（power fi ul），深深震撼了我。它是一种能量（energy），带来（bring）了我遗失已久的重要的事物（something）。于是我先用水彩进行实验（experiment）。最后（finally），我为了绘画买了一些油画颜料（paint）。尽管我乐于（take delight in）打破数十年不画油画的禁忌，可我发现（discover）自己如今更喜欢粉笔与墨水。我把自己的线稿画改成漫画（cartoon）发给朋友们。这次，我不再忧虑（anxious），能够接纳自身的缺点（weakness），却坚持创作。我享受全然的自由（freedom）与内心（mind）的平和。成为一名成功的（successful）画家需要（require）强大的决心（determination）。我意识到我总是害怕（afraid）奢求太多。这些恐惧曾经阻止（stop）我取得任何进步（progress）。那个梦提醒（remind）了我，恐惧与期望（desire）能够激励（motivate）我去冒险、去实践探索。现在我真正理解（understand）了成长比成功更要紧（matter）。

sentences.en: When I was a little girl, I had a passion for drawing, freely and joyously making marks on the walls at home.
sentences.cn: 当我还是一个小女孩时，我酷爱（havea passion for）绘画（drawing），自由自在、开心地在家中的墙上涂画。

sentences.en: In primary school, I learned to write with chalk.
sentences.cn: 在小学（primary school），我学习（leam）用粉笔（chalk）写字。

sentences.en: Writing seemed to be another form of drawing.
sentences.cn: 写字仿佛是画画的另一种（another）形式。

sentences.en: I shaped individual letters into repeating lines, which were abstract, delightful but meaningless patterns.
sentences.cn: 我把单个字母（letter）塑造（shape）成重复的线条，这些线条是抽象的（abstract）、令人愉悦但（but）毫无意义的图案。

sentences.en: In secondary school, art was my favourite subject.
sentences.cn: 中学时期，美术是我最喜欢的（favourite）学科（subject）。

sentences.en: I spent all my leisure time exploring the beauty of art.
sentences.cn: 我把所有闲暇（leisure）时间都用来探寻艺术之美（beauty）。

sentences.en: Because I loved it so much, I was convinced I had a talent for it.
sentences.cn: 因为我十分热爱（love）它，我坚信（convinced）自己拥有艺术天赋。

sentences.en: For the art O-level exam, I had to present an oil painting.
sentences.cn: 美术基础考试（exam）中，我必须提交（present）幅油画。

sentences.en: I found it challenging, but still expected to pass.
sentences.cn: 我觉得这件事很具有挑战性（challenging），但依旧期待（expect）能够通过。

sentences.en: I failed, with a low grade.
sentences.cn: 最终我没能通过，成绩很差。

sentences.en: I'd been overly confident.
sentences.cn: 我之前太过自信（confident）。

sentences.en: This failure hit me deeply and made me upset.
sentences.cn: 这次失败（failure）深深打击了我，让我十分沮丧（upset）。

sentences.en: I'd been declared talentless.
sentences.cn: 我被宣告（declare）毫无艺术天赋。

sentences.en: But other channels of creativity stayed open- I went on writing poems and stories.
sentences.cn: 但仍有其他创作（creativity）途径（channel）-一我继续创作诗（poem）和故事。

sentences.en: Still, I often went to exhibitions.
sentences.cn: 我也时常去看展览（exhibition）。

sentences.en: I continued my habitual drawing, which I now regarded as childish doodling.
sentences.cn: 我保持着平日里画画的习惯，只是如今我把它看待（regard）成幼稚的涂鸦。

sentences.en: In my 30s, creativity ity I made friends with painters and gained a totally new understanding of art.
sentences.cn: 三十多岁时，我结识了画家朋友们，对艺术获得（gain）了完全（totally）薪新的理解。

sentences.en: However, I lacked the courage to let myself have a go at actually doing it.
sentences.cn: 然而，我缺少让我自已（myself）真正（actually）动手尝试创作的勇气（courage）。

sentences.en: Though my acquaintances were abstract painters, printmakers or sculptors, I took oil painting as the taboo high form I dared not practise.
sentences.cn: 虽然（though）我的熟人（acquaintance）有抽象画家、版画家或是雕刻家（sculptor），我却把油画视作高不可攀的禁区而不敢（dare）尝试。

sentences.en: One night in my early 40s, I dreamed that a big woman in red walked towards me, handed me a bag of paints, and encouraged me to start painting.
sentences.cn: 四十岁出头的一个夜晚，我梦见（dream）一位身形高大的红衣女子向（towards）我走来，递给（hand）我一袋颜料，并鼓励（encourage）我开始作画。

sentences.cn: 这个梦非常有力量（power fi ul），深深震撼了我。

sentences.en: It was a form of energy, bringing back something I'd lost.
sentences.cn: 它是一种能量（energy），带来（bring）了我遗失已久的重要的事物（something）。

sentences.en: Accordingly, I started by experimenting with watercolours.
sentences.cn: 于是我先用水彩进行实验（experiment）。

sentences.en: Finally, I bought some oil paints for drawing.
sentences.cn: 最后（finally），我为了绘画买了一些油画颜料（paint）。

sentences.en: Although I took delight in breaking my decades- long taboo about working with oil paints, I have discovered I now prefer chalk and ink.
sentences.cn: 尽管我乐于（take delight in）打破数十年不画油画的禁忌，可我发现（discover）自己如今更喜欢粉笔与墨水。

sentences.en: I let my line drawings turn into cartoons and send to friends.
sentences.cn: 我把自己的线稿画改成漫画（cartoon）发给朋友们。

sentences.en: Instead of being anxious, I can accept my weaknesses but keep going this time.
sentences.cn: 这次，我不再忧虑（anxious），能够接纳自身的缺点（weakness），却坚持创作。

sentences.en: I enjoy complete freedom and peace of mind.
sentences.cn: 我享受全然的自由（freedom）与内心（mind）的平和。

sentences.en: Becoming a successful painter requires great determination.
sentences.cn: 成为一名成功的（successful）画家需要（require）强大的决心（determination）。

sentences.en: I realized I was always afraid of wanting too much.

sentences.en: These fears once stopped me from making any progress.

sentences.en: That dream reminded me that those fears and desires could motivate me to take risks and do experiments.

readings.title: When you make a mistake
readings.text: When you make a mistake or say something wrong, you tend to be critical of yourself. Then stress is caused. You may get angry, feel disappointed and sink into sadness. Therefore, we ought to deal with stress properly. Max is a 16-year-old boy who used to be very competitive and suffer from constant stress. Now he is learning to give himself patience and kindness. When he doesn't win contests or get top marks, he whispers to himself, "It's OK not to be perfect." He knows he always makes full efforts and that is enough. What Max does is called self-compassion. With self-compassion, you behave toward yourself gently as you do to a close friend. It permits you to forgive yourself when you mess up or fail. After feelings of guilt go away, you get more peaceful and you can think more clearly. This way self-compassion drives you to move forward. Plenty of studies confirm that it is very helpful. However, some people disagree. They think self-compassion may lead people to be less active. But Brenes and Chen's research showed an opposite quiz result. They gave students a difficult vocabulary and let them review for a second quiz. They found those who were able to face their failure spent more time on revision. Specialists advise you to write a letter to yourself. Be honest in the letter, express your sadness and accept your true feelings. In addition, doing what you love is a useful way to attain inner peace. A psychologist suggests touching your chest gently with your hands. This gesture will make you feel safe and loved.
readings.translation: 当你犯错（mistake）或是说错（wrong）话时，往往会对自已（yourself）挑剔（be critical of）。随之便会产生压力。你可能会生气（angry）、感到沮丧（disappointed）并陷入（sink into）悲伤（sadness）。因此（therefore），我们应该（ought）正确地（properly）应对压力。麦克斯是一名16岁的男孩，他过去一心求胜（competitive），并且承受着持续不断的（constant）压力。如今他学着对自己多点耐心（patience）与宽容（kindness）。当他没能赢得比赛（contest）或是取得高分时，他会对自己小声说（whisper）：“不完美（perfect）也没关系。”他清楚自已总是全力以赴（make full efforts），这就足够（enough）了。麦克斯的这种做法被叫作（call）自我和解。拥有自我和解，你会像对待挚友一般对待自己，表现（behave）得温和友善。它允许（permit）你在搞砸（mess up）事情或失败（fail）时原谅（forgive）自已。当内疫（guilt）的感觉（feeling）消失后，你会变得更加平静（peaceful），也能更加清晰地（clearly）思考。如此一来，自我和解便能推动（drive）你前进。大量（plenty of）研究证实（confirm），这种心态十分有益（helpful）。然而，一些人不认同（disagree）这一观点。他们认为自我和解可能会让人变得不活跃。但布雷内斯与陈的研究（research）却呈现出了相反的（opposite）结果。他们给学生们安排了一场有难度的词汇（vocabulary）小测验（quiz），随后让他们为第二次测验进行复习。他们发现，那些能够直面（face）失败的学生会花费（spend）更多时间复习（revision）。专家（specialist）建议你给自己写一封信。在信中坦诚（honest）一些，表达自己的悲伤并接受（accept）你真实的情感。此外（in addition），做自己热爱的事是获得（attain）内心（inner）平静的实用（useful）方法。一位心理学家（psychologist）建议，用手轻轻触碰自己的胸膛（chest）。这个姿势（gesture）会让你感到安全（safe）与被爱。

sentences.cn: 随之便会产生压力。

sentences.en: You may get angry, feel disappointed and sink into sadness.
sentences.cn: 你可能会生气（angry）、感到沮丧（disappointed）并陷入（sink into）悲伤（sadness）。

sentences.en: Therefore, we ought to deal with stress properly.
sentences.cn: 因此（therefore），我们应该（ought）正确地（properly）应对压力。

sentences.en: Max is a 16-year-old boy who used to be very competitive and suffer from constant stress.
sentences.cn: 麦克斯是一名16岁的男孩，他过去一心求胜（competitive），并且承受着持续不断的（constant）压力。

sentences.en: Now he is learning to give himself patience and kindness.
sentences.cn: 如今他学着对自己多点耐心（patience）与宽容（kindness）。

sentences.en: When he doesn't win contests or get top marks, he whispers to himself, "It's OK not to be perfect."
sentences.cn: 当他没能赢得比赛（contest）或是取得高分时，他会对自己小声说（whisper）：“不完美（perfect）也没关系。”

sentences.en: He knows he always makes full efforts and that is enough.
sentences.cn: 他清楚自已总是全力以赴（make full efforts），这就足够（enough）了。

sentences.en: What Max does is called self-compassion.
sentences.cn: 麦克斯的这种做法被叫作（call）自我和解。

sentences.en: With self-compassion, you behave toward yourself gently as you do to a close friend.
sentences.cn: 拥有自我和解，你会像对待挚友一般对待自己，表现（behave）得温和友善。

sentences.en: It permits you to forgive yourself when you mess up or fail.
sentences.cn: 它允许（permit）你在搞砸（mess up）事情或失败（fail）时原谅（forgive）自已。

sentences.en: After feelings of guilt go away, you get more peaceful and you can think more clearly.
sentences.cn: 当内疫（guilt）的感觉（feeling）消失后，你会变得更加平静（peaceful），也能更加清晰地（clearly）思考。

sentences.en: This way self-compassion drives you to move forward.
sentences.cn: 如此一来，自我和解便能推动（drive）你前进。

sentences.en: Plenty of studies confirm that it is very helpful. However, some people disagree.
sentences.cn: 大量（plenty of）研究证实（confirm），这种心态十分有益（helpful）。

sentences.en: They think self-compassion may lead people to be less active.
sentences.cn: 然而，一些人不认同（disagree）这一观点。他们认为自我和解可能会让人变得不活跃。

sentences.en: But Brenes and Chen's research showed an opposite quiz result.
sentences.cn: 但布雷内斯与陈的研究（research）却呈现出了相反的（opposite）结果。

sentences.en: They gave students a difficult vocabulary and let them review for a second quiz.
sentences.cn: 他们给学生们安排了一场有难度的词汇（vocabulary）小测验（quiz），随后让他们为第二次测验进行复习。

sentences.en: They found those who were able to face their failure spent more time on revision.
sentences.cn: 他们发现，那些能够直面（face）失败的学生会花费（spend）更多时间复习（revision）。

sentences.en: Specialists advise you to write a letter to yourself.
sentences.cn: 专家（specialist）建议你给自己写一封信。

sentences.en: Be honest in the letter, express your sadness and accept your true feelings.
sentences.cn: 在信中坦诚（honest）一些，表达自己的悲伤并接受（accept）你真实的情感。

sentences.en: In addition, doing what you love is a useful way to attain inner peace.
sentences.cn: 此外（in addition），做自己热爱的事是获得（attain）内心（inner）平静的实用（useful）方法。

sentences.en: A psychologist suggests touching your chest gently with your hands.
sentences.cn: 一位心理学家（psychologist）建议，用手轻轻触碰自己的胸膛（chest）。

sentences.en: This gesture will make you feel safe and loved.
sentences.cn: 这个姿势（gesture）会让你感到安全（safe）与被爱。

readings.title: Keep Your Dream
readings.text: When Michael was in high school, his English teacher assigned the class a project to write a composition about their ambitions to state what career they wanted to take up when they became adults That night, Michael sat in his bedroom with great excitement. He wrote a 7-page passage about -owning a vast and magnificent his biggest ambition- horse ranch! He described every aspect carefully- the ranch would be 200 acres, and it was wide, with 50 lovely brown and white horses. He even drew a vivid picture to accompany the passage. The next morning, submitted it to his he held the paper tightly and teacher with a proud expression. Two days later, Michael got his paper back. The beat of his heart nearly stopped when he saw a large “F" on the first page. After class, he walked to the teacher's desk sadly and asked, “Excuse me, but could you tell me why I got an F?" The teacher shook her head and responded, “You lack adequate funds. Operating a ranch needs lots of money for land, horses, and food. It's almost impossible for you. If you write a new article, I'll adjust your grade." Michael thought about it throughout the entire night. The next day, he took the same paper to the teacher without making any changes. He said firmly, “I'm willing to accept the F but I'll never abandon my dream." Now, Michael's dream has come true through years of persistence. He owns a 200-acre ranch! The 50 horses run and play on the green grass freely every day. Last month, his former English teacher even came to visit him and expressed great pride in his achievements. ambition courage patience confidence Dream effort persistence determination self-discipline diligence proactivity
readings.translation: 迈克尔上高中（highschool）时，他的英语老师给全班布置（assign）了一项课题（project）一一写一篇作文（composition），谈谈自己的志向（ambition）一阐述自己成为成年人（adult）时想（want）从事什么职业（career）。那天夜晚（night），迈克尔满怀兴奋（excitement）地坐在卧室（bedroom）里。他写了一篇7页的文章（passage），阐述自己最大的志向一一拥有（own）一座广阔（vast）又壮丽的（magnificent）马（horse）场（ranch）！他仔细地（carefully）描述（describe）了每一个方面（aspect）一一这座牧场将（would）占地200英亩（acre），空间宽阔（wide），养着50匹棕白相间的可爱骏马。他甚至还画了一幅生动的（vivid）画来搭配（accompany）这篇文章。第二天早晨（next morning）他紧紧地（tightly）着文稿，带着自豪的表情（expression）把它上交（submit）给了老师。两天后，迈克尔拿回了自己的作文。看到首页上一个大大的（large）“F”时，他的心跳（beat）几乎（nearly）停止。下课后，他难过地（sadly）走到老师办公桌前问道：“打扰一下（excuse me），您能告诉我为什么我得了F吗？”老师摇了摇头回答（respond）说：“你缺少足够的（adequate）资金（funds）。经营（operate）一个牧场需要很多钱购置土地、马匹和饲料。这对你来说几乎是不可能的（impossible）。如果你重写一篇文章，我会调整（adjust）你的成绩。”迈克尔整整一夜（throughout the entire night）都在恩考这件事。第二天，他没有（without）做任何修改，拿着原稿去找了老师。他坚定地（firmly）说：“我愿意（willing）接受这个F，但我永远不会放弃（abandon）我的梦想。”经过多年的坚持（persistence），迈克尔如今实现了梦想。他拥有了一座200英亩的牧场！那50匹马每天在绿草地上自由地（freely）奔跑玩要（play）。上个月，他以前的（former）英语老师特意前去探望他，并为他取得的成就（achievement）感到无比骄傲（pride）。

readings.title: Reading is Carrying Water with a Basket
readings.text: On a rural farm, there lives a father and a son. The father has a strong interest in literature. He always gets up at dawn to read books outside their cottage. One sunny morning, the son walks slowly to his father and asks with a confused look, “Dad, I read storybooks at night, but I retain little of the stories the next morning. Is reading really beneficial to me?" The father does not give an immediate response to his son. He smiles and takes out a shabby basket that is used to carry coal. “Go to the river and get will explain the reason to you." The son feels very surprised, but he follows his father's instruction. Hehurries off to the river. He tries countless times to fill the basket with water, but every time the water swiftly leaks out. After an hour, he comes back with nothing but an empty basket. “I've tried many times, but I can never solve this problem,' he says in a low voice. The father laughs and says, “You're right. The basket can't carry water obviously. But look at it carefully isn't it different now?" The son glances at the basket and finds that the dirty basket has become clean! Then the father says, “Reading is just like carrying water with the basket. Although we may not memorize every paragraph or piece of the story, we are changed a lot by reading. It shows us the truth of the world and clarifies our direction in life. You become able to perceive the world with a clearer sight. This is the best solution to your doubt." The son nods and he understands that reading is not merely for memory, but for shaping one's humanity.
readings.translation: 在一个乡村的（rural）农场里，住着一对父（father）子。父亲对文学（literature）有着浓厚的兴趣（interest）。他总是在黎明（dawn）时分起床，到他们的小屋（cottage）外面（outside）读（read）书。一个晴朗的（sunny）早晨，儿子慢慢地（slowly）走到父亲跟前，一脸困惑的（confused）问（ask）道：“爸爸，我晚上读故事书（storybook），可是第二天早上只能记住（retain）很少的（little）内容。读书真的对我有用（beneficial）吗？”父亲没有立刻（immediate）给他的儿子回应（response）。他笑了笑，拿出一个破旧的（shabby）用来装煤的篮子（basket）。儿子感到非常惊诉（surprised），但他还是听从（follow）了他父亲的指示（instruction）。他勿勿赶往（hurry off to）河边。他试了无数（countless）次用篮子装水，但每次水都很快地（swiftly）漏（leak）了出来。一个小时后，他只（nothing but）带回来一个空（empty）篮子。“我试了很多次，但我永远解决（solve）不了这个问题。”他低声（voice）说。父亲笑（laugh）着说道：“你说得对。这篮子显然（obviously）是装不了水的。但你仔细看看，它现在是不是不一样了？”儿子警了一眼（glance）篮子，发现原本脏的（dirty）篮子已经变得干净（clean）了！接着父亲说道：“读书就像用篮子打水一样。虽然（although）我们可能记（memorize）不住故事里的每一个段落（paragraph）或片段（piece），但通过阅读，我们自身改变了很多。它向我们揭示了世界的真相（truth），并为我们理清（clarify）人生的方向（direction）。你能够（able）用更清晰的视野（sight）去感知（perceive）世界。这就是解开你的疑惑的最佳答案（solution）。儿子点了点头（nod），他明白了读书不仅仅（merely）是为了记住内容，更是为了塑造一个人的人性（humanity）。

sentences.en: On a rural farm, there lives a father and a son.

sentences.en: The father has a strong interest in literature.
sentences.cn: 父亲对文学（literature）有着浓厚的兴趣（interest）。

sentences.en: He always gets up at dawn to read books outside their cottage.
sentences.cn: 他总是在黎明（dawn）时分起床，到他们的小屋（cottage）外面（outside）读（read）书。

sentences.en: One sunny morning, the son walks slowly to his father and asks with a confused look, “Dad, I read storybooks at night, but I retain little of the stories the next morning. Is reading really beneficial to me?"
sentences.cn: 一个晴朗的（sunny）早晨，儿子慢慢地（slowly）走到父亲跟前，一脸困惑的（confused）问（ask）道：“爸爸，我晚上读故事书（storybook），可是第二天早上只能记住（retain）很少的（little）内容。读书真的对我有用（beneficial）吗？”

sentences.en: The father does not give an immediate response to his son.
sentences.cn: 父亲没有立刻（immediate）给他的儿子回应（response）。

sentences.en: He smiles and takes out a shabby basket that is used to carry coal.
sentences.cn: 他笑了笑，拿出一个破旧的（shabby）用来装煤的篮子（basket）。

sentences.en: “Go to the river and get will explain the reason to you." The son feels very surprised, but he follows his father's instruction.
sentences.cn: 儿子感到非常惊诉（surprised），但他还是听从（follow）了他父亲的指示（instruction）。

sentences.en: Hehurries off to the river.
sentences.cn: 他勿勿赶往（hurry off to）河边。

sentences.en: He tries countless times to fill the basket with water, but every time the water swiftly leaks out.
sentences.cn: 他试了无数（countless）次用篮子装水，但每次水都很快地（swiftly）漏（leak）了出来。

sentences.en: After an hour, he comes back with nothing but an empty basket.
sentences.cn: 一个小时后，他只（nothing but）带回来一个空（empty）篮子。“我试了很多次，但我永远解决（solve）不了这个问题。”

sentences.en: “I've tried many times, but I can never solve this problem,' he says in a low voice. The father laughs and says, “You're right. The basket can't carry water obviously. But look at it carefully isn't it different now?"
sentences.cn: 他低声（voice）说。父亲笑（laugh）着说道：“你说得对。这篮子显然（obviously）是装不了水的。但你仔细看看，它现在是不是不一样了？”

sentences.en: The son glances at the basket and finds that the dirty basket has become clean! Then the father says, “Reading is just like carrying water with the basket. Although we may not memorize every paragraph or piece of the story, we are changed a lot by reading. It shows us the truth of the world and clarifies our direction in life. You become able to perceive the world with a clearer sight. This is the best solution to your doubt."
sentences.cn: 儿子警了一眼（glance）篮子，发现原本脏的（dirty）篮子已经变得干净（clean）了！接着父亲说道：“读书就像用篮子打水一样。虽然（although）我们可能记（memorize）不住故事里的每一个段落（paragraph）或片段（piece），但通过阅读，我们自身改变了很多。它向我们揭示了世界的真相（truth），并为我们理清（clarify）人生的方向（direction）。

sentences.en: The son nods and he understands that reading is not merely for memory, but for shaping one's humanity.
sentences.cn: 你能够（able）用更清晰的视野（sight）去感知（perceive）世界。这就是解开你的疑惑的最佳答案（solution）。儿子点了点头（nod），他明白了读书不仅仅（merely）是为了记住内容，更是为了塑造一个人的人性（humanity）。

readings.title: A Brave Young
readings.text: Li Jiating is a 13-year-old girl. She has won online praise for her courageous act risking her life to save a child who fell into anicy lake. The accident occurred on a Saturday afternoon. Li Jiating was riding her bike past a lake. A 4-year-old boy accidentally fell into the freezing water while playing on thin ice. Several people at the scene called the police right away, but they hesitated to rescue the boy by themselves. They were worried that the ice would collapse if they stepped onto the icy lake. At this critical moment, Li Jiating bravely stepped forward without hesitation. She said, "I'm light. Let me save him!" Carrying a plastic pipe, she carefully moved towards the hole in the ice. She extended one end of the pipe to the toddler and urged him to cling to it tightly. Then she tried to pull him to safety. Suddenly, the ice broke, and Li Jiating fell into the icy water! Despite the intense cold, she still held the pipe firmly. Luckily, the firefighters arrived in time and rescued the boy successfully. After confirming that the boy was safe, Li Jiating left the scene and rode home quickly. Her family = safety didn't know what had happened until that night. Later, the family of the rescued boy visited Li's home to express their gratitude for her heroic actions. On Monday, local officials came to Li Jiating's home to praise her courage. Her school also honoured her as an “Outstanding Student" for her brave deeds. Even though she received a lot of praise, Li remained modest. "I didn't think too much and simply wanted to save him from danger as fast as possible," she said. In life, we can help people in need as much as we can, but we should also do what we can do, and we can ask adults for help.
readings.translation: 李佳婷是一名13岁的女孩（girl）。她冒着生命危险救（save）了一名掉入（fall into）冰湖（icy lake）的孩子，这一勇敢的（courageous）行为收获了网友的称赞。事故（accident）发生（occur）在一个星期六（Saturday）下午（afternoon）。当时李佳婷正骑（ride）自行车（bike）经过一片湖。一名四岁男孩在薄（thin）冰上玩耍时意外（accidentally）跌入了冰冷的（freezing）湖水（water）中。在现场的几个人（people）立刻报了警（police），但他们犹豫（hesitate）着不敢亲自去救（rescue）这个男孩，他们担心（worried）踏（step）上冰面后冰层会破裂（collapse）。危急（critical）时刻，李佳婷毫不犹豫（hesitation）地站出来（step forward）。她说道：“我体重轻，我来救他！”她拿着一根塑料管子（pipe），小心翼翼地（carefully）走向（towards）冰面的破洞（hole），将管子一端（end）伸向（extend）幼童（toddler），催促（urge）他紧紧（tightly）抓住（cling to）它。随后她春力把孩子往安全的地方（safety）拉（pull）。突然冰层开裂，李佳婷也掉入冰冷的湖水中。即便寒气刺骨（intense cold），她依旧紧紧擦着管子。幸运的是（luckily），消防员（firefighter）及时赶到，成功救出了男孩。确认男孩平安后，李佳婷便离开了（leave）现场，骑车勿匆回了家。直到当晚，她的家人才知晓发生了什么。后来（later），被救男孩的家人专程登门，向她的英勇（heroic）之举表示感谢（gratitude）。周一，当地工作人员来到李佳婷家中，赞扬她的勇敢。她所在的学校也因其勇敢的行为（deed）授予她“优秀学生”称号。即便收到了诸多赞誉，李佳婷仍保持着谦逊（modest）。她说：“我当时没想太多，只想着尽可能快地（asfast as possible）把他从危险（danger）中救出来。”生活中，我们可以尽可能去帮助需要帮助的人，但是我们要量力而行，同时可以向成年人寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Li Jiating is a 13-year-old girl.
sentences.cn: 李佳婷是一名13岁的女孩（girl）。

sentences.en: She has won online praise for her courageous act risking her life to save a child who fell into anicy lake.
sentences.cn: 她冒着生命危险救（save）了一名掉入（fall into）冰湖（icy lake）的孩子，这一勇敢的（courageous）行为收获了网友的称赞。

sentences.en: The accident occurred on a Saturday afternoon.
sentences.cn: 事故（accident）发生（occur）在一个星期六（Saturday）下午（afternoon）。

sentences.en: Li Jiating was riding her bike past a lake.
sentences.cn: 当时李佳婷正骑（ride）自行车（bike）经过一片湖。

sentences.en: A 4-year-old boy accidentally fell into the freezing water while playing on thin ice.
sentences.cn: 一名四岁男孩在薄（thin）冰上玩耍时意外（accidentally）跌入了冰冷的（freezing）湖水（water）中。

sentences.en: Several people at the scene called the police right away, but they hesitated to rescue the boy by themselves. They were worried that the ice would collapse if they stepped onto the icy lake.
sentences.cn: 在现场的几个人（people）立刻报了警（police），但他们犹豫（hesitate）着不敢亲自去救（rescue）这个男孩，他们担心（worried）踏（step）上冰面后冰层会破裂（collapse）。

sentences.en: At this critical moment, Li Jiating bravely stepped forward without hesitation.
sentences.cn: 危急（critical）时刻，李佳婷毫不犹豫（hesitation）地站出来（step forward）。

sentences.en: She said, "I'm light. Let me save him!"
sentences.cn: 她说道：“我体重轻，我来救他！”

sentences.en: Carrying a plastic pipe, she carefully moved towards the hole in the ice. She extended one end of the pipe to the toddler and urged him to cling to it tightly.
sentences.cn: 她拿着一根塑料管子（pipe），小心翼翼地（carefully）走向（towards）冰面的破洞（hole），将管子一端（end）伸向（extend）幼童（toddler），催促（urge）他紧紧（tightly）抓住（cling to）它。

sentences.en: Then she tried to pull him to safety.
sentences.cn: 随后她春力把孩子往安全的地方（safety）拉（pull）。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the ice broke, and Li Jiating fell into the icy water!
sentences.cn: 突然冰层开裂，李佳婷也掉入冰冷的湖水中。

sentences.en: Despite the intense cold, she still held the pipe firmly.
sentences.cn: 即便寒气刺骨（intense cold），她依旧紧紧擦着管子。

sentences.en: Luckily, the firefighters arrived in time and rescued the boy successfully.
sentences.cn: 幸运的是（luckily），消防员（firefighter）及时赶到，成功救出了男孩。

sentences.en: After confirming that the boy was safe, Li Jiating left the scene and rode home quickly.
sentences.cn: 确认男孩平安后，李佳婷便离开了（leave）现场，骑车勿匆回了家。

sentences.en: Her family = safety didn't know what had happened until that night.
sentences.cn: 直到当晚，她的家人才知晓发生了什么。

sentences.en: Later, the family of the rescued boy visited Li's home to express their gratitude for her heroic actions.
sentences.cn: 后来（later），被救男孩的家人专程登门，向她的英勇（heroic）之举表示感谢（gratitude）。

sentences.en: On Monday, local officials came to Li Jiating's home to praise her courage.
sentences.cn: 周一，当地工作人员来到李佳婷家中，赞扬她的勇敢。

sentences.en: Her school also honoured her as an “Outstanding Student" for her brave deeds.
sentences.cn: 她所在的学校也因其勇敢的行为（deed）授予她“优秀学生”称号。

sentences.en: Even though she received a lot of praise, Li remained modest.
sentences.cn: 即便收到了诸多赞誉，李佳婷仍保持着谦逊（modest）。

sentences.en: "I didn't think too much and simply wanted to save him from danger as fast as possible," she said.
sentences.cn: 她说：“我当时没想太多，只想着尽可能快地（asfast as possible）把他从危险（danger）中救出来。”

sentences.en: In life, we can help people in need as much as we can, but we should also do what we can do, and we can ask adults for help.
sentences.cn: 生活中，我们可以尽可能去帮助需要帮助的人，但是我们要量力而行，同时可以向成年人寻求帮助。

readings.title: An Unsung Hero of the College Cafe
readings.titleCn: 大学咖啡馆的无名英雄
readings.text: Need a break between classes or just a quick energy boost to start the morning? The College Cafe has just that and more. Not only does this cafe serve up drinks, it also delivers smiles. Emma Thompson, a cafe worker in a blue shirt and black cap, makes sure that each customer gets precisely what they purchase. She goes back and forth efficiently between coffee machines to make the drinks. After finishing an order, she calls out the name on the cup. As the customer grabs the drink from her hand, she smiles and says, “Hello, how is your day?" Even when she is busy, she doesn't let it get in the way of her genuine conversations. Emma gets up at a quarter past five and drives for 25 minutes every day to get to work on time. Sometimes she arrives early to serve the students. “I do so because I like to make coffee for the students. I know they need it in the morning," Emma says. Her experience as a mother and wife has shaped who she is today. She believes she is here to serve. One thing Emma may not know is that her contagious smile can positively impact students, helping them have a much better day than before seeing her. Sarah Johnson, a senior psychology major, loves coffee and goes to the cafe at least six days a week. Going to the cafe starts her day off well and gets her ready for class. “Emma always has a huge smile on her face, which always puts me in a cheerful mood," Johnson says. “I enjoy working in the cafe," Emma says. She has served here for 15 years and can't imagine working anywhere else. She has every intention of staying and continuing doing what she loves. coffee machine
readings.translation: 课间（between）需要休息（break）片刻，或是清晨需要快速（quick）提神（energy boost）？学院（college）咖啡馆恰好能提供这些，还不止于此。这家咖啡馆不仅提供各式饮料（drink），也传递（deliver）微笑。艾玛·汤普森身穿蓝色（blue）衬衫（shirt）、头戴黑色帽子（cap），是咖啡馆的一名员工，她确保（make sure）每个（each）顾客（customer）都能准确地（precisely）拿到自己所购买（purchase）的饮品。她在各类咖啡（coffee）机间来回（back and forth）穿梭，高效地（efficiently）制作饮料。每完成（finish）一单之后（after），她就会大声念出杯身上的名字（name）。顾客（customer）从她手中取（grab）饮料时，她总会笑着说（say）：“你好，今天过得怎么样？”即便是工作很繁忙（busy）的时候，她也不会让忙碌妨碍自己（get int he way）（和顾客）真诚的（genuine）交流。艾玛每（every）天五点一刻（quarter）起床，驾车25分钟（minute），准时上班。有时（sometimes）她会提前到达（arrive），早早地为学生们提供服务。“我这么做是因为（because）我喜欢为学生们制作咖啡。我知道他们清晨需要来一杯。”艾玛说道。她作为一名母亲以及妻子（wife）的经历造就了如今的她。她认为自已来到这里就是为了服务。有一件事情（thing）艾玛也许（may）并不知晓：她那富有感染力的（contagious）笑容能积极地（positively）影响（impact）学生们，让大家在见到（see）她之后，一整天都比之前（before）更加舒心。萨拉·约翰逊是心理学（psychology）专业（major）的毕业班学生（senior），她喜爱咖啡，每周至少有六天都会来这家咖啡馆。来这里开启（start）新的一天，为上课做好准备（ready）。“艾玛脸上总（always）挂着灿烂的笑容（huge smile），总能让我心情（mood）愉悦（cheerful）。”约翰逊说。“我很喜欢在这家咖啡馆工作。”艾玛说。她已经在这里工作了15年，无法想象去其他的任何地方（anywhere else）工作。她打算（have every intention of）一直留（stay）在这里，继续做自己热爱的事。

readings.title: What Is a Friend?
readings.text: The meaning of“friend”varies from person to person. For my younger sister Lily, a friend is regarded as adventure partner, with whom she shares a common passion for running and cycling. Last weekend, while chasing colourful butterflies in the park, the two girls dashed into a flower bed and discovered numerous tiny pebbles. Whenever Lily tripped over something and burst into tears, her friend would assist her in standing up and brush the dust off her clothes gently. As for my mother, a true friend refers to a close companion like Mrs Green, with whom she maintains a routine of slow morning walks outdoors every day, wearing warm and sweet smiles. The two ladies often chat about delicious baked desserts and lovely little cats, and they occasionally exchange home-made cookies to enrich their daily life. In my father's eyes, his friends are those kind uncles in our neighbourhood, who cooperate to build tool shelves and repair worn-out bicycles in our backyard. During the picnic held last week, they worked together to put up a tent, inside which we enjoyed tasty hamburgers and spent an unforgettable and joyful time. When it comes to me, my most trustworthy friend is Tom, who is my deskmate as well as our class monitor. We often play basketball or enjoy reading in our spare time after school. The moment I hurt my leg and was confined to bed last month, he came to see me every day, taking neat notes for me and sharing funny jokes to lift my spirits. After I returned to campus, he volunteered to carry my schoolbag and fetch me hot milk on a daily basis. We always support each other through difficulties, and I truly cherish our friendship. Friends are stars that brighten my life. They are so vital that I can hardly imagine my life without them. -mate
readings.translation: “朋友”（friend）的含义（meaning）因人（person）而异（vary）。对我的妹妹（sister）莉莉而言，朋友被看作是冒险（adventure）伙伴，她和好友都酷爱（passion）跑步（running）与骑行（cycling）。上周末（weekend），这两个女孩在公园里追逐五彩缤纷的（colourful）蝴蝶（butterfly）时，冲（dash）进了一片花（flower）坛，发现了许许多多极小的（tiny）鹅卵石。每当（whenever）莉莉被东西纤倒、突然大哭（burst into tears）时，她的朋友都会帮助（assist）她站起来，轻轻拍掉她衣服上的尘土（dust）。对我母亲来说，朋友就是格林太太这样亲密的伙伴。她们每天清晨都会外出慢走散步，脸上洋溢着温暖（warm）甜美的（sweet）笑容（smile）。两位女士（lady）常常聊（chat）起美味的烘焙甜点（dessert）与可爱的小猫，她们偶尔（occasionally）还会交换（exchange）自制的饼干来丰富（enrich）彼此的日常生活。在我父亲眼中，他的朋友就是小区里那些善良的叔叔们。他们会合作（cooperate）在我们的后院搭建工具架（shelf）、修理（repair）破旧的自行车（bicycle）。上周野餐（picnic）时，他们合力搭起帐篷（tent），我们在帐篷里享受（enjoy）美味的（tasty）汉堡（hamburger），度过了一段难忘（unforgettable）又欢乐的时光。而对我来说，我最值得信赖的朋友是汤姆，他既是我的同桌（deskmate）也是我们班的班长（monitor）。放学后，我们常一起打篮球或享受阅读（reading）。上个月，我腿部受伤、被限制（confine）卧床时，他每天都来看望我，给我带来工整的（neat）笔记（note），并且分享有趣的（funny）笑话（joke）振奋我的精神（spirit）。在我返校（campus）之后，他还主动每天帮我背书包、给我拿来（fetch）热牛奶。我们总在困境中互相扶持，我格外珍惜（cherish）我们的友谊（fiendship）。朋友如同点亮我生活的星辰。他们无比重要，以至于我难以想象（imagine）没有他们的生活。

sentences.en: In my father's eyes, his friends are those kind uncles in our neighbourhood, who cooperate to build tool shelves and repair worn-out bicycles in our backyard.

sentences.en: We often play basketball or enjoy reading in our spare time after school.

sentences.en: The moment I hurt my leg and was confined to bed last month, he came to see me every day, taking neat notes for me and sharing funny jokes to lift my spirits.

readings.title: Is Comparison the Thief of Joy?
readings.text: Not long ago, on a cold winter night, a teenager wanted more screen time, but her parent said no. The girl argued that she should be allowed to scroll for an extra 30 minutes. The parent replied,“None of your friends' parents allow them to use electronic devices after 9 o'clock." The girl answered back, "I thought in this household, we shouldn't compare ourselves with other people, Dad." The parent that was me, by the way-was speechless. Since my kids were young, I had always told them not to compare themselves with others. I had said countless t times that comparisons are the “thief of joy" That night, my daughter didn't win the debate. But she made me realize that one piece of advice I had given might not be entirely correct. To be fair, I had done what many of us do- I repeated something I heard without thinking more deeply about it. Now, it's time to get it right-starting with the question- Are all social comparisons really bad? Of course, comparing ourselves with others often gets us into emotional trouble. For example, if your classmate gets a higher mark on a maths test, you might feel sad or jealous. But if we are aware of how it works, we can use it to improve ourselves. The comparisons we make whether they make us feel good or bad-are actually important for our growth. Science shows us how to compare in a smarter way to reduce the negative feelings. Let's see how. If you compare yourself with someone who does better than you, this comparison may lead to feelings of envy if you only focus on what they have and you don't. But you can also feel energized and inspired if you use these comparisons as a source of motivation. For example, you can think, "If they can achieve it, so can I. " If you compare yourself with someone who does worse than you, you might feel fear or worry. But you can also feel grateful. This kind of comparison helps you appreciate what you have instead of always wanting more. What I wish I had taught my daughter earlier is this difference. How we feel about ourselves depends not only on who we compare ourselves with, but also on how we think about that comparison.
readings.translation: 不久前，在一个寒冷的冬夜，一名青少年（teenager）想要更多的时间（time）看（电子）屏幕（screen），但她的父亲（母亲）（parent）没有同意。女孩争辩（argue）说她应该被允许（allow）额外（extra）刷手机（scroll）30分钟。父亲（母亲）回答（reply）说：“你朋友的父母没有一个（noneof）允许他们（them）在9点之后使用电子设备。”女孩反驳道（answer back）：“我认为（think），在这个家里（household），我们不应该把我们自己和别的（other）人比较（compare），爸爸。”那位父亲就是我，顺便说一下一一哑口无言（speechless）。从（since）我的孩子（kid）们年幼时（young）起，我就一直告诉他们不要把他们自己和其他人（others）比较。我说过无数（countless）次，比较（comparison）是“快乐（joy）的窃贼（thief）”那天晚上，我女儿（daughter）没有赢得（win）那场争论（debate）。但她让我认识到（realize），我给出的一条建议（advice）可能并非完全（entirely）正确（correct）。平心而论（tobe fair），我做了我们很多人都会做的事一一我没有（without）更加深入地思考便重复（repeat）了自己听到的话。现在，是时候把这件事弄明白了一一从这个问题（question）开始一一所有的社会（social）比较真的都不好吗？当然，拿自己和别人比较常常会使我们陷入情绪的（emotional）苦恼（trouble）。比如，如果你的同班同学（classmate）在一场数学（maths）测试（test）中得了更高的分数（mark），你可能会感到伤心（sad）或妒忌（jealous）。但（but）如果我们意识到（bea ware of）其运作方式，就可以利用它来提升（improve）自己。我们所做的比较一一无论它们让我们感觉是好是坏一一实际上（actually）对我们的成长（growth）都是重要的（important）。科学（science）向我们展示了如何用更明智的方式进行比较，以减少（reduce）负面的（negative）情绪。让我们来看看怎么做。如果你拿自己和比你更优秀的人比较，并且只关注他们拥有而你没有的东西，那么这种比较可能会引发忌妒（envy）的情绪。但如果你把这些比较当作动力（motivation）来源（source），你也会感到振奋（energized）并受到启发（inspired）。比如，你可以这样想：“如果他们能完成（achieve），我也可以。”如果你拿自己和不如你的某个人（someone）比较，你可能会感到恐惧（fear）或担忧（worry）。但你也可能会心怀感激（grate fi ul）。这种比较能帮你感激（appreciate）自已己所拥有的，而不是（instead of）一味索取更多。我真希望当初能更早地（early）教会（teach）我女儿这种差异（difference）。我们对自身的感受不仅取决于我们与谁比较，还取决于我们如何看待这种比较。

sentences.en: Not long ago, on a cold winter night, a teenager wanted more screen time, but her parent said no.
sentences.cn: 不久前，在一个寒冷的冬夜，一名青少年（teenager）想要更多的时间（time）看（电子）屏幕（screen），但她的父亲（母亲）（parent）没有同意。

sentences.en: The girl argued that she should be allowed to scroll for an extra 30 minutes.
sentences.cn: 女孩争辩（argue）说她应该被允许（allow）额外（extra）刷手机（scroll）30分钟。

sentences.en: The parent replied,“None of your friends' parents allow them to use electronic devices after 9 o'clock."
sentences.cn: 父亲（母亲）回答（reply）说：“你朋友的父母没有一个（noneof）允许他们（them）在9点之后使用电子设备。”

sentences.en: The girl answered back, "I thought in this household, we shouldn't compare ourselves with other people, Dad."
sentences.cn: 女孩反驳道（answer back）：“我认为（think），在这个家里（household），我们不应该把我们自己和别的（other）人比较（compare），爸爸。”

sentences.en: The parent that was me, by the way-was speechless.
sentences.cn: 那位父亲就是我，顺便说一下一一哑口无言（speechless）。

sentences.en: Since my kids were young, I had always told them not to compare themselves with others.
sentences.cn: 从（since）我的孩子（kid）们年幼时（young）起，我就一直告诉他们不要把他们自己和其他人（others）比较。

sentences.en: I had said countless t times that comparisons are the “thief of joy" That night, my daughter didn't win the debate.
sentences.cn: 我说过无数（countless）次，比较（comparison）是“快乐（joy）的窃贼（thief）”那天晚上，我女儿（daughter）没有赢得（win）那场争论（debate）。

sentences.en: But she made me realize that one piece of advice I had given might not be entirely correct.
sentences.cn: 但她让我认识到（realize），我给出的一条建议（advice）可能并非完全（entirely）正确（correct）。

sentences.en: To be fair, I had done what many of us do- I repeated something I heard without thinking more deeply about it.
sentences.cn: 平心而论（tobe fair），我做了我们很多人都会做的事一一我没有（without）更加深入地思考便重复（repeat）了自己听到的话。

sentences.en: Now, it's time to get it right-starting with the question- Are all social comparisons really bad?
sentences.cn: 现在，是时候把这件事弄明白了一一从这个问题（question）开始一一所有的社会（social）比较真的都不好吗？

sentences.en: Of course, comparing ourselves with others often gets us into emotional trouble.
sentences.cn: 当然，拿自己和别人比较常常会使我们陷入情绪的（emotional）苦恼（trouble）。

sentences.en: For example, if your classmate gets a higher mark on a maths test, you might feel sad or jealous.
sentences.cn: 比如，如果你的同班同学（classmate）在一场数学（maths）测试（test）中得了更高的分数（mark），你可能会感到伤心（sad）或妒忌（jealous）。

sentences.en: But if we are aware of how it works, we can use it to improve ourselves.
sentences.cn: 但（but）如果我们意识到（bea ware of）其运作方式，就可以利用它来提升（improve）自己。

sentences.en: The comparisons we make whether they make us feel good or bad-are actually important for our growth.
sentences.cn: 我们所做的比较一一无论它们让我们感觉是好是坏一一实际上（actually）对我们的成长（growth）都是重要的（important）。

sentences.en: Science shows us how to compare in a smarter way to reduce the negative feelings.
sentences.cn: 科学（science）向我们展示了如何用更明智的方式进行比较，以减少（reduce）负面的（negative）情绪。

sentences.en: Let's see how.
sentences.cn: 让我们来看看怎么做。

sentences.en: If you compare yourself with someone who does better than you, this comparison may lead to feelings of envy if you only focus on what they have and you don't.
sentences.cn: 如果你拿自己和比你更优秀的人比较，并且只关注他们拥有而你没有的东西，那么这种比较可能会引发忌妒（envy）的情绪。

sentences.en: But you can also feel energized and inspired if you use these comparisons as a source of motivation.
sentences.cn: 但如果你把这些比较当作动力（motivation）来源（source），你也会感到振奋（energized）并受到启发（inspired）。

sentences.en: For example, you can think, "If they can achieve it, so can I. " If you compare yourself with someone who does worse than you, you might feel fear or worry.
sentences.cn: 比如，你可以这样想：“如果他们能完成（achieve），我也可以。”如果你拿自己和不如你的某个人（someone）比较，你可能会感到恐惧（fear）或担忧（worry）。

sentences.en: But you can also feel grateful.
sentences.cn: 但你也可能会心怀感激（grate fi ul）。

sentences.en: This kind of comparison helps you appreciate what you have instead of always wanting more.
sentences.cn: 这种比较能帮你感激（appreciate）自已己所拥有的，而不是（instead of）一味索取更多。

sentences.en: What I wish I had taught my daughter earlier is this difference.
sentences.cn: 我真希望当初能更早地（early）教会（teach）我女儿这种差异（difference）。

sentences.en: How we feel about ourselves depends not only on who we compare ourselves with, but also on how we think about that comparison.
sentences.cn: 我们对自身的感受不仅取决于我们与谁比较，还取决于我们如何看待这种比较。

readings.title: Millennium Iron Flowers Bear Hope
readings.text: Bright sparks light up the night sky, resembling a rain of pretty flowers. This amazing show is called "striking iron flowers". It's an ancient folk art in China and it has a history of over 1, o00 years! It is deeply rooted in traditional Chinese culture. Striking iron flowers is often performed during main festivals， such as the Spring Festival and the Lantern t—kids Festival. When the first sparks fly, cheers break out- clap their hands loudly, and elders smile, saying the sparks can “dispel bad luck". The crowd is filled with excitement. The sparks glow brightly, standing for happiness and good wishes. Do you know how this craft is performed? It's not easy! First, performers put old iron into a large furnace. They put wood or coal inside to burn, and the temperature gets so high that the air around it feels like a warm wind. Then, they heat the iron to a very high temperature until it melts into liquid. In the final stage, they use professional tools to splash the liquid iron into the air. When the liquid iron comes into contact with the cold air, it turns into lovely sparks. To do this, a performer needs powerful arms, great skills and lots of courage. It shows how wise Chinese craftsmen are. Currently, more and more young people are showing great enthusiasm for this folk art, hoping to carry it forward to keep traditional Chinese culture alive. Thus, we should protect and pass down this precious heritage by learning the related skills. What How
readings.translation: 明亮的火花（spark）点亮夜空，看起来像（resemble）一场美丽的花雨（rain）。这场令人惊叹的（amazing）表演名为“打（strike）铁（iron）花”。它是一项古老的中国民间艺术，距今已有一千多年的历史！它深深地（deeply）植根于中国传统的（traditional）文化。打铁花通常在主要的节日（festival）期间上演，例如（such as）春节（the Spring Festival）和元宵节（the Lan term Festival）。当第一（first）簇火花飞起（fly）时，欢呼声（cheer）瞬间爆发一一孩子（kid）们大声地（loudly）鼓掌（clap），长辈（elder）们满脸笑容，说这火花能“驱散（dispel）厄运（bad luck）”。人群（crowd）充满了兴奋（excitement）。火花明亮地（brightly）闪耀（glow）着，象征着幸福（happiness）与美好祝愿。你知道这项手艺（craft）是怎么表演的吗？这可不容易（easy）！首先，表演者（performer）会将废旧的铁放进一座大熔炉（fiurnace）里。他们把木头（wood）或煤（coal）放在里面（inside）燃烧，温度变得十分高以至于周围的空气（air）都热得像一阵暖（warm）风。随后，他们把铁加热（heat）到极高的温度，直到它熔化成液体（liquid）。在最后阶段，他们使用（use）专业的（professional）工具将铁水泼洒（splash）向空中。当铁水接触（contact）到冷空气时，它就会变成美丽的（lovely）火花。完成这样的表演，表演者需要有强有力的手臂（arm）、精湛的技艺和十足的勇气。这门技艺展现了中国工匠（craftsman）是多么充满智慧（wise）。目前（currently），越来越多的年轻人对这项民间艺术表现出了极大的热情（enthusiasm），希望（hope）将其传承下去，让中国传统文化永葆活力（alive）。因此（thus），我们应当通过学习相关的（related）技艺保护并传承这一珍贵的（precious）遗产（heritage）。
