sentences.en: Beijing hosted the first World Humanoid Robot Games in August 2025.
sentences.cn: 2025年8月，北京主办（host）了首届世界人形机器人（humanoid robot）运动会。

sentences.en: It marked the world's first event that integrated sports, arts and applied scenarios.
sentences.cn: 这是全球首次将体育、艺术和应用（applied）场景相结合（integrate）的赛事。

sentences.en: It highlighted advancements in robotics technology.
sentences.cn: 该赛事突出（highlight）了机器人科学（robotics）技术（technology）的进展。

sentences.en: A professor said that the Games helped to “give the public a realistic impression of what things really are." The Games showed the latest achievements of China's humanoid robots.
sentences.cn: 一位教授（professor）表示，此次比赛有助于“让公众（public）对实际（realistic）情况有一个真实的印象（impression）”这个比赛展示（show）了中国人形机器人（领域）的最新（latest）科研成果。

sentences.en: It also successfully filled the gap in international competitions in this field.
sentences.cn: 同时，这场运动会也成功填补（fil）了该领域（field）在国际（international）赛事中的空白。

sentences.en: A total of 280 teams from 16 countries brought hundreds of robots to compete.
sentences.cn: 来自16个国家的共计280支队伍带来了数百台机器人参与竞赛（compete）。

sentences.en: ceremony，the robots showed At the opening great skills.
sentences.cn: 在开幕式（opening ceremony）上，这些机器人展示了出色的技能。

sentences.en: They jumped, danced, performed kung fu, and even took part in a fashion show with human models.
sentences.cn: 它们跳跃（jump）、跳舞（dance）、表演（perform）功夫（kung fu），甚至还与真人模特同台参加时装表演（fashion show）。

sentences.en: During the competition, some robots could successfully navigate rough terrain.
sentences.cn: 在比赛中，一些机器人能够成功地穿过高低不平的（rough）地形。

sentences.en: However, things were not always smooth.
sentences.cn: 然而，事情并非总是顺利的（smooth）。

sentences.en: Many robots fell down, crashed into each other or experienced technical faults.
sentences.cn: 许多机器人摔倒、相互碰撞（crash into）或者出现技术故障（fault）。

sentences.en: They needed humans to repair them; otherwise, they could not continue competing.
sentences.cn: 它们需要人类来修理（repair）；否则（otherwise），它们就无法继续竞赛了。

sentences.en: There were also a couple of falls during a soccer match.
sentences.cn: 在一场足球（soccer）比赛（match）中也有几次（a couple of）摔倒的情况发生。

sentences.en: But one robot managed to solve the problem by itself in the end.
sentences.cn: 但有一台机器人最后自己（itself）解决了问题。

sentences.en: In spite of this, just like real athletes, people cheered loudly after a robot scored a nice goal with a quick shot, or won the game at the last minute.
sentences.cn: 尽管如此，就像真正的运动员（athlete）一样，当机器人凭借一次快速的射门（shot）踢进一个漂亮的球（scored anice goal）之后或在最后一刻赢得比赛时，人们都会大声欢呼。

sentences.en: Some people even stood up and waved colorful signs.
sentences.cn: 有些人甚至站起来挥动（wave）着五颜六色的标牌（sign）。

sentences.en: It was such a lively scene.
sentences.cn: 这一场面（scene）十分热闹。

sentences.en: But the Games also raised questions about how far robots could go on their own.
sentences.cn: 但这些比赛也引起（raise）了关于机器人能在多大程度上自主运作的思考。

sentences.en: They did some great things, but still needed humans to help.
sentences.cn: 它们虽然能做一些厉害的事情，但仍需要人类的协助。

sentences.en: Batteries needed replacing and broken parts needed fixing, so the robots often stayed close to their human operators.
sentences.cn: 电池（battery）需要替换（replace），损坏的部件需要修理，因此这些机器人通常会紧贴着人类操作员行动。

sentences.en: China is trying its best to do more research with the aim of inventing more efficient humanoid robots and is promoting rapid progress in robot technology through government investment.
sentences.cn: 中国正全力以赴做更多研究，旨在发明（invent）出更高效的（efficient）人形机器人，并通过政府投资（investment）推动（promote）机器人技术的迅速（rapid）发展。

sentences.en: These smart robots will be used in all walks of life.
sentences.cn: 这些智能机器人不久将被应用于各行各业。

readings.title: AI Finds NestsTech Saves Birds
readings.text: The plain wanderer is a small and rare bird living on the grassland. Different from most birds, female plain wanderers are bigger and stronger. Females responsible for defending nests and chicks from are animals like foxes, while males hatch the eggs and keep them warm. Their feathers make them look like part of the land. Sadly, their numbers are dropping humans occupy their grassland habitats for farms and cities. To save them, scientists are using AI. The key is the birds' calls. Female birds make soft sounds to communicate with their chicks and warn of danger. These calls are faint and easy to miss, but AI can detect them clearly. Scientists put microphones in the grassland to record sounds day and night. Then they put these recordings into a computer program. AI learns to distinguish the plain wanderer's calls from other noises like the sound of wind or insects. This helps scientists find female birds and count their numbers. “AI helps us monitor these birds without disturbing them," says Dr Li, the project leader. "We can identify the most important areas for them and work to protect those places." Once, AI helped scientists find a hidden nest with three baby birds. Without AI, they might never have found it. AI is really a powerful tool to save wildlife. As human activities continue to spread across natural landscapes, countless rare species are facing the threat of extinction. Traditional wildlife survey methods often require plenty of manpower, time andon-site observations, which may also disturb the birds' normal living habits. The combination of AI technology and ecological protection sets a good example for wildlife conservation worldwide. It not only improves the accuracy and efficiency of species monitoring, but also allows researchers to collect reliable data quietly. If we can balance economic development with ecological preservation, more endangered creatures will surely survive and live in peace with humans on Earth. intelligence automation facial recognition voice assistant chatbot self-driving car big data smart home
readings.translation: 领鹑（plain Wanderer）是一种生活在草原（grassland）上的小型的稀有的（rare）鸟类。与大多数鸟类不同的是，雌性的（female）领鹑体型更大、更强壮。雌鸟负责（responsible）保卫巢穴（nest）和雏鸟（chick），抵御（defend）狐狸（fox）等动物（animal）的侵袭，而雄鸟（male）则负责孵（hatch）鸟蛋并为其保暖。它们的羽毛（feather）使它们看起来就像是这片土地的一部分。不幸的是（sadly），由于人类侵占（occupy）它们的草原栖息地（habitat）用于建农场和城市，它们的数量正在不断减少（drop）。为了保护它们，科学家们正在利用人工智能。关键（key）在于这些鸟的叫声。雌鸟会发出轻柔的（soft）声音（sound）与幼鸟交流，并警告（warn）它们有危险。这些叫声是微弱的（faint）且容易被忽略，但人工智能能够清晰地发现（detect）它们。科学家们在草原上安装麦克风（microphone），夜以继日地录制声音。然后他们将这些录音（recording）输入到计算机程序中。人工智能能学会区分出（distinguish）领鹑的叫声与其他噪音（noise），如风（wind）或昆虫（insect）的声音的差别。这有助于科学家找到雌鸟并统计（count）它们的数量。“人工智能帮助我们监测这些鸟类而不打扰（disturb）它们，”项目（project）负责人李博士说道。“我们可以识别出（identify）对它们来说最重要的区域，并努力保护那些（those）地方。”有一次，人工智能帮助科学家找到了一个有三只幼鸟的隐蔽（hidden）巢穴。如果没有人工智能，他们可能永远也找不到它。人工智能确实（really）是拯教野生动物（wildlife）的有力工具。随着人类活动不断侵占自然区域，无数珍稀物种（species）正面临灭绝（extinction）威胁（threat）。传统的野生动物调查（survey）方法（method）往往需要大量人力、时间和现场（on-site）观测（observation），这还可能破坏鸟类的正常生活习惯（habit）。人工智能技术与生态保护的结合（combination）为全球的野生动物保护树立了一个好的榜样。它不仅提升（improve）了物种监测的准确性（accuracy）和效率，还使研究人员能够悄悄地（quietly）收集到可靠的（reliable）数据。如果我们可以平衡经济发展与生态保护（preservation），更多的濒危生物便能存活（survive）下来，与人类在地球上和平共处（live in peace）。

sentences.en: The plain wanderer is a small and rare bird living on the grassland.
sentences.cn: 领鹑（plain Wanderer）是一种生活在草原（grassland）上的小型的稀有的（rare）鸟类。

sentences.en: Different from most birds, female plain wanderers are bigger and stronger.
sentences.cn: 与大多数鸟类不同的是，雌性的（female）领鹑体型更大、更强壮。

sentences.en: Females responsible for defending nests and chicks from are animals like foxes, while males hatch the eggs and keep them warm.
sentences.cn: 雌鸟负责（responsible）保卫巢穴（nest）和雏鸟（chick），抵御（defend）狐狸（fox）等动物（animal）的侵袭，而雄鸟（male）则负责孵（hatch）鸟蛋并为其保暖。

sentences.en: Their feathers make them look like part of the land.
sentences.cn: 它们的羽毛（feather）使它们看起来就像是这片土地的一部分。

sentences.en: Sadly, their numbers are dropping humans occupy their grassland habitats for farms and cities.
sentences.cn: 不幸的是（sadly），由于人类侵占（occupy）它们的草原栖息地（habitat）用于建农场和城市，它们的数量正在不断减少（drop）。

sentences.en: To save them, scientists are using AI.
sentences.cn: 为了保护它们，科学家们正在利用人工智能。

sentences.en: The key is the birds' calls.
sentences.cn: 关键（key）在于这些鸟的叫声。

sentences.en: Female birds make soft sounds to communicate with their chicks and warn of danger.
sentences.cn: 雌鸟会发出轻柔的（soft）声音（sound）与幼鸟交流，并警告（warn）它们有危险。

sentences.en: These calls are faint and easy to miss, but AI can detect them clearly.
sentences.cn: 这些叫声是微弱的（faint）且容易被忽略，但人工智能能够清晰地发现（detect）它们。

sentences.en: Scientists put microphones in the grassland to record sounds day and night.
sentences.cn: 科学家们在草原上安装麦克风（microphone），夜以继日地录制声音。

sentences.en: Then they put these recordings into a computer program.
sentences.cn: 然后他们将这些录音（recording）输入到计算机程序中。

sentences.en: AI learns to distinguish the plain wanderer's calls from other noises like the sound of wind or insects.
sentences.cn: 人工智能能学会区分出（distinguish）领鹑的叫声与其他噪音（noise），如风（wind）或昆虫（insect）的声音的差别。

sentences.en: This helps scientists find female birds and count their numbers.
sentences.cn: 这有助于科学家找到雌鸟并统计（count）它们的数量。

sentences.en: “AI helps us monitor these birds without disturbing them," says Dr Li, the project leader.
sentences.cn: “人工智能帮助我们监测这些鸟类而不打扰（disturb）它们，”项目（project）负责人李博士说道。

sentences.en: "We can identify the most important areas for them and work to protect those places."
sentences.cn: “我们可以识别出（identify）对它们来说最重要的区域，并努力保护那些（those）地方。”

sentences.en: Once, AI helped scientists find a hidden nest with three baby birds.
sentences.cn: 有一次，人工智能帮助科学家找到了一个有三只幼鸟的隐蔽（hidden）巢穴。

sentences.en: Without AI, they might never have found it.
sentences.cn: 如果没有人工智能，他们可能永远也找不到它。

sentences.en: AI is really a powerful tool to save wildlife.
sentences.cn: 人工智能确实（really）是拯教野生动物（wildlife）的有力工具。

sentences.en: As human activities continue to spread across natural landscapes, countless rare species are facing the threat of extinction.
sentences.cn: 随着人类活动不断侵占自然区域，无数珍稀物种（species）正面临灭绝（extinction）威胁（threat）。

sentences.en: Traditional wildlife survey methods often require plenty of manpower, time andon-site observations, which may also disturb the birds' normal living habits.
sentences.cn: 传统的野生动物调查（survey）方法（method）往往需要大量人力、时间和现场（on-site）观测（observation），这还可能破坏鸟类的正常生活习惯（habit）。

sentences.en: The combination of AI technology and ecological protection sets a good example for wildlife conservation worldwide.
sentences.cn: 人工智能技术与生态保护的结合（combination）为全球的野生动物保护树立了一个好的榜样。

sentences.en: It not only improves the accuracy and efficiency of species monitoring, but also allows researchers to collect reliable data quietly.
sentences.cn: 它不仅提升（improve）了物种监测的准确性（accuracy）和效率，还使研究人员能够悄悄地（quietly）收集到可靠的（reliable）数据。

sentences.en: If we can balance economic development with ecological preservation, more endangered creatures will surely survive and live in peace with humans on Earth. intelligence automation facial recognition voice assistant chatbot self-driving car big data smart home
sentences.cn: 如果我们可以平衡经济发展与生态保护（preservation），更多的濒危生物便能存活（survive）下来，与人类在地球上和平共处（live in peace）。

readings.title: Is Playing Music Good for the Brain?
readings.text: The men who broke into Joseph Haydn's grave thought the secret of his genius might be seen on his skull. A scan of the composer's brain may have been musical talent does more enlightening. But in fact, r not leave signals on the head. Making music is like a mental workout. The brain must regulate sound, vision, as well as fine motor control, concentration and imagination. Over time, this enhances the brain. Many studies show that professional musicians have more grey matter (the neural tissue for thinking, movement and memory) in some brain areas than non-musicians. Though there is no conclusive proof, extant research hints that other benefits may accrue. A study found musicians may exhibit better executive function, which helps with planning and problem- solving. A recent study even found they may be less sensitive to aches. Music is indeed like medicine to heal painful hearts. Do children with musical aptitude gain a competitive edge? A paper found musicians who started training before the age of seven have a larger corpus callosum compared with those who commenced later. A study illustrated that learning an instrument improves children's second-language acquisition and non- verbal thinking ability. Acquiring systematic musical training in one's later life can delay age-related brain decline. A small study on the elderly found that continuing to learn an instrument was linked to less loss of verbal working memory and grey-matter volume. It means music practice may diminish the risk of dementia. However, it's still ambiguous whether this is because musical brains are stronger or because people without dementia maintain musical hobbies for an extended period. The instruments you play also matter. A study of 1, loo elderly Britons found pianists and brass players usually have better working memory. Besides, the brain's limbic system, which is in charge of pleasure, becomes active when you play instrument. Endorphin, a hormone that makes ani you feel good and reduces pain, is released when you focus on playing. Performing in a band, orchestra or choir reduces stress and helps people bond socially. Just listening to music may also help. A study found that those who listen to music regularly have a 39% lower risk of cognitive decline. But there is no evidence that music directly causes this. The good news is that studies show consistent training leads to brain changes in both amateurs and gifted professionals. But if you are as gifted as Haydn, you may request a guard to protect your tomb.
readings.translation: 那些闯入约瑟夫·海顿墓穴的人以为他天赋（genius）的秘密（secret）可以从他的头骨（skull）上找到答案。对这位作曲家（composer）的大脑（brain）的扫描（scan）或许能得到更有启发的（enlightening）发现。但事实上，音乐的（musical）天赋并不会在人的头（head）上留下信号（signal）。进行音乐创作就像是一种脑力锻炼（workout）。大脑必须调节（regulate）声音、视觉以及精细肌肉运动的（motor）控制、专注力（concentration）和想象力（imagination）。久而久之，这会增强（enhance）大脑。许多研究表明，专业音乐家（musician）在某些大脑区域的灰（grey）质（负责思考、运动和记忆（memory）的神经（neural）组织）比非音乐家多。虽然没有确凿的（conclusive）证据，但现有（extant）研究显示还可能产生其他益处。一项研究发现，音乐家可能表现出（exhibit）更好的执行的（executive）功能，这有助于规划和解决问题。最近的（recent）一项研究甚至发现，他们可能对疼痛（ache）不那么敏感（sensitive）。音乐确实（indeed）像良药，能治疗（heal）饱受伤痛的（painful）心灵。有音乐天赋（aptitude）的孩子会获得竞争优势（edge）吗？一篇论文（paper）发现，7岁前就开始训练的音乐家与之后才开始（commence）训练的相比（compare），聨眠体更大。一项研究表明（illustrate），学习乐器（instrument）能提高儿童的第二语言习得（acquisition）能力和非语言思维能力（ability）。在晚年接受系统的（systematic）音乐训练可以延迟（delay）与年龄相关的脑部衰退（decline）。一项针对老年人的小型研究发现，持续学习乐器能够减少语言的（verbal）工作记忆丧失（loss）和灰质体积的减少。这意味着音乐练习可能降低（diminish）患痴呆症（dementia）的风险（risk）。然而，这是因为音乐大脑更强健，还是因为没有痴呆的人能在长（extended）期（period）内保持音乐爱好（hobby），目前仍然是模棱两可的（ambiguous）。你所演奏的乐器也很重要。一项针对1100名英国老年人的研究发现，钢琴家（pianist）和铜管乐器（brass）演奏者通常具有更好的工作记忆。此外，当你演奏乐器时，负责（in charge of）愉悦（pleasure）的大脑边缘系统会变得活跃。当你专注于演奏时，会释放内啡肽，这是一种让你感觉良好并减轻疼痛的激素（hormone）。在乐队（band）、管弦乐队（orchestra）或合唱团（choir）中表演可以减轻压力（stress），并有助于人们建立在社交方面（socially）的联系。仅仅听音乐也可能有所帮助。一项研究发现，经常（regularly）听音乐的人认知能力下降的风险降低了39%。但目前没有证据（evidence）表明音乐直接导致了这一结果。好消息是，研究表明，无论是业余爱好者（amateur）还是专业人士，持续的（consistent）训练都会导致大脑发生变化。但如果你像海顿一样有天赋（gifted），你或许得要求（request）一个守卫来保护（protect）你的坟墓（tomb）。

sentences.en: The men who broke into Joseph Haydn's grave thought the secret of his genius might be seen on his skull.
sentences.cn: 那些闯入约瑟夫·海顿墓穴的人以为他天赋（genius）的秘密（secret）可以从他的头骨（skull）上找到答案。

sentences.en: A scan of the composer's brain may have been musical talent does more enlightening.
sentences.cn: 对这位作曲家（composer）的大脑（brain）的扫描（scan）或许能得到更有启发的（enlightening）发现。

sentences.en: But in fact, r not leave signals on the head.
sentences.cn: 但事实上，音乐的（musical）天赋并不会在人的头（head）上留下信号（signal）。

sentences.en: Making music is like a mental workout.
sentences.cn: 进行音乐创作就像是一种脑力锻炼（workout）。

sentences.en: The brain must regulate sound, vision, as well as fine motor control, concentration and imagination.
sentences.cn: 大脑必须调节（regulate）声音、视觉以及精细肌肉运动的（motor）控制、专注力（concentration）和想象力（imagination）。

sentences.en: Over time, this enhances the brain.
sentences.cn: 久而久之，这会增强（enhance）大脑。

sentences.en: Many studies show that professional musicians have more grey matter (the neural tissue for thinking, movement and memory) in some brain areas than non-musicians.
sentences.cn: 许多研究表明，专业音乐家（musician）在某些大脑区域的灰（grey）质（负责思考、运动和记忆（memory）的神经（neural）组织）比非音乐家多。

sentences.en: Though there is no conclusive proof, extant research hints that other benefits may accrue.
sentences.cn: 虽然没有确凿的（conclusive）证据，但现有（extant）研究显示还可能产生其他益处。

sentences.en: A study found musicians may exhibit better executive function, which helps with planning and problem- solving.
sentences.cn: 一项研究发现，音乐家可能表现出（exhibit）更好的执行的（executive）功能，这有助于规划和解决问题。

sentences.en: A recent study even found they may be less sensitive to aches.
sentences.cn: 最近的（recent）一项研究甚至发现，他们可能对疼痛（ache）不那么敏感（sensitive）。

sentences.en: Music is indeed like medicine to heal painful hearts.
sentences.cn: 音乐确实（indeed）像良药，能治疗（heal）饱受伤痛的（painful）心灵。

sentences.en: Do children with musical aptitude gain a competitive edge?
sentences.cn: 有音乐天赋（aptitude）的孩子会获得竞争优势（edge）吗？

sentences.en: A paper found musicians who started training before the age of seven have a larger corpus callosum compared with those who commenced later.
sentences.cn: 一篇论文（paper）发现，7岁前就开始训练的音乐家与之后才开始（commence）训练的相比（compare），聨眠体更大。

sentences.en: A study illustrated that learning an instrument improves children's second-language acquisition and non- verbal thinking ability.
sentences.cn: 一项研究表明（illustrate），学习乐器（instrument）能提高儿童的第二语言习得（acquisition）能力和非语言思维能力（ability）。

sentences.en: Acquiring systematic musical training in one's later life can delay age-related brain decline.
sentences.cn: 在晚年接受系统的（systematic）音乐训练可以延迟（delay）与年龄相关的脑部衰退（decline）。

sentences.en: A small study on the elderly found that continuing to learn an instrument was linked to less loss of verbal working memory and grey-matter volume.
sentences.cn: 一项针对老年人的小型研究发现，持续学习乐器能够减少语言的（verbal）工作记忆丧失（loss）和灰质体积的减少。

sentences.en: It means music practice may diminish the risk of dementia.
sentences.cn: 这意味着音乐练习可能降低（diminish）患痴呆症（dementia）的风险（risk）。

sentences.en: However, it's still ambiguous whether this is because musical brains are stronger or because people without dementia maintain musical hobbies for an extended period.
sentences.cn: 然而，这是因为音乐大脑更强健，还是因为没有痴呆的人能在长（extended）期（period）内保持音乐爱好（hobby），目前仍然是模棱两可的（ambiguous）。

sentences.en: The instruments you play also matter.
sentences.cn: 你所演奏的乐器也很重要。

sentences.en: A study of 1, loo elderly Britons found pianists and brass players usually have better working memory.
sentences.cn: 一项针对1100名英国老年人的研究发现，钢琴家（pianist）和铜管乐器（brass）演奏者通常具有更好的工作记忆。

sentences.en: Besides, the brain's limbic system, which is in charge of pleasure, becomes active when you play instrument.
sentences.cn: 此外，当你演奏乐器时，负责（in charge of）愉悦（pleasure）的大脑边缘系统会变得活跃。

sentences.en: Endorphin, a hormone that makes ani you feel good and reduces pain, is released when you focus on playing.
sentences.cn: 当你专注于演奏时，会释放内啡肽，这是一种让你感觉良好并减轻疼痛的激素（hormone）。

sentences.en: Performing in a band, orchestra or choir reduces stress and helps people bond socially.
sentences.cn: 在乐队（band）、管弦乐队（orchestra）或合唱团（choir）中表演可以减轻压力（stress），并有助于人们建立在社交方面（socially）的联系。

sentences.en: Just listening to music may also help.
sentences.cn: 仅仅听音乐也可能有所帮助。

sentences.en: A study found that those who listen to music regularly have a 39% lower risk of cognitive decline.
sentences.cn: 一项研究发现，经常（regularly）听音乐的人认知能力下降的风险降低了39%。

sentences.en: But there is no evidence that music directly causes this.
sentences.cn: 但目前没有证据（evidence）表明音乐直接导致了这一结果。

sentences.en: The good news is that studies show consistent training leads to brain changes in both amateurs and gifted professionals.
sentences.cn: 好消息是，研究表明，无论是业余爱好者（amateur）还是专业人士，持续的（consistent）训练都会导致大脑发生变化。

sentences.en: But if you are as gifted as Haydn, you may request a guard to protect your tomb.
sentences.cn: 但如果你像海顿一样有天赋（gifted），你或许得要求（request）一个守卫来保护（protect）你的坟墓（tomb）。

readings.title: BMF-a Smart Indoor Farm
readings.text: We all know fresh is best when it comes to food. However, most produce at the supermarket has a long tour covering hundreds of miles before its arrival on the table. During this long journey, fruits mostly lose their nutrition and fresh and vegetables flavour. While farmer's markets are a favourable choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more, bringing fresh greens right to people's apartments and workplaces. BMF is an indoor garden system designed for daily use. It can be easily built for a family, providing a whole bunch of fresh vegetables to meet their weekly needs. Additionally, it can support a larger audience such as a hospital, restaurant or school, where a stable supply of fresh produce is in great demand. The innovative design requires little effort to operate, making it possible for anyone to have a supply of fresh greens without professional gardening skills. It's a farm that particularly relies on cutting-edge technology. By connecting through the Cloud, BMF can be remotely monitored and controlled, saving users a lot of time and energy. Also, there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time, allowing users to know the growth status of their plants at any time. Because the system is fully automated, it dramatically reduces water consumption required for irrigation. Rather than wastefully watering rows of soil, the system calculates the appropriate amount of water and then waters the plants precisely, which is not only efficient but also environmentally friendly. After harvest, users simply replace the plants with a new pre-seeded pod to get the next growth round started quickly. Moreover, having a system in the same building where it's eaten means zero transportation emissions of plants from soil to salad, which helps reduce air pollution. In addition, there's no need for pesticides and other harmful chemicals that pollute traditional farmland and the surrounding environment, rendering the produce healthier and safer to eat. BMF employees live out sustainability in their everyday lives. About half of them walk or bike to work, cutting down on carbon emissions. Inside the office, they encourage the recycling of some used things and waste reduction by limiting dustbins and avoiding single-use chopsticks and plastic bags. "We are passionate about reducing waste, carbon and chemicals in our environment," said a BMF employee. Their efforts set a good example for others to follow, driving the world towards a more sustainable tomorrow.
readings.translation: 我们都知道，食物贵在新鲜。然而，超市（supermarket）里的大多数农产品在到达（arrival）餐桌（table）之前，都要经历一段长达数百（hundreds of）英里（mile）的长途旅行（tour）。在这漫长的旅程中，水果和蔬菜（vegetable）通常（mostly）会失去其营养（nutrition）和新鲜的风味（flavour）。而农贸市场是一个减少运输距离的有利（favourable）选择，巴比伦微型农场（BMF）甚至将这一距离进一步缩短（shorten），把新鲜的绿叶菜直接送到人们的公寓（apartment）和工作场所（workplace）。巴比伦微型农场（BMF）是一款专为日常使用设计（design）的室内（indoor）种植系统。它可以很容易给一个家庭建造（build），提供大量（bunch）新鲜蔬菜以满足他们一周的（weekly）食用所需。此外，它还可以支持（support）更大的受众（audience）场所，比如医院、餐厅或学校，因为这些地方对稳定（stable）供应新鲜农产品的需求（demand）很大。这种创新的（innovative）设计操作起来几乎不需要太多精力，使得任何人（anyone）都能够无需专业的园艺学（gardening）技能就能收获新鲜蔬莱。这是一个特别（particularly）依赖前沿（cutting-edge）科技的农场。通过云端互连，巴比伦徽型农场（BMF）可以进行远程地（remotely）监控和控制（control），为用户节省许多时间和精力。此外，还有一款便利的应用程序能够实时提供生长数据，使用户能够随时了解植物的生长（growth）状况（status）。由于该系统是全（fully）自动化的（automated），它急剧地（dramatically）减少了灌溉（irrigation）所需的消耗量（consumption）。不是浪费地对整排土壤进行浇水，而是由系统计算（calculate）出合适的（appropriate）水量并精确地（precisely）浇灌植物，这种方式不仅高效而且环保（environmentally friendly）。收获（harvest）后，用户只需用新的预先播种的容器（pod）替换植株，就能快速启动下一轮（round）生长过程。（transportation）过程是零（zero）排放（emission），这有助于减少空气污染（pollution）。而且，无需使用杀虫剂（pesticide）和其他会污染（pollute）传统农田（farmland）和周边环境的有害的（harmful）化学物质（chemical），使得（render）农产品食用起来更加健康、安全。巴比伦微型农场（BMF）的员工（employee）在每日的（everyday）生活中践行可持续性（sustainability）（环保理念）。其中约一半的人步行或骑自行车上班，从此减少碳排放。在办公室里，他们鼓励对一些废旧的（used）物品进行回收利用，并通过减少垃圾箱（dustbin）的数量以及避免使用一次性筷子（chopstick）和塑料（plastic）袋来减少（reduction）废弃物。一位BMF员工表示：“我们热衷于（be passionate about）减少我们所处环境中的废弃物、碳排放和化学物质。”他们的努力为其他人树立了良好的榜样，推动世界朝着更加可持续的（sustainable）明天（tomorrow）迈进。

sentences.en: We all know fresh is best when it comes to food.
sentences.cn: 我们都知道，食物贵在新鲜。

sentences.en: However, most produce at the supermarket has a long tour covering hundreds of miles before its arrival on the table.
sentences.cn: 然而，超市（supermarket）里的大多数农产品在到达（arrival）餐桌（table）之前，都要经历一段长达数百（hundreds of）英里（mile）的长途旅行（tour）。

sentences.en: During this long journey, fruits mostly lose their nutrition and fresh and vegetables flavour.
sentences.cn: 在这漫长的旅程中，水果和蔬菜（vegetable）通常（mostly）会失去其营养（nutrition）和新鲜的风味（flavour）。

sentences.en: While farmer's markets are a favourable choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more, bringing fresh greens right to people's apartments and workplaces.
sentences.cn: 而农贸市场是一个减少运输距离的有利（favourable）选择，巴比伦微型农场（BMF）甚至将这一距离进一步缩短（shorten），把新鲜的绿叶菜直接送到人们的公寓（apartment）和工作场所（workplace）。

sentences.en: BMF is an indoor garden system designed for daily use.
sentences.cn: 巴比伦微型农场（BMF）是一款专为日常使用设计（design）的室内（indoor）种植系统。

sentences.en: It can be easily built for a family, providing a whole bunch of fresh vegetables to meet their weekly needs.
sentences.cn: 它可以很容易给一个家庭建造（build），提供大量（bunch）新鲜蔬菜以满足他们一周的（weekly）食用所需。

sentences.en: Additionally, it can support a larger audience such as a hospital, restaurant or school, where a stable supply of fresh produce is in great demand.
sentences.cn: 此外，它还可以支持（support）更大的受众（audience）场所，比如医院、餐厅或学校，因为这些地方对稳定（stable）供应新鲜农产品的需求（demand）很大。

sentences.en: The innovative design requires little effort to operate, making it possible for anyone to have a supply of fresh greens without professional gardening skills.
sentences.cn: 这种创新的（innovative）设计操作起来几乎不需要太多精力，使得任何人（anyone）都能够无需专业的园艺学（gardening）技能就能收获新鲜蔬莱。

sentences.en: It's a farm that particularly relies on cutting-edge technology.
sentences.cn: 这是一个特别（particularly）依赖前沿（cutting-edge）科技的农场。

sentences.en: By connecting through the Cloud, BMF can be remotely monitored and controlled, saving users a lot of time and energy.
sentences.cn: 通过云端互连，巴比伦徽型农场（BMF）可以进行远程地（remotely）监控和控制（control），为用户节省许多时间和精力。

sentences.en: Also, there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time, allowing users to know the growth status of their plants at any time.
sentences.cn: 此外，还有一款便利的应用程序能够实时提供生长数据，使用户能够随时了解植物的生长（growth）状况（status）。

sentences.en: Because the system is fully automated, it dramatically reduces water consumption required for irrigation.
sentences.cn: 由于该系统是全（fully）自动化的（automated），它急剧地（dramatically）减少了灌溉（irrigation）所需的消耗量（consumption）。

sentences.en: Rather than wastefully watering rows of soil, the system calculates the appropriate amount of water and then waters the plants precisely, which is not only efficient but also environmentally friendly.
sentences.cn: 不是浪费地对整排土壤进行浇水，而是由系统计算（calculate）出合适的（appropriate）水量并精确地（precisely）浇灌植物，这种方式不仅高效而且环保（environmentally friendly）。

sentences.en: After harvest, users simply replace the plants with a new pre-seeded pod to get the next growth round started quickly.
sentences.cn: 收获（harvest）后，用户只需用新的预先播种的容器（pod）替换植株，就能快速启动下一轮（round）生长过程。

sentences.en: Moreover, having a system in the same building where it's eaten means zero transportation emissions of plants from soil to salad, which helps reduce air pollution.
sentences.cn: （transportation）过程是零（zero）排放（emission），这有助于减少空气污染（pollution）。

sentences.en: In addition, there's no need for pesticides and other harmful chemicals that pollute traditional farmland and the surrounding environment, rendering the produce healthier and safer to eat.
sentences.cn: 而且，无需使用杀虫剂（pesticide）和其他会污染（pollute）传统农田（farmland）和周边环境的有害的（harmful）化学物质（chemical），使得（render）农产品食用起来更加健康、安全。

sentences.en: BMF employees live out sustainability in their everyday lives.
sentences.cn: 巴比伦微型农场（BMF）的员工（employee）在每日的（everyday）生活中践行可持续性（sustainability）（环保理念）。

sentences.en: About half of them walk or bike to work, cutting down on carbon emissions.
sentences.cn: 其中约一半的人步行或骑自行车上班，从此减少碳排放。

sentences.en: Inside the office, they encourage the recycling of some used things and waste reduction by limiting dustbins and avoiding single-use chopsticks and plastic bags.
sentences.cn: 在办公室里，他们鼓励对一些废旧的（used）物品进行回收利用，并通过减少垃圾箱（dustbin）的数量以及避免使用一次性筷子（chopstick）和塑料（plastic）袋来减少（reduction）废弃物。

sentences.en: "We are passionate about reducing waste, carbon and chemicals in our environment," said a BMF employee.
sentences.cn: 一位BMF员工表示：“我们热衷于（be passionate about）减少我们所处环境中的废弃物、碳排放和化学物质。”

sentences.en: Their efforts set a good example for others to follow, driving the world towards a more sustainable tomorrow.
sentences.cn: 他们的努力为其他人树立了良好的榜样，推动世界朝着更加可持续的（sustainable）明天（tomorrow）迈进。

readings.title: John Todd and His Eco-Machine
readings.text: When John Todd was a child, he was fond of exploring the forest surrounding his estate in the countryside and curious about observing how nature resolved problems. For instance, a polluted stream often smelt and could turn clear after flowing through the grass or plants and along rocks where tiny creatures inhabited the underwater area. As he matured gradually, John was eager to know whether this natural process could be applied to tackle the pollution caused by humans. After specializing in agriculture, medicine and fisheries in college, Johnresumed observing nature and posing deep questions about its mysterious functions. Why can certain plants absorb harmful bacteria? Which sort of fish is able to feed on cancer- causing chemicals? He thought it was reasonable to infer that with a rational combination of animals and plants, he might be able to deal with waste in the same manner nature functioned. Thus, he made up (ner) ! his mind to build what he later named an eco-machine. The assignment John set for himself was to remove harmful substances from some sludge. First, he built a series of transparent fiberglass tanks that were connected to each other in the lab. Then he made a collection of some plants and animals from local ponds and streams and put them into the tanks. He waited patiently, and little by little, these different organisms adapted to each other and formed a stable and balanced ecosystem to meet his expectation. few weeks later, John added the sludge into the tanks. He was shocked by the unbelievable and satisfying results. The plants and animals in the eco-machine took the sludge as nutrients and started to consume it actively. Within several weeks, the sludge was completely digested, and only pure water remained. How magic it is! Over the years, John has undertaken many challenging tasks. He developed a greenhouse-like facility to treat sewage from 1,600 families in South under+ take=undertake Burlington. In addition, he designed an eco-machine to purify canal water in Fuzhou, a city located in the southeast of China. John calls his work “ecological design". “Life on Earth is like a package of spare components for inventors," he says.“You put organisms in new relationships and observe what happens. Then you allow these new systems to develop their own ways of automatic repair and recovery." John's eco-machine has been widely used in the majority of parts of the world, contributing to the resolution of numerous environmental issues. It also encourages more people to make joint efforts to build a greener future.
readings.translation: 约翰·托德小时候就喜爱（was fond of）在自家乡村（countryside）庄园（estate）周边的森林（forest）里探险，对大自然如何解决（resolve）问题充满好奇（curious）。比如，一条被污染的（polluted）小河（stream）往往散发着臭气（smell），但流（flow）经草（grass）或植物，以及水下的（underwater）区域有小生物（creature）栖息（inhabit）的岩石后，水就会变清。随着逐渐成熟（mature），约翰渴望（eager）知道这种自然净化过程能否用于处理（tackle）人类造成的污染问题。大学期间，约翰专门研究（specialize）了农业、医学和水产渔业（fishery）之后他重新开始（resume）观察大自然，并对它的神秘的（mysterious）运行机理提问（pose）深刻的问题。为什么某些植物能吸收有害细菌（bacteria）？哪种（sort）鱼能以致癌化学物质为食？他认为有理由推断（infer），，利用动植物合理的（rational）结合，他或许能够用与大自然相同的运作方式（manner）处理废弃物。于是，他下定决心建造后来被他称为“生态机器”的装置。约翰给他自己（himself）布置的任务（assignment）是清除一些淤泥（sludge）中的有害物质（substance）。首先，他在实验室（lab）里建造了一组相互连通的透明的（transparent）玻璃纤维（fiberglass）箱（tank）。然后，他从当地的池塘（pond）和小河中采集了一些动植物的收集物（collection），把它们放（put）进箱中。他耐心地等待着，渐渐地，这些不同的生物（organism）相互适应，形成了一种稳定且平衡的（balanced）生态系统，达到了他的预期（expectation）。几周（week）后，约翰把淤泥添加（add）进了箱中。他被这难以置信（unbelievable）且令人满意的（satisfying）结果震惊（shocked）了。生态机器里的动植物把淤泥当作养分（nutrient），开始主动（actively）消耗它。几周之内，淤泥就被完全消化（digest）了，只剩下纯净的水。多么神奇（magic）啊！多年来，约翰承担（undertake）了许多具有挑战性的任务。他开发了一个类似温室的设施（facility），用于处理南（south）伯灵顿1600户家庭的污水（sewage）。此外，他还设计了一台生态机器，用于净化（purify）福州的运河（canal）水，福州是位于（locate in）中国东南部（southeast）的一座城市。约翰称他的工作为“生态（ecological）设计”。“地球上的生命就像发明家（inventor）的一堆（a package of）备用零件（component），”他说：“你把生物置于新的关系（relationship）中，观察会发生什么。然后你让这些新系统自行发展出自动的（automatic）修复和恢复（recovery）的方法。”约翰的生态机器已在世界大部分（majority）地区得到广泛应用，是众多环境问题的解决（resolution）的原因之一（contribute）。这也激励了更多的人共同努力（make joint efforts）打造一个更绿色的未来。

readings.title: Make Inception a Reality
readings.text: Christopher Nolan's epic2oioblockbuster Inception is widely believed to be inspired by sci-fi animations and intricate, thrilling stories. But its main idea may be closer to reality today than ever before. In the film, Dom Cobb and his team adopt an advanced technology penetrate people's dreams to steal information. They aim to implant an idea into a CEO's consciousness during sleep to influence his behaviour in waking life. That's where real-life science and tech come into play. According to a 2020 study published in Consciousness and Cognition—conducted by Adam Haar Horowitz and his colleagues people can influence their dreams through a process called targeted dream incubation (TDI). In the study, researchers fitted participants with a wearable Bluetooth-enabled glove-like device This device uses sensors to track the wearer's sleep patterns and sends out sensory cues to influence dreams. As Haar Horowitz states, “We showed that dream incubation is tied to performance benefits on three tests of creativity, by both objective and subjective metrics. Dreaming about a specific theme seems to help after sleep." To achieve TDI, they used the Dormio glove to induce hypnagogia, the definition of which is a transitional dream state between waking and sleeping. In this state, the human brain is easily influenced. That means some stimuli can trigger ideas in subjects minds. Imagine you're falling asleep, but still awake. Suddenly, you hear an unexpected noise in your surroundings. In hypnagogia, the mind naturally interprets such outside stimuli in a way that makes sense in the dream scenario. Researchers placed 25 study participants in a hypnagogic state using Dormio. And once each of them emerged from their hynagogic state, they were required to perform various tests of creativity. The results showed that TDI helped them perform better on the tasks. various TDI is by no means the sole innovation that can change our perception of dream-related experiences researchers have even probed how to stop humans from needing sleep to dream at all. But TDI has distinct implications for a person's creative potential.“"Iconic people like Mary Shelley got creative ideas from their dreams," Haar Horowitz explains. "What makes our research different is that we deliberately cause these creativity-enhancing dreams in a precise and targeted way." We may still be far from doing what Dom Cobb and his friends did in the film. However, judging from existing research, it is very possible that humans will be able to control dreams to such a high level someday.
readings.translation: 克里斯托弗·诺兰执导的2010年史诗般的（epic）、非常成功的电影（blockbuster）《盗梦空间》被广泛认定（believe）是被科幻（sci-fi）动画片和错综复杂的（intricate）、扣人心弦的（thrilling）的故事所赋予灵感（inspire）。但如今其主要的（main）理念或许比以往任何时候都更接近现实（reality）。在影片中，多姆·柯布和他的团队采用了（adopt）一项先进的技术（technology）来进入（penetrate）人们的梦境以窃取信息（information）。他们打算在一名CEO睡觉（sleep）时将一个想法植入（implant）他的意识（consciousness）中，从而影响他醒着时的（waking）生活中的行为。这就是现实生活中的（real-life）科学和技术（tech）发挥作用的地方。根据2020年发表在《意识与认知（cognition）》杂志上的一项由亚当·哈尔·霍罗威茨及其同事实施（conduct）的研究，通过一种被叫做（call）定向梦境诱导（targeted dream incubation）（TDI）的过程可以操控梦境。在该研究中，研究人员给参与者配备了一款可穿戴的（wearable）蓝牙式的类似手套的设备（device）。该设备利用传感器（sensor）来追踪佩戴者的睡眠模式（pattern），并释放感官提示（cue）来影响梦境。正如霍罗威茨所陈述（state）：“通过客观的和主观的（subjective）两个（both）衡量指标（metrics），我们发现，梦境诱导训练与三项创造力（creativity）测试中的表现提升紧密相关（be tied to）。在睡眠之后，梦到特定主题（theme）似乎有帮助。”为了实现定向梦境诱导，他们使用了“多尔米奥”手套（glove）来引起（induce）临睡幻觉，它的定义（definition）是一种介于清醒状态与入眠之间的过渡的（transitional）梦境状态。在这种状态下，人的大脑是容易受到影响的。这意味着一些刺激（stimuli）可以用来触发（trigger）实验对象（subject）脑海中的想法。想象一下，你正在入睡（fall asleep），但你仍然是醒着的（awake）。突然，你听到周围环境（surroundings）中出现了一个出乎意料的（unexpected）噪音（noise）。在临睡幻觉中，大脑会自然地（naturally）以一种梦境中的场景（scenario）讲得通（make sense）的方式来诠释（interpret）这种外部刺激。研究人员让25名研究参与者通过使用“多尔米奥”手套进入入睡前的状态，然后一旦他们任何一个从入睡前的状态中摆脱出来（emerge），他们就被要求（require）去完成各种各样的（various）创造力测试。结果（result）表明，定向梦境诱导技术帮助他们在任务中表现得更好。定向梦境诱导绝不是（by no means）唯一的（sole）能够改变（change）我们对梦境相关体验（experience）认知的新方法（innovation）一一研究人员甚至还在探究（probe）如何让人类完全不再需要睡觉就能做梦。但定向梦境诱导对一个人的创作的创造潜力有着明显的影响（implication）。“像玛丽·雪莱这样的标志性的（iconic）人物，从他们的梦中获得了创作的灵感，”哈尔·霍罗威茨解释道（explain）。“让我们的研究与众不同的是，我们故意（deliberately）以精确的（precise）且有针对性的方式引发这些能提升创造力的梦境。”我们或许仍远未达成电影中多姆·柯布及其同伴所做的（事情）。然而（however），从现存的（existing）研究来看，人类相当有可能有朝一日（someday）实现高度成熟的梦境自主操控。

sentences.en: Christopher Nolan's epic2oioblockbuster Inception is widely believed to be inspired by sci-fi animations and intricate, thrilling stories.
sentences.cn: 克里斯托弗·诺兰执导的2010年史诗般的（epic）、非常成功的电影（blockbuster）《盗梦空间》被广泛认定（believe）是被科幻（sci-fi）动画片和错综复杂的（intricate）、扣人心弦的（thrilling）的故事所赋予灵感（inspire）。

sentences.en: But its main idea may be closer to reality today than ever before.
sentences.cn: 但如今其主要的（main）理念或许比以往任何时候都更接近现实（reality）。

sentences.en: In the film, Dom Cobb and his team adopt an advanced technology penetrate people's dreams to steal information.
sentences.cn: 在影片中，多姆·柯布和他的团队采用了（adopt）一项先进的技术（technology）来进入（penetrate）人们的梦境以窃取信息（information）。

sentences.en: They aim to implant an idea into a CEO's consciousness during sleep to influence his behaviour in waking life.
sentences.cn: 他们打算在一名CEO睡觉（sleep）时将一个想法植入（implant）他的意识（consciousness）中，从而影响他醒着时的（waking）生活中的行为。

sentences.en: That's where real-life science and tech come into play.
sentences.cn: 这就是现实生活中的（real-life）科学和技术（tech）发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: According to a 2020 study published in Consciousness and Cognition—conducted by Adam Haar Horowitz and his colleagues people can influence their dreams through a process called targeted dream incubation (TDI).
sentences.cn: 根据2020年发表在《意识与认知（cognition）》杂志上的一项由亚当·哈尔·霍罗威茨及其同事实施（conduct）的研究，通过一种被叫做（call）定向梦境诱导（targeted dream incubation）（TDI）的过程可以操控梦境。

sentences.en: In the study, researchers fitted participants with a wearable Bluetooth-enabled glove-like device This device uses sensors to track the wearer's sleep patterns and sends out sensory cues to influence dreams.
sentences.cn: 在该研究中，研究人员给参与者配备了一款可穿戴的（wearable）蓝牙式的类似手套的设备（device）。该设备利用传感器（sensor）来追踪佩戴者的睡眠模式（pattern），并释放感官提示（cue）来影响梦境。

sentences.en: As Haar Horowitz states, “We showed that dream incubation is tied to performance benefits on three tests of creativity, by both objective and subjective metrics. Dreaming about a specific theme seems to help after sleep."
sentences.cn: 正如霍罗威茨所陈述（state）：“通过客观的和主观的（subjective）两个（both）衡量指标（metrics），我们发现，梦境诱导训练与三项创造力（creativity）测试中的表现提升紧密相关（be tied to）。在睡眠之后，梦到特定主题（theme）似乎有帮助。”

sentences.en: To achieve TDI, they used the Dormio glove to induce hypnagogia, the definition of which is a transitional dream state between waking and sleeping.
sentences.cn: 为了实现定向梦境诱导，他们使用了“多尔米奥”手套（glove）来引起（induce）临睡幻觉，它的定义（definition）是一种介于清醒状态与入眠之间的过渡的（transitional）梦境状态。

sentences.en: In this state, the human brain is easily influenced.
sentences.cn: 在这种状态下，人的大脑是容易受到影响的。

sentences.en: That means some stimuli can trigger ideas in subjects minds.
sentences.cn: 这意味着一些刺激（stimuli）可以用来触发（trigger）实验对象（subject）脑海中的想法。

sentences.en: Imagine you're falling asleep, but still awake.
sentences.cn: 想象一下，你正在入睡（fall asleep），但你仍然是醒着的（awake）。

sentences.en: Suddenly, you hear an unexpected noise in your surroundings.
sentences.cn: 突然，你听到周围环境（surroundings）中出现了一个出乎意料的（unexpected）噪音（noise）。

sentences.en: In hypnagogia, the mind naturally interprets such outside stimuli in a way that makes sense in the dream scenario.
sentences.cn: 在临睡幻觉中，大脑会自然地（naturally）以一种梦境中的场景（scenario）讲得通（make sense）的方式来诠释（interpret）这种外部刺激。

sentences.en: Researchers placed 25 study participants in a hypnagogic state using Dormio. And once each of them emerged from their hynagogic state, they were required to perform various tests of creativity.
sentences.cn: 研究人员让25名研究参与者通过使用“多尔米奥”手套进入入睡前的状态，然后一旦他们任何一个从入睡前的状态中摆脱出来（emerge），他们就被要求（require）去完成各种各样的（various）创造力测试。

sentences.en: The results showed that TDI helped them perform better on the tasks.
sentences.cn: 结果（result）表明，定向梦境诱导技术帮助他们在任务中表现得更好。

sentences.en: various TDI is by no means the sole innovation that can change our perception of dream-related experiences researchers have even probed how to stop humans from needing sleep to dream at all.
sentences.cn: 定向梦境诱导绝不是（by no means）唯一的（sole）能够改变（change）我们对梦境相关体验（experience）认知的新方法（innovation）一一研究人员甚至还在探究（probe）如何让人类完全不再需要睡觉就能做梦。

sentences.en: But TDI has distinct implications for a person's creative potential.“"Iconic people like Mary Shelley got creative ideas from their dreams," Haar Horowitz explains. "What makes our research different is that we deliberately cause these creativity-enhancing dreams in a precise and targeted way."
sentences.cn: 但定向梦境诱导对一个人的创作的创造潜力有着明显的影响（implication）。“像玛丽·雪莱这样的标志性的（iconic）人物，从他们的梦中获得了创作的灵感，”哈尔·霍罗威茨解释道（explain）。“让我们的研究与众不同的是，我们故意（deliberately）以精确的（precise）且有针对性的方式引发这些能提升创造力的梦境。”

sentences.en: We may still be far from doing what Dom Cobb and his friends did in the film.
sentences.cn: 我们或许仍远未达成电影中多姆·柯布及其同伴所做的（事情）。

sentences.en: However, judging from existing research, it is very possible that humans will be able to control dreams to such a high level someday.
sentences.cn: 然而（however），从现存的（existing）研究来看，人类相当有可能有朝一日（someday）实现高度成熟的梦境自主操控。

readings.title: Du Futhe Sage of Poetry
readings.text: Du Fu, who was a very famous S Chinese poet, lived in the Tang Dynasty, which existed in China over 1,300 years ago. Du Fu was born in Henan in a family of minor officials, and was very clever and began to write poetry when he was only seven years old. As a young man, he wanted to serve the empire by becoming official, so he tried topass the imperial exams. However, he failed. As a result, he lived a hard life in the capital, Chang'an, for ten years and was very poor. When a big war started, Du Fu and his family had to escape to stay safe, and on his difficult journey, he experienced the pain of war and much suffering. These experiences ultimately inspired him to write many great poems. In Du Fu's poems, which often indicate the harsh realities of his time, we can clearly find the pain of a mother losing her child, the hunger of soldiers, and the ruin of homes, all of which he witnessed with his own eyes. His words are so lively that they truly bring history to life, allowing readers to feel as if they are experiencing those tragic moments themselves. Du Fu's poems show his deep love for the people, as they repeatedly express that even when he was poor and sick, he always cared about others. This is especially evident in one of his famous poems, which says, “If I had a thousand big and warm houses, I would shelter all the poor and cold people and keep them happy!" readings.translation: 杜甫是一位非常著名的（famous）中国诗人（poet），他生活在1300多（over）年以前（ago）存在（exist）于中国（China）的唐朝。杜甫出生在河南一个普通基层（minor）官吏（official）家庭，他非常聪明（clever），年仅（only）七（seven）岁就开始（begin）写诗歌（poetry）。作为一个年轻人（man），他想通过成为一名官员来报效朝廷（empire），于是他努力去通过（pass）科举考试（imperial exams）。然而，他落榜了。结果，他在都城（capital）长安过了十年艰苦的（hard）生活，并且非常贫穷。当一场大战（war）爆发时，杜甫和他的家人不得不逃跑（escape）以保安全。在充满艰难困苦的（difficult）行程（journey）中，他亲身经历了战争的痛苦（pain）和许多苦难（suffering）。这些经历最终（ultimately）激发他写出了许多伟大的诗篇。在杜甫那些常常揭露（indicate）他所处时代的残酷（harsh）现实的诗中，我们能真切地读到一位母亲失去小孩（child）的痛苦、士兵（soldier）们的饥饿（hunger）以及家园的毁灭（ruin）一一所有这些都是他亲眼目赌（witness）的。他的文字（word）是如此生动（lively），它们真正地让历史（history）变得鲜活，让读者（reader）感到（feel）仿佛正在亲身经历那些悲惨的（tragic）时刻。杜甫的诗作显示出（show）了他对人民深切的（deep）爱，因为诗中重复地（repeatedly）表达出：即使在他自己贫病（sick）交加的时候，他也始终关心（care about）着他人。这一点在他的一首著名的诗中尤为明显（evident），诗中写道：“安得广厦（house）千（thousand）万间，大庇（shelter）天下寒（cold）士俱欢颜（happy）！”杜甫写了许多杰出的（outstanding）诗歌，并且关心贫苦百姓。他被称赞（acclaim）为“诗圣”（Sag eof Poetry）

sentences.en: Du Fu, who was a very famous S Chinese poet, lived in the Tang Dynasty, which existed in China over 1,300 years ago.
sentences.cn: 杜甫是一位非常著名的（famous）中国诗人（poet），他生活在1300多（over）年以前（ago）存在（exist）于中国（China）的唐朝。

sentences.en: Du Fu was born in Henan in a family of minor officials, and was very clever and began to write poetry when he was only seven years old.
sentences.cn: 杜甫出生在河南一个普通基层（minor）官吏（official）家庭，他非常聪明（clever），年仅（only）七（seven）岁就开始（begin）写诗歌（poetry）。

sentences.en: As a young man, he wanted to serve the empire by becoming official, so he tried topass the imperial exams. However, he failed.
sentences.cn: 作为一个年轻人（man），他想通过成为一名官员来报效朝廷（empire），于是他努力去通过（pass）科举考试（imperial exams）。

sentences.en: As a result, he lived a hard life in the capital, Chang'an, for ten years and was very poor.
sentences.cn: 然而，他落榜了。结果，他在都城（capital）长安过了十年艰苦的（hard）生活，并且非常贫穷。

sentences.en: When a big war started, Du Fu and his family had to escape to stay safe, and on his difficult journey, he experienced the pain of war and much suffering.
sentences.cn: 当一场大战（war）爆发时，杜甫和他的家人不得不逃跑（escape）以保安全。在充满艰难困苦的（difficult）行程（journey）中，他亲身经历了战争的痛苦（pain）和许多苦难（suffering）。

sentences.en: These experiences ultimately inspired him to write many great poems.
sentences.cn: 这些经历最终（ultimately）激发他写出了许多伟大的诗篇。

sentences.en: In Du Fu's poems, which often indicate the harsh realities of his time, we can clearly find the pain of a mother losing her child, the hunger of soldiers, and the ruin of homes, all of which he witnessed with his own eyes.
sentences.cn: 在杜甫那些常常揭露（indicate）他所处时代的残酷（harsh）现实的诗中，我们能真切地读到一位母亲失去小孩（child）的痛苦、士兵（soldier）们的饥饿（hunger）以及家园的毁灭（ruin）一一所有这些都是他亲眼目赌（witness）的。

sentences.en: His words are so lively that they truly bring history to life, allowing readers to feel as if they are experiencing those tragic moments themselves.
sentences.cn: 他的文字（word）是如此生动（lively），它们真正地让历史（history）变得鲜活，让读者（reader）感到（feel）仿佛正在亲身经历那些悲惨的（tragic）时刻。

sentences.en: Du Fu's poems show his deep love for the people, as they repeatedly express that even when he was poor and sick, he always cared about others.
sentences.cn: 杜甫的诗作显示出（show）了他对人民深切的（deep）爱，因为诗中重复地（repeatedly）表达出：即使在他自己贫病（sick）交加的时候，他也始终关心（care about）着他人。

sentences.en: This is especially evident in one of his famous poems, which says, “If I had a thousand big and warm houses, I would shelter all the poor and cold people and keep them happy!" Du Fu wrote many outstanding poems and cared about the poor.
sentences.cn: 这一点在他的一首著名的诗中尤为明显（evident），诗中写道：“安得广厦（house）千（thousand）万间，大庇（shelter）天下寒（cold）士俱欢颜（happy）！”

readings.title: The 2026 Milan Winter Olympics
readings.text: The 25th Winter Olympics concluded successfully on February 22nd in Italy. This was the third time that Italy had hosted such a grand international winter sports event. With the slogan “It's Your Vibe", the event aimed to encourage everyone to enjoy the passion of winter sports. Different from previous Winter Olympics, this event marked the first time that it had been co-hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, creating a special “city and mountain" co-host mode that had set a new example in the history of the Winter Olympics. Milan responsible for ice sports and cultural events, was while Cortina d'Ampezzoconcentrated on snow sports. Apart from this innovative co-hosting mode, the 2026 Winter Olympics also introduced new reforms to its competition events. There were 16 sports in the Games, including familiar ones like figure skating, short track speed skating, freestyle skiing and snowboarding. Besides, a new sport called ski mountaineering was added for this occasion. In addition, the 2026Winter Olympics adopted a variety of digital innovations. The most fantastic one was the “Digital Torchbearer" programme. People across the globe could participate in the virtual torch relay and share their Olympic stories through social media. The attractive official mascots were two cute stoats, Tina and Milo. Designed by creative local students, they represented the harmony between urban life and nature. Six snowflake partners called Flo were also members of the mascot family, representing cooperative spirit. The Games carried the concept of ecological conservation and launched a green campaign. The torch was made of recycled materials, and some venues could be reused after the Games. The Winter Olympics is not only an athletic feast centred on medals, but also a symbol of friendship, courage and sustainability. So let's applaud all athletes and enjoy the splendid winter sports!
readings.translation: 第25届冬季（winter）奥林匹克运动会（Olympics）于2月（February）22日在意大利（Italy）成功地（successfully）结束（conclude）。这是意大利第三（third）次举办如此盛大的（grand）国际冬季体育赛事。其口号（slogan）“意韵由你（It's Your Vibe）”，旨在鼓励每个人（everyone）感受冬季运动的激情。不同于（different from）往届冬奥会，本届冬奥会首次由米兰和科尔蒂纳丹佩佐联合承办，开创了“城市与山岳（mountain）”办赛模式（mode），为冬奥会的发展史树立了（set）新的典范（example）。米兰负责（responsible）冰上运动和与文化有关的活动，而科尔蒂纳丹佩佐则专注于（concentrate on）雪（snow）上赛事。除了（apart from）这种创新的（innovative）联合承办模式外，2026年冬奥会的比赛项目还迎来了新的改革（reform）。本届冬奥会共有16个大型体育项目，其中包括大家熟悉的（familiar）花样滑冰（skating）、短道（track）速滑、自由式滑雪此外，2026年冬奥会采用了（adopt）多种（variety）数字化（digital）创新（innovation）。其中最精彩的（fantastic）便是“数字火炬手”项目。世界各地的（globe）人都可以参与（participate）虚拟的火炬（torch）接力（relay），并通过社交媒体分享自己的奥运故事。吸引人的（attractive）官方吉祥物是两只可爱的（cute）白融，蒂娜和米洛。它们是由当地富有创造力的学生设计的，象作（cooperative）精神。本届赛事蕴含着生态（ecological）保护的理念。并发起绿色活动（campaign）。火炬由可回收的（recycled）材料（material）制成，而且部分场馆（venues）在赛事结束后可以再次使用。冬奥会不仅是一场以奖牌为中心（centre on）的体育（athletic）盛会（feast），更是一种象征着友谊、勇气和可持续性的（sustainability）活动。所以让我们为所有运动员鼓掌（applaud），一同享受这场灿烂的（splendid）冬季运动吧！

sentences.en: Milan responsible for ice sports and cultural events, was while Cortina d'Ampezzoconcentrated on snow sports.

sentences.en: Apart from this innovative co-hosting mode, the 2026 Winter Olympics also introduced new reforms to its competition events.

sentences.en: There were 16 sports in the Games, including familiar ones like figure skating, short track speed skating, freestyle skiing and snowboarding. Besides, a new sport called ski mountaineering was added for this occasion. In addition, the 2026Winter Olympics adopted a variety of digital innovations.
sentences.cn: 本届冬奥会共有16个大型体育项目，其中包括大家熟悉的（familiar）花样滑冰（skating）、短道（track）速滑、自由式滑雪此外，2026年冬奥会采用了（adopt）多种（variety）数字化（digital）创新（innovation）。

sentences.en: The most fantastic one was the “Digital Torchbearer" programme.

sentences.en: People across the globe could participate in the virtual torch relay and share their Olympic stories through social media.

sentences.en: The attractive official mascots were two cute stoats, Tina and Milo.
sentences.cn: 吸引人的（attractive）官方吉祥物是两只可爱的（cute）白融，蒂娜和米洛。

sentences.en: Designed by creative local students, they represented the harmony between urban life and nature. Six snowflake partners called Flo were also members of the mascot family, representing cooperative spirit.
sentences.cn: 它们是由当地富有创造力的学生设计的，象作（cooperative）精神。

sentences.en: The Games carried the concept of ecological conservation and launched a green campaign.
sentences.cn: 本届赛事蕴含着生态（ecological）保护的理念。并发起绿色活动（campaign）。

sentences.cn: 火炬由可回收的（recycled）材料（material）制成，而且部分场馆（venues）在赛事结束后可以再次使用。

sentences.en: The Winter Olympics is not only an athletic feast centred on medals, but also a symbol of friendship, courage and sustainability.

readings.title: CujuAncient China's “Football'
readings.text: Ancient Chinadeveloped over 2o0special sports. Many of them have a long history, and are believed to share similarities with modern sports. One sport that dates back to the Warring States period is Cuju. It was originally developed for ancient military training. Cuju is an ancient Chinese ball game. It is one of the traditional Chinese sports and a form of folk art. "ball"At first, the ball was made of leather and stuffed with feathers. In 2004, FIFA acknowledged Cuju as the earliest form of football, which made Chinese people proud. By the Han Dynasty, Cuju had become a widely welcomed and highly skilled activity. Even emperors at that time were Cuju fans. They not only liked watching the games but also practiced their footwork on the field. During the Song Dynasty, the competitive goal- scoring style gradually changed into a performance that focused on skills. The most famous Cuju star was Gao Qiu at that time. It is said that Gao Qiu gained the favour of Emperor Huizong of the Song Dynasty due to his excellent Cuju skills. Furthermore, even women and children enjoyed playing Cuju at that time. There were paintings of men and women playing Cuju together on some bronze mirrors of the Song Dynasty, reflecting the popularity of Cuju as a form of amusement in China's history. In Cuju matches, each team of six players competes to score by kicking the ball through the opponent's goal. Does that sound familiar? Today, Cuju is not only regarded as a sport but also as a spiritual and cultural symbol for the Chinese people. Like other sports around the world, traditional Chinese sports such as martial arts, dragon boat racing and Cuju were developed from practical needs in daily life, production or military training, while also shaping different cultural qualities.
readings.translation: 文学艺术与体育古代的（ancient）中国发展（develop）出了200多种特别的（special）体育运动（sport）。其中许多有着悠久的历史，并且被认为（believe）与现代体育运动有相似性（similarity）。一项可追溯到战国时期（period）的运动就是就瀚。它起初（originally）是为古代的军事（military）训练而发展起来的。瀚是中国古代的一种球类运动（ballgame）。它既是中国传统体育项目之一，也是一种民间艺术形式。“”字代表（stand for）的是“踢（kick）”“瀚”的意思是“球”。起初，球是用皮革（leather）制成，内部塞满（stuff）羽毛（feather）。2004年，国际足联承认（acknowledge）跪瀚为最早的足球（football）雏形，这让中国人感到自豪（proud）。在汉代，就瀚成为了一项广泛（widely）受欢迎（welcome）且非常（highly）有技能的（skilled）活动。甚至连当时的皇帝（emperor）都是跪瀚迷。他们不仅喜欢（like）观看（watch）比赛（game），还会在球场上练习脚法（footwork）在宋代期间（during），以进球得分为目标的竞争性（competitive）形式逐渐转变为一种注重技巧表演（performance）的形式。那时候最著名的跪瀚明星（star）是高。据说高因（dueto）其优秀的豌瀚技艺赢得了宋徽宗的偏爱（favour）。此外（furthermore），那时甚至连妇女（women）和儿童也喜欢就瀚。宋代的一些青铜（bronze）镜子（mirror）上就有男女一起瀚的绘画，这反映了就瀚作为中国历史上一种娱乐（amusement）形式的流行（popularity）程度。在就瀚比赛中，每队（team）六名队员通过将球踢进对方（opponent）的球门（goal）来得分。听起来是不是很熟悉？如今，就翰不仅被视为一项运动，也（also）是中国人民的一种精神（spiritual）与文化（cultural）的象征（symbol）。像世界各地的其他运动一样，中国传统体育运动，如武术（martial arts）、龙（dragon）舟（boat）赛（racing）和就瀚，都是从日常生活、生产或军事训练的实际需求（need）中发展而来的，同时（while）也塑造了不同的（different）文化特质。

readings.title: A Sweet Traditional Chinese Art
readings.titleCn: 一门甜蜜的传统中国艺术
readings.text: Do you know sugar painting? Like paper cutting, it's a wonderful traditional Chinese art form as well. Artists use a small spoon with a long handle to avoid burns while scooping hot, melted sugar. The sugar is usually a mix of white sugar and other kinds of sugar. Then the artists draw some pretty and vivid pictures on a flat stone slab. Sugar painting, which has a history of more than 1,300 years, is always popular at busy temple fairs. But how did this fun art begin? The history of sugar painting dates back to the Tang Dynasty. According to folk legend, there was a famous poet named Chen Zi'ang who had a great passion for eating sugar, but he enjoyed it in an unusual way. First, he melted the sugar over a small stove until it turned golden and sticky. Then, he drew some flowers and trees with the melted unusual sugar on a flat, oiled board. When the sugar cooled and hardened, he peeled it off gently and ate it. That's how sugar painting began. Over time, this simple way of enjoying sugar evolved into a folk art. As years passed, sugar painting changed and improved gradually. In the Qing Dynasty, artists mastered new skills. They began drawing patterns with good blessings to make sugar paintings, such as birds and fish. So charming were these paintings that more and more people came to embrace this art form. These traditional patterns, carrying good wishes, have remained popular ever since. Today, sugar painting has grown into a more exciting art form, ranging from cartoon characters to 3D creations. Frequently purchased by foreign visitors to China as souvenirs, sugar painting is not merely a sweet snack it also serves as a window for people everywhere learn about traditional Chinese art. With its sweetness and beauty, sugar painting continues to win people's hearts everywhere around the world.
readings.translation: 你了解糖画（sugar painting）吗？和剪纸（paper cutting）一样，它也是一门精妙的中国（Chinese）传统（traditional）艺术（art）形式。手艺人（artist）用长柄（handle）小（small）勺（spoon），雷取（scoop）滚烫的（hot）融化了的（melted）糖，以此避免烫伤。这种糖通常是白砂糖（white sugar）和其他糖类的混合（mix）。随后，手艺人们在平整的（flat）石（stone）板上，勾勃出漂亮的（pretty）、生动的图片（picture）。拥有一千三百多年历史的糖画，一直盛行于热闹的（busy）庙会（temple fair）之中。但是，这门有趣的（fun）艺术究竞是如何起源的呢？糖画的历史可以追潮到（date back to）唐朝。根据民间（folk）传说（legend），著名诗人陈子昂十分喜爱吃糖，不过他吃糖的方式却是不平常的（unusual）。首先，他用小火炉（stove）熬煮糖，直到（until）糖色变成（turn）金黄、质地黏稠（sticky）为止。接着，他用融化了的糖在平整的涂油木板（board）上画出花草树木。待糖液冷却（cool）凝固后，他轻轻（gently）揭下（peel off）食用。糖画便由此诞生。久而久之，这种简单的（simple）食糖方式逐渐发展成（evolve into）一门民间艺术。岁月流转，糖画技艺不断改良、日臻完善。到了清代，手艺人们掌握了新的（new）技法，他们开始绘制蕴含美好祝福（blessing）的图案（pattern）来制作糖画，如鸟（bird）和鱼。糖画是如此的迷人（charming），以至于越来越多的人开始接纳（embrace）这种艺术形式。这些承载着美好祝愿（wish）的传统图案从那以后一直很受欢迎。如今，糖画已发展成一种更加引人入胜的（exciting）艺术形式，题材涵盖卡通形象乃至3D造型（creation）。外国（foreign）游客（visitor）来华常购买糖画当作纪念品（souvenir）。它不只是一份香甜的小吃（snack）一一更是世界各地（everywhere）的人们了解中国传统艺术的窗口（window）。凭借它的甜蜜（sweetness）与美感，糖画不断深受世界各地人们的喜爱（winpeople's hearts）。

sentences.en: Do you know sugar painting?
sentences.cn: 你了解糖画（sugar painting）吗？

sentences.en: Like paper cutting, it's a wonderful traditional Chinese art form as well.
sentences.cn: 和剪纸（paper cutting）一样，它也是一门精妙的中国（Chinese）传统（traditional）艺术（art）形式。

sentences.en: Artists use a small spoon with a long handle to avoid burns while scooping hot, melted sugar.
sentences.cn: 手艺人（artist）用长柄（handle）小（small）勺（spoon），雷取（scoop）滚烫的（hot）融化了的（melted）糖，以此避免烫伤。

sentences.en: The sugar is usually a mix of white sugar and other kinds of sugar.
sentences.cn: 这种糖通常是白砂糖（white sugar）和其他糖类的混合（mix）。

sentences.en: Then the artists draw some pretty and vivid pictures on a flat stone slab.
sentences.cn: 随后，手艺人们在平整的（flat）石（stone）板上，勾勃出漂亮的（pretty）、生动的图片（picture）。

sentences.en: Sugar painting, which has a history of more than 1,300 years, is always popular at busy temple fairs.
sentences.cn: 拥有一千三百多年历史的糖画，一直盛行于热闹的（busy）庙会（temple fair）之中。

sentences.en: But how did this fun art begin?
sentences.cn: 但是，这门有趣的（fun）艺术究竞是如何起源的呢？

sentences.en: The history of sugar painting dates back to the Tang Dynasty.
sentences.cn: 糖画的历史可以追潮到（date back to）唐朝。

sentences.en: According to folk legend, there was a famous poet named Chen Zi'ang who had a great passion for eating sugar, but he enjoyed it in an unusual way.
sentences.cn: 根据民间（folk）传说（legend），著名诗人陈子昂十分喜爱吃糖，不过他吃糖的方式却是不平常的（unusual）。

sentences.en: First, he melted the sugar over a small stove until it turned golden and sticky.
sentences.cn: 首先，他用小火炉（stove）熬煮糖，直到（until）糖色变成（turn）金黄、质地黏稠（sticky）为止。

sentences.en: Then, he drew some flowers and trees with the melted unusual sugar on a flat, oiled board.
sentences.cn: 接着，他用融化了的糖在平整的涂油木板（board）上画出花草树木。

sentences.en: When the sugar cooled and hardened, he peeled it off gently and ate it.
sentences.cn: 待糖液冷却（cool）凝固后，他轻轻（gently）揭下（peel off）食用。

sentences.en: That's how sugar painting began.
sentences.cn: 糖画便由此诞生。

sentences.en: Over time, this simple way of enjoying sugar evolved into a folk art.
sentences.cn: 久而久之，这种简单的（simple）食糖方式逐渐发展成（evolve into）一门民间艺术。

sentences.en: As years passed, sugar painting changed and improved gradually.
sentences.cn: 岁月流转，糖画技艺不断改良、日臻完善。

sentences.en: In the Qing Dynasty, artists mastered new skills.
sentences.cn: 到了清代，手艺人们掌握了新的（new）技法，他们开始绘制蕴含美好祝福（blessing）的图案（pattern）来制作糖画，如鸟（bird）和鱼。

sentences.en: They began drawing patterns with good blessings to make sugar paintings, such as birds and fish.
sentences.cn: 糖画是如此的迷人（charming），以至于越来越多的人开始接纳（embrace）这种艺术形式。

sentences.en: So charming were these paintings that more and more people came to embrace this art form.
sentences.cn: 这些承载着美好祝愿（wish）的传统图案从那以后一直很受欢迎。

sentences.en: These traditional patterns, carrying good wishes, have remained popular ever since.
sentences.cn: 如今，糖画已发展成一种更加引人入胜的（exciting）艺术形式，题材涵盖卡通形象乃至3D造型（creation）。

sentences.en: Today, sugar painting has grown into a more exciting art form, ranging from cartoon characters to 3D creations.
sentences.cn: 外国（foreign）游客（visitor）来华常购买糖画当作纪念品（souvenir）。

sentences.en: Frequently purchased by foreign visitors to China as souvenirs, sugar painting is not merely a sweet snack it also serves as a window for people everywhere learn about traditional Chinese art.
sentences.cn: 它不只是一份香甜的小吃（snack）一一更是世界各地（everywhere）的人们了解中国传统艺术的窗口（window）。

sentences.en: With its sweetness and beauty, sugar painting continues to win people's hearts everywhere around the world.
sentences.cn: 凭借它的甜蜜（sweetness）与美感，糖画不断深受世界各地人们的喜爱（winpeople's hearts）。

readings.title: Winning
readings.text: When Peter was an infant, he lost his legs. But that didn't make him feel sorrow at all. He never stopped trying various sports, either. His parents always encouraged him to do anything he liked. He tried swimming, wheelchair basketball and other sports, but he didn't find his affection. Though faced with repeated disappointments, he wouldn't tolerate frustration taking root in his heart. Anyway, he regarded every hardship as a stepping stone toward his undiscovered devotion When he was 7, he tried sledge hockey for the first time. At that moment, he felt the delight of sliding fast on the ice rink. He knew he adored it. When he was twelve years old, he told his parents, “It's all I want to do. I practice it every day after class." Later, Peterjoined a sledge hockey team. He arose early every morning to train for sledge hockey When Peter was an adolescent , he was very good at it. He began playing in an adult team. This was a big challenge for him because playing with adults was extremely difficult. But he never quit halfway. Now Peter is the youngest athlete in the US Paralympics sledge hockey team. An elderly player in the team says Peter is very fantastic. “Everybody dreams of taking part in the Olympic Games and being the champion," he says. “That's something I couldn't accomplish, but Peter can make it." Life is full of twists and turns, and hardship is never a permanent barrier on our road. Despite his physical disability, Peter's perseverance eventually paid off. Any obstacle he conquered has shaped him into a better individual. His optimistic mindset also inspired people around him. It's afact that when God locks adoor, he always opens a window for you. There is never absolute despair in life. You must be confident in yourself. Keep trying hard, and you will find your own methods to be successful.
readings.translation: 当彼得还是娶儿（infant）的时候，他失去了双腿（leg）。但那一点也不让他感到悲伤（sorrow）。他也（either）从未停止尝试各种各样的（various）运动项目。他的父母总是鼓励（encourage）他去做喜欢的任何事情（anything）。他尝试过游泳（swimming）、轮椅（wheelchair）篮球（basketball）以及其他运动，但他没有找到自己的喜爱（affection）。尽管屡次面临失望（disappointment），但他不容忍（tolerate）沮丧（frustration）在心中生根（root）。无论如何（anyway），他将每一次困难（hardship）都视为通向他那份尚未被发掘的挚爱（devotion）的垫脚石。在他七岁时，他第一次尝试了雪撬（sledge）曲棍球（hockey）。那一刻，他感受到了在冰场上快速滑行的乐趣（delight）。他知道自己喜欢（adore）上了这项运动。在他十二（twelve）岁时，他告诉（tell）他的父母：“这就是我想要做的全部事情。我每天课后都练习它。”后来，彼得加入（join）了一支雪撬曲棍球队。他每天早早起床（arise）进行雪撬曲棍球训练。当彼得成了一名青少年（adolescent）时，他已经非常擅长它了。他开始在一支成人队伍中打球。这对他来说是一个巨大的挑战，因为与成年人一起打球极其（extremely）困难。但他从未半途而废（quit halfway）如今，彼得是美国残奥会雪撬曲棍球队中最年轻的运动员（athlete）。队里的一位年长的（elderly）选手（player）称赞（accomplish）的，但彼得能成功。生活充满了跌宕起伏（twist sand turns），困难从来都不是我们道路（road）上的永久障碍（barrier）。尽管他的身体有残疾（disability），但彼得的毅力（perseverance）最终得到了回报（payoff）。他攻克（conquer）的任何（any）一个障碍都塑造他成为了一个更好的人。他乐观的（optimistic）心态也激励了他周围的人。事实（fact）是，当上帝（god）锁（lock）上一扇门（door）时，他总会为你打开（open）一扇窗。生活中从没有绝对的（absolute）绝望（despair）。你必须对自己有信心（confident）。不断努力尝试，你就会找到你自己的走向成功的方法。

sentences.en: At that moment, he felt the delight of sliding fast on the ice rink.
sentences.cn: 那一刻，他感受到了在冰场上快速滑行的乐趣（delight）。

sentences.en: He knew he adored it.
sentences.cn: 他知道自己喜欢（adore）上了这项运动。

sentences.en: When he was twelve years old, he told his parents, “It's all I want to do. I practice it every day after class." Later, Peterjoined a sledge hockey team.
sentences.cn: 在他十二（twelve）岁时，他告诉（tell）他的父母：“这就是我想要做的全部事情。我每天课后都练习它。”

sentences.en: He arose early every morning to train for sledge hockey When Peter was an adolescent , he was very good at it.
sentences.cn: 后来，彼得加入（join）了一支雪撬曲棍球队。他每天早早起床（arise）进行雪撬曲棍球训练。

sentences.en: He began playing in an adult team. This was a big challenge for him because playing with adults was extremely difficult.
sentences.cn: 当彼得成了一名青少年（adolescent）时，他已经非常擅长它了。他开始在一支成人队伍中打球。

sentences.en: But he never quit halfway. Now Peter is the youngest athlete in the US Paralympics sledge hockey team.
sentences.cn: 这对他来说是一个巨大的挑战，因为与成年人一起打球极其（extremely）困难。

sentences.en: An elderly player in the team says Peter is very fantastic. “Everybody dreams of taking part in the Olympic Games and being the champion," he says.
sentences.cn: 但他从未半途而废（quit halfway）如今，彼得是美国残奥会雪撬曲棍球队中最年轻的运动员（athlete）。

sentences.en: “That's something I couldn't accomplish, but Peter can make it."
sentences.cn: 队里的一位年长的（elderly）选手（player）称赞（accomplish）的，但彼得能成功。

sentences.en: Life is full of twists and turns, and hardship is never a permanent barrier on our road.
sentences.cn: 生活充满了跌宕起伏（twist sand turns），困难从来都不是我们道路（road）上的永久障碍（barrier）。

sentences.en: Despite his physical disability, Peter's perseverance eventually paid off.
sentences.cn: 尽管他的身体有残疾（disability），但彼得的毅力（perseverance）最终得到了回报（payoff）。

sentences.en: Any obstacle he conquered has shaped him into a better individual.
sentences.cn: 他攻克（conquer）的任何（any）一个障碍都塑造他成为了一个更好的人。

sentences.en: His optimistic mindset also inspired people around him.
sentences.cn: 他乐观的（optimistic）心态也激励了他周围的人。

sentences.en: It's afact that when God locks adoor, he always opens a window for you.

sentences.en: There is never absolute despair in life.

sentences.en: You must be confident in yourself.

sentences.en: Keep trying hard, and you will find your own methods to be successful.

readings.title: How to Enjoy Classic Literature?
readings.text: Classic literature holds timeless wisdom and fascinating stories. Maybe you are keen to explore these masterpieces but don't know how to start. Or perhaps you've tried reading classics before but gained little pleasure from them. Don't panic! Here are some tips that will teach you how to make them a fulfilling part of your literary journey. Pick the book that resonates with you. We all have our preferences when it comes to contemporary reads, so why should our attitude towards classic literature differ? Think about the genres you enjoy reading, including fables, and pick out a story that best suits your interests. Listen to an audiobook. One of the best ways of immersing yourself in a story is to hear it read out loud. Plenty of classic books were designed specifically for this purpose.A good audiobook narrator can excite your imagination, capturing not only the story but the context and history behind it depending on their tone of voice and delivery. Read more slowly. Contemporary fiction can feel rapid at times, just like a sprint, while classic works are much more of a marathon to get through. This is partly because, during their initial publication, many classic books were serialized, meaning that readers would often have to wait weeks before they could continue reading. Instead of rushing to the finish line, try to "go local" and savor the text, as the author expected. Fill in the gaps with research. When reading classic literature, one of the most common hurdles is the time gap between the author and the present day. Here are several effective strategies on how to read classic literature and do some research along the way. First, look up the history. If a story is set during an event or a period of significant history, research it for a better understanding of the context. Second, make a word list. Jot down any unfamiliar words or phrases, look them up online and build your own dictionary. Third, draft a list of characters. Classic novels usually have many characters. If there are too many for you to keep track of, make a quick reference list to keep handy. There is no shortcut to reading classics, but these strategies can make your journey smoother. In time, you will discover classics are accessible treasures that nourish your mind endlessly. （history） (strategy)。
readings.translation: 经典文学（classic literature）蕴含着永恒的（timeless）智慧和极有吸引力的（fascinating）故事。也许你渴望（keen）探索（explore）这些杰作（masterpiece），但却不知道该如何（how）开始。或者你之前曾尝试过阅读（read）经典作品，但并未从中获得（gain）多少乐趣（pleasure）。别惊慌（panic）！这里（here）有一些技巧将教你如何让它们成为你的文学（literary）之旅中让人感觉有意义的（fulfilling）一部分。选择能引起你共鸣（resonate）的书（book）。在阅读当代的（contemporary）读物时，我们每个人都有自已的偏好，那么为什么我们对经典文学的态度（attitude）会有所不同（difer）呢？思考你喜欢阅读的体裁，包括寓言故事（fable），然后挑选出最（best）满足（suit）你的兴趣的故事吧。听有声读物（audiobook）。沉浸在（immerse）故事中的最佳方式之一就是通过听别人大声地（loud）朗读故事。许多经典书籍就是为此目的而专门（specifically）设计的。一位优秀的有声书叙述者（narrator）能够激发（excite）你的想象力，凭借他们的语调和表演风格（delivery），不仅能传达（capture）故事本身，还传达出故事背后（behind）的情境和历史慢读。当代小说（fiction）有时会让人感觉是迅速的（rapid），就像短跑比赛（sprint）一样，而经典作品（work）更像是一场需完成的马拉松赛跑（marathon）。部分原因在于，许多经典书籍最初出版（publication）时是连载（serialize）形式，读者（reader）往往将会（would）等待数周才能继续阅读。不要匆忙冲（rush）到终点线，试着“放慢脚步”品味（savor）文本，正如作者（author）期望的那样。用研究来填补（fill in）空白。在阅读经典文学时，最常见的（common）障碍（hurdle）之一就是作者和当今（the present day）之间的时代差距。这里有一些（several）关于如何阅读经典文学并在阅读过程中进行一些研究的有效策略首先，查阅历史。如果一个故事是以一个事件（event）或一个重要的历史时期（period）为背景（set）的，研究它对背景有一个更好的（better）理解。第二，做一个单词表。快速记下（jot down）任何不熟悉的（unfamiliar）单词或短语（phrase），在网上（online）查找，并建立自己的词典（dictionary）。第三，草拟（draft）一个人物（character）列表。经典小说（novel）往往人物众多。如果有太多的东西让你记录，做一个快速的参考清单（reference list）随时备用（keep handy）。阅读经典作品没有捷径（shortcut），但这些策略能让你的阅读之旅更加顺畅。随着时间的推移，你会发现经典作品是可接近的（accessible）珍宝，不断地（endlessly）滋养（nourish）着你的头脑。

sentences.cn: 在阅读当代的（contemporary）读物时，我们每个人都有自已的偏好，那么为什么我们对经典文学的态度（attitude）会有所不同（difer）呢？

sentences.en: Think about the genres you enjoy reading, including fables, and pick out a story that best suits your interests.
sentences.cn: 思考你喜欢阅读的体裁，包括寓言故事（fable），然后挑选出最（best）满足（suit）你的兴趣的故事吧。

sentences.en: Listen to an audiobook.
sentences.cn: 听有声读物（audiobook）。

sentences.en: One of the best ways of immersing yourself in a story is to hear it read out loud.
sentences.cn: 沉浸在（immerse）故事中的最佳方式之一就是通过听别人大声地（loud）朗读故事。

sentences.en: Plenty of classic books were designed specifically for this purpose.
sentences.cn: 许多经典书籍就是为此目的而专门（specifically）设计的。

sentences.en: A good audiobook narrator can excite your imagination, capturing not only the story but the context and history behind it depending on their tone of voice and delivery. Read more slowly.
sentences.cn: 一位优秀的有声书叙述者（narrator）能够激发（excite）你的想象力，凭借他们的语调和表演风格（delivery），不仅能传达（capture）故事本身，还传达出故事背后（behind）的情境和历史慢读。

sentences.en: Contemporary fiction can feel rapid at times, just like a sprint, while classic works are much more of a marathon to get through.
sentences.cn: 当代小说（fiction）有时会让人感觉是迅速的（rapid），就像短跑比赛（sprint）一样，而经典作品（work）更像是一场需完成的马拉松赛跑（marathon）。

sentences.en: This is partly because, during their initial publication, many classic books were serialized, meaning that readers would often have to wait weeks before they could continue reading.
sentences.cn: 部分原因在于，许多经典书籍最初出版（publication）时是连载（serialize）形式，读者（reader）往往将会（would）等待数周才能继续阅读。

sentences.en: Instead of rushing to the finish line, try to "go local" and savor the text, as the author expected.
sentences.cn: 不要匆忙冲（rush）到终点线，试着“放慢脚步”品味（savor）文本，正如作者（author）期望的那样。

sentences.en: Fill in the gaps with research.
sentences.cn: 用研究来填补（fill in）空白。

sentences.en: When reading classic literature, one of the most common hurdles is the time gap between the author and the present day.
sentences.cn: 在阅读经典文学时，最常见的（common）障碍（hurdle）之一就是作者和当今（the present day）之间的时代差距。

sentences.en: Here are several effective strategies on how to read classic literature and do some research along the way.
sentences.cn: 这里有一些（several）关于如何阅读经典文学并在阅读过程中进行一些研究的有效策略首先，查阅历史。

sentences.en: First, look up the history. If a story is set during an event or a period of significant history, research it for a better understanding of the context.
sentences.cn: 如果一个故事是以一个事件（event）或一个重要的历史时期（period）为背景（set）的，研究它对背景有一个更好的（better）理解。

sentences.en: Second, make a word list.
sentences.cn: 第二，做一个单词表。

sentences.en: Jot down any unfamiliar words or phrases, look them up online and build your own dictionary.
sentences.cn: 快速记下（jot down）任何不熟悉的（unfamiliar）单词或短语（phrase），在网上（online）查找，并建立自己的词典（dictionary）。

sentences.en: Third, draft a list of characters.
sentences.cn: 第三，草拟（draft）一个人物（character）列表。

sentences.en: Classic novels usually have many characters.
sentences.cn: 经典小说（novel）往往人物众多。

sentences.en: If there are too many for you to keep track of, make a quick reference list to keep handy.
sentences.cn: 如果有太多的东西让你记录，做一个快速的参考清单（reference list）随时备用（keep handy）。

sentences.en: There is no shortcut to reading classics, but these strategies can make your journey smoother.
sentences.cn: 阅读经典作品没有捷径（shortcut），但这些策略能让你的阅读之旅更加顺畅。

sentences.en: In time, you will discover classics are accessible treasures that nourish your mind endlessly.
sentences.cn: 随着时间的推移，你会发现经典作品是可接近的（accessible）珍宝，不断地（endlessly）滋养（nourish）着你的头脑。

readings.title: History, Courage and Growing up
readings.text: The“ISurvived”series，a humble idea born about 15 years ago, has grown into a global literary phenomenon. Every novel transports young readers into the heart of true historical catastrophes from shocking weather events like hurricanes and tsunamis to widespread plagues. Through each gripping story, the writer demonstrates how an ordinary kid can rise to the occasion, displaying courage and resilience in the face of overwhelming danger. In 2010, Lauren Tarshis released her debut book, never anticipating that over the next decade and a half, the series would become a bestseller. To date, over 20 million copies have been printed, a remarkable achievement for any children's author. The series has 25 novels, with her newest publication n came out last October. Each book requires interviews with survivors, visits to historical sites, and meticulous study of original documents. During a recent visit to the Blue Willow Bookshop's Tweens Read Book Festival in Houston, Tarshis spoke about the latest novel of hers. It narrates the story of a boy named Ray who combats the perils of the Dust Bowl in the Panhandle of Texas. “A lot of kids have suggested this topic and asked for a story about the Great Depression," she explained. “So this is virtually two books in one. My research was thrilling because I visited destinations I had never been to. Walking across those dusty fields, I could profoundly feel what those children endured. It's been a tremendous experience." The idea for the series originated from her own family. As a mother of four, Tarshis noticed that her son Dylan labored to find books he fancied. "Dylan said to me, 'I desire to read a book about a cool topic with a protagonist that's a kid like me.' That was a big inspiration," she recalled. She realized that when a narrative centers upon an authentic youth at its core, young readers become deeply engaged. This insight prompted her to combine thrilling historical events with relatable child protagonists. Although each book in the series is a compelling page-turner, the underlying messages and themes are long-lasting and impactful. “My goal is to enable children to explore unfamiliar parts of the world and develop a genuine sense of connection to places they had never known before," Tarshis said. "I want them to see that people frequently undergo severe adversity, and it's about healing, finding help, and being patient while recovering from something scary:" By weaving these values into every adventure, she encourages young readers to be confident, confront obstacles with optimism and compassion, transforming historical events into powerful life lessons. advantages disadvantages
readings.translation: 《幸存者》系列丛书（series），诞生（born）于大约15年前一个不大的（humble）构想，已成为一种全球性的（global）文学现象。每一部小说都将年轻读者带入（transport）真实历史灾难（catastrophe）的深处一一从飚风（hurricane）、海啸（tsunamis）这类令人震惊的（shocking）天气事件，到大范围的瘟疫（plague）。通过每一个扣人心弦的（gripping）故事，作者（writer）展示了一个普通孩子如何迎难而上，在面对巨大的（overwhelming）危险时展现出勇气和坚韧（resilience）。2010年，劳伦·塔西斯发布（release）了她的首部作品（dc but book），（当时她）根本没预料到（anticipate），在接下来的15年（the next decade anda half）里，这个系列会成为畅销书（bestseller）。截至目前（todate），已印刷（print）超过2000万册，对于任何儿童作家来说，这都是一个了不起的成就（achievement）。该系列共有25部小说，她的最新出版作品（publication）于去年10月（October）出版。每一本书都需要对幸存者（survivor）进行采访（interview）、参观历史遗迹，并对原来的（original）文件进行严谨细致的（meticulous）研究。在最近（recent）一次参加休斯顿蓝柳树书店（bookshop）的“青少年阅读节”时，塔西斯谈到了她的（hers）最新小说。这部小说讲述（narrate）了一个名叫（name）雷的男孩在得克萨斯州狭长地带对抗（combat）“黑风暴灾区”带来的危险（peril）的故事。“很多孩子都提议（suggest）了这个主题，并要求讲述有关大萧条（the Great Depression）的故事，”她解释道。“所以这实际上（virtually）就是一部包含两部分的书。我的研究过程是令人激动的（thrilling），因为我走访了从未去过的目的地（destination）。走在那些满是尘土的（dusty）田野上，我能够深刻地（profoundly）感受到那些孩子承受（endure）了什么。这是一次非常棒的（tremendous）经历。"这个系列丛书的创意来源于（originate from）她自己的家庭经历。作为四个孩子的母亲，塔西斯注意到她的儿子迪伦努力（labour）寻找自己想要（fancy）的书籍。“迪伦对我说：‘我渴望（desire）读一本关于有趣的主题、且主角（protagonist）是像我这样的孩子的书。，这是很大的启发（inspiration）。”她回忆道。她意识到，当一个故事（narrative）核心聚焦于（centers upon）真实存在的青少年时，年轻读者就会被深深吸引（engaged）。这一感悟促使（prompt）她将惊险刺激的历史事件与能产生共鸣的（relatable）儿童主角相结合。文学丶艺术与体育尽管该系列丛书中的每一本书都是引人入胜（compelling）、让人手不释卷的读物，但其潜在的（underlying）信息和主题却是持久的（long-lasting）且触动人心的。塔西斯说：“我的目标是使孩子们能够（enable）探索世界中那些不熟悉的（unfamiliar）部分，并培养他们对那些之前从未了解过的地方产生真实的（genuine）归属感。我希望他们能看到人们经常（frequently）会经历（undergo）极为恶劣的逆境（adversity），而关键在于治愈、寻求帮助以及在从可怕的（scary）事情中恢复时保持耐心。”通过将这些价值观融入每一部冒险故事（adventure）中，她鼓励年轻读者树立自信（confident），以乐观（optimism）和同情的心态去面对（confront）障碍，将历史事件转化为深刻的人生启示。

sentences.en: She realized that when a narrative centers upon an authentic youth at its core, young readers become deeply engaged.

sentences.en: This insight prompted her to combine thrilling historical events with relatable child protagonists.
