sentences.en: Although each book in the series is a compelling page-turner, the underlying messages and themes are long-lasting and impactful.
sentences.cn: 文学丶艺术与体育尽管该系列丛书中的每一本书都是引人入胜（compelling）、让人手不释卷的读物，但其潜在的（underlying）信息和主题却是持久的（long-lasting）且触动人心的。

sentences.en: “My goal is to enable children to explore unfamiliar parts of the world and develop a genuine sense of connection to places they had never known before," Tarshis said.
sentences.cn: 塔西斯说：“我的目标是使孩子们能够（enable）探索世界中那些不熟悉的（unfamiliar）部分，并培养他们对那些之前从未了解过的地方产生真实的（genuine）归属感。

sentences.en: "I want them to see that people frequently undergo severe adversity, and it's about healing, finding help, and being patient while recovering from something scary:" By weaving these values into every adventure, she encourages young readers to be confident, confront obstacles with optimism and compassion, transforming historical events into powerful life lessons. advantages disadvantages
sentences.cn: 我希望他们能看到人们经常（frequently）会经历（undergo）极为恶劣的逆境（adversity），而关键在于治愈、寻求帮助以及在从可怕的（scary）事情中恢复时保持耐心。”通过将这些价值观融入每一部冒险故事（adventure）中，她鼓励年轻读者树立自信（confident），以乐观（optimism）和同情的心态去面对（confront）障碍，将历史事件转化为深刻的人生启示。

readings.title: The Amazing Journey of Seeds
readings.text: Plants have roots, leaves, and flowers, along with seeds. After the fruits ripen, the seeds need to be dispersed. Under suitable condition, new plants grow from seeds. Some seeds fall next to their parent plants and grow. When numerous plants grow densely together, they are too crowded to get enough sunshine and water. Some of them fail to survive. Therefore, some plants spread their seeds far away from their parent plants. How do they achieve this? Some plants spread their seeds with the wind. Maple seeds are shaped like wings. The wings make the seed spin, like a small helicopter, helping it drift farther away. Dandelion seeds are equipped with feathery hairs like parachutes, enabling them to drift freely in the air. As the wind blows, these seeds will be carried far away. Eventually, they descend to the ground, and new plants may grow there. Water is a good helper for seed dispersal. A number of plants thrive near water, and their seeds drop into the water and float away with the water current. For instance, coconuts have a buoyant husk, so they can float on the sea. Animals also contribute greatly to the spread of seeds. Certain seeds are equipped with special “hooks" or “stickers", which can catch onto the fur of passing animals or even onto people's clothes! By this means, they get a free ride, occasionally on a long trip. Birds can carry some seeds to distant locations, too. Besides, when some plants like peas reach maturity, their pods split open, forcing the seeds out several feet. Although seeds cannot move by themselves, they can travel with the help of wind, water and animals. Isn't that incredible?
readings.translation: 植物（plant）有根、叶和花，以及（along with）种子（seed）。果实（fruit）成熟（ripen）后，种子需要被传播（disperse）。在适宜的（suitable）条件下（under），新的植物从种子中生长出来。有些种子会掉落在它们的母本植株旁边，然后生长出来。当众多植物密集地（densely）生长在一起时，它们会太（too）拥挤（crowded），以至于无法获得（get）足够的阳光（sunshine）和水分。其中一些就会无法存活。因此，有些植物会将自己的种子传播（spread）到远离（faraway from）它们的母本植株的地方。它们是如何实现这一点的呢？有些植物会借助风（wind）来传播种子。枫树（maple）的种子形状像翅膀（wing）。这些翅膀会带动种子旋转（spin），就像一架小型直升机（helicopter）一样，帮助（help）种子飘（drift）得更远。蒲公英（dandelion）的种子配备了（equip）像降落伞（parachute）一样的羽毛似的（feathery）毛，使它们能够在空气中自由地（freely）飘浮。随着风吹（blow），这些种子会被吹得更远。最终，它们会降落到（descend）地面上，新的植物很可能会在那里生长出来。水是种子播撒（dispersal）的好（good）帮手（helper）。许多植物苗壮成长（thrive）在靠近水源的地方，其种子会落入水中，并随着水流漂走（float away）。例如，椰子（coconut）有一个有浮力的外壳，因此它们能够漂浮在海面上。动物对种子的传播也有很大（greatly）贡献。某些种子配备特殊的“钩（hook）”或“粘贴物（sticker）”，能够钩住（catch onto）路过的动物的皮毛（fur），甚至人们的衣服（clothes）！用这种方法（means），它们就搭上了免费的便车，有时（occasionally）是一段长途旅行（long trip）。鸟类也可以将一些种子带到较远的地方。此外，当一些植物如豌豆（pea）成熟（maturity）时，它们的豆英（pod）会裂开（split open），迫使（force）种子进出几英尺（foot）远。尽管（although）种子自身无法移动（move），但在风、水和动物的帮助下，他们就可以传播。这难道不难以置信（incredible）吗？

sentences.en: Plants have roots, leaves, and flowers, along with seeds.
sentences.cn: 植物（plant）有根、叶和花，以及（along with）种子（seed）。

sentences.en: After the fruits ripen, the seeds need to be dispersed.
sentences.cn: 果实（fruit）成熟（ripen）后，种子需要被传播（disperse）。

sentences.en: Under suitable condition, new plants grow from seeds.
sentences.cn: 在适宜的（suitable）条件下（under），新的植物从种子中生长出来。

sentences.en: Some seeds fall next to their parent plants and grow.
sentences.cn: 有些种子会掉落在它们的母本植株旁边，然后生长出来。

sentences.en: When numerous plants grow densely together, they are too crowded to get enough sunshine and water.
sentences.cn: 当众多植物密集地（densely）生长在一起时，它们会太（too）拥挤（crowded），以至于无法获得（get）足够的阳光（sunshine）和水分。

sentences.en: Some of them fail to survive.
sentences.cn: 其中一些就会无法存活。

sentences.en: Therefore, some plants spread their seeds far away from their parent plants.
sentences.cn: 因此，有些植物会将自己的种子传播（spread）到远离（faraway from）它们的母本植株的地方。

sentences.en: How do they achieve this?
sentences.cn: 它们是如何实现这一点的呢？

sentences.en: Some plants spread their seeds with the wind.
sentences.cn: 有些植物会借助风（wind）来传播种子。

sentences.en: Maple seeds are shaped like wings.
sentences.cn: 枫树（maple）的种子形状像翅膀（wing）。

sentences.en: The wings make the seed spin, like a small helicopter, helping it drift farther away.
sentences.cn: 这些翅膀会带动种子旋转（spin），就像一架小型直升机（helicopter）一样，帮助（help）种子飘（drift）得更远。

sentences.en: Dandelion seeds are equipped with feathery hairs like parachutes, enabling them to drift freely in the air.
sentences.cn: 蒲公英（dandelion）的种子配备了（equip）像降落伞（parachute）一样的羽毛似的（feathery）毛，使它们能够在空气中自由地（freely）飘浮。

sentences.en: As the wind blows, these seeds will be carried far away.
sentences.cn: 随着风吹（blow），这些种子会被吹得更远。

sentences.en: Eventually, they descend to the ground, and new plants may grow there.
sentences.cn: 最终，它们会降落到（descend）地面上，新的植物很可能会在那里生长出来。

sentences.en: Water is a good helper for seed dispersal.
sentences.cn: 水是种子播撒（dispersal）的好（good）帮手（helper）。

sentences.en: A number of plants thrive near water, and their seeds drop into the water and float away with the water current.
sentences.cn: 许多植物苗壮成长（thrive）在靠近水源的地方，其种子会落入水中，并随着水流漂走（float away）。

sentences.en: For instance, coconuts have a buoyant husk, so they can float on the sea.
sentences.cn: 例如，椰子（coconut）有一个有浮力的外壳，因此它们能够漂浮在海面上。

sentences.en: Animals also contribute greatly to the spread of seeds.
sentences.cn: 动物对种子的传播也有很大（greatly）贡献。

sentences.en: Certain seeds are equipped with special “hooks" or “stickers", which can catch onto the fur of passing animals or even onto people's clothes!
sentences.cn: 某些种子配备特殊的“钩（hook）”或“粘贴物（sticker）”，能够钩住（catch onto）路过的动物的皮毛（fur），甚至人们的衣服（clothes）！

sentences.en: By this means, they get a free ride, occasionally on a long trip.
sentences.cn: 用这种方法（means），它们就搭上了免费的便车，有时（occasionally）是一段长途旅行（long trip）。

sentences.en: Birds can carry some seeds to distant locations, too.
sentences.cn: 鸟类也可以将一些种子带到较远的地方。

sentences.en: Besides, when some plants like peas reach maturity, their pods split open, forcing the seeds out several feet.
sentences.cn: 此外，当一些植物如豌豆（pea）成熟（maturity）时，它们的豆英（pod）会裂开（split open），迫使（force）种子进出几英尺（foot）远。

sentences.en: Although seeds cannot move by themselves, they can travel with the help of wind, water and animals.
sentences.cn: 尽管（although）种子自身无法移动（move），但在风、水和动物的帮助下，他们就可以传播。

sentences.en: Isn't that incredible?
sentences.cn: 这难道不难以置信（incredible）吗？

readings.title: Harbour Seala Guest in Sanya
readings.text: Pandas live in the forests. But do you know "sea appeared in the sea near Sanya, Hainan Province. After people first saw it near Wuzhizhou Island on August 23,2023, divers also encountered it several times. And they filmed it lounging in the sea or climbing to rest on a float. Harbour seals are protected wild animals at a national level, living in temperate areas on the coast, such as the Bering Sea and the Sea of Japan in the North Pacific. In China, this species mainly appears in the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea. These seals are great swimmers. They use their hind flippers and the back of their bodies to propel themselves forward. They are also skilled divers, making more than 30 dives per day. They have the ability to reach depths of up to 300 metres. On land, they can only use their forelimbs and upper body to move, resulting in a somewhat silly and cute appearance. Because their behaviour is so lovely, they often capture the hearts of many fans when seen in zoos. People even refer to them as "sea pandas". A professor from Hainan University said, "The recent survey shows that the water here is becoming purer, and there are more fish and corals now. The fishery resources in Wuzhizhou Island have increased by more than two times in the past decade. These good changes may attract this special guest." As for where this harbour seal is from and why it comes here, there is no certain conclusion yet. In fact, scientists are still paying attention to this issue and doing further research. As one Internet user said,"Animals are very spiritual creatures of nature. They are an important part of our world. If we destroy their homes, we destroy our own future too." A worker said, "We will maintain the protection of the water environment. We sincerely hope that it can settle down here and become a new member of Wuzhizhou Island" This special visit tells us: a cleaner sea draws more wonderful lives.
readings.translation: 大熊猫（panda）生活在森林里。但你知道“海上大熊猫”吗？几年前，一只斑海豹（harbour seal）在海南省（province）三亚附近的海域出现（appear）。2023年8月（August）23日，人们首次在蜈支洲岛（island）附近见到它，之后潜水员（diver）也多次与它偶遇（encounter）。他们还拍摄（film）到了它在海里懒洋洋地躺着（lounge）或者爬上（climb）浮漂（float）休息（rest）的画面。斑海豹是受国家的（national）层面保护的野生动物（wild animal），它们生活在温带（temperate areas）沿海（coast）地区，比如北太平洋的白令海和日本海。在中国，这类物种（species）主要（mainly）出现在渤海和黄海。这些海豹是出色的游泳者（swimmer）。它们用后鳍肢和身体后部来推进（propel）自己向前（forward）游动。它们也是熟练的（skilled）潜水员，每天能进行超过30次的潜水（dive）。它们能够下潜到300米（metre）的深度（depth）。在陆地上，它们只能依靠前肢（forelimb）和上部的（upper）身体移动，因此呈现出一种呆萌（silly）又可爱的模样（appearance）。由于它们的行为（behaviour）是如此可爱，当在动物园（zoo）里看到它们时，它们常常会俘获许多粉丝（fan）的心。人们甚至称（refer to...as...）它们为“海上大熊猫”。一位来自海南大学的教授表示：“最近的调查（survey）表明，这里的水质正在变得更干净（pure），现在鱼和珊瑚（coral）也更多了。在过去十年（decade）里，蜈支洲岛的渔业（fishery）资源（resource）增长了两倍以上。这些良好的变化可能会吸引这位特殊的客人（guest）。”至于这只斑海豹来自哪里以及它为何来到这里，目前还没有确切的（certain）结论（conclusion）。事实上，科学家们仍在关注这个问题并展开更进一步的（further）研究。正如一位网友所说：“动物是自然界（nature）中非常有灵性（spiritual）的生物（creature）。它们是我们世界的重要部分。如果我们破坏（destroy）它们的家园，我们也是破坏了我们自己的未来。”一位工作人员表示：“我们将继续坚持水环境保护（protection）。我们真诚地（sincerely）希望它能在这里定居（settle down），并成为蜈支洲岛的新成员。”这次特殊的来访告诉我们：一片更干净的海域会吸引（draw）更多的奇妙生命。

readings.title: Plants Can Speak When They
readings.text: even “shout" if you treat them badly. Although this is ane exaggeration, plants can make sounds when they are stressed, according to a recent paper published in Cell. “Plants continuously have interactive relationships with insects and other animals, and many of these sound for communication, so it would organisms utilize be evolutionarily disadvantageous for plants not to use sound at all," Lilach Hadany, co-author of the study, said in an interview with the magazine Science Focus. A professional journalist recorded her words. With this in mind, the research team initiated the experiment by recording the sounds emitted by plants. They placed tobacco and tomato plants in soundproof boxes to block out ambient noise. Several ultrasonic microphones were then put near the plants, which can record at frequencies between 20 and 250 kilohertz. These high-frequency sounds are usually inaudible for human ears. The maximum audible frequency for human adults'ears is approximately 16kilohertz. The researchers arranged and divided the plants into three groups: one group wasn't watered for five days, another group had the stems cut off and the last group was untouched. The microphones caught sounds at a frequency of 40 to 80 kilohertz from the first two groups. The sound, which was comparable to the noise of popcorn popping when “translated" into a frequency humans can hear, grew louder and louder during the five days of water shortage. The sound then began to decline as the plants dried out. A stressed plant produced the popping sound around 30 to 50 times per hour, whereas the untouched group only produced around once per hour, according to the study. The researchers haven't yet discovered how the sounds are made. One theory is that they could be made during cavitation, which is a process of an air bubble in the plant collapsing under some kind of pressure. After the experiment, the team collected the data on stressed plants and then developed machine-learning software capable of making judgements about plants stress levels. It could differentiate between unstressed plants, thirsty plants and damaged plants, which can be useful for farmers in monitoring the conditions of their crops. In this way, farmers can take timely measures to save them.
readings.translation: 照顾好你的（your）植物（plant）吧！如果你对它们不好（badly），它们可能会“尖叫（scream）”甚至“呼喊（shout）"虽然这有些夸张（exaggeration），但根据最近发表在《细胞》杂志上的一篇论文（paper）所述，植物在有压力（stressed）时能够发出声音（sound）。该研究的合著者（co-author）莉拉赫·哈达尼在接受《科学聚焦》期刊（magazine）采访（interview）时说道：“植物与昆虫（insect）和其他动物（animal）之间持续地（continuously）存在着互动的（interactive）关系，而这些生物中的许多都利用（utilize）声音来进行交流（communication），所以如果植物完全不使用声音，那在进化上（evolutionarily）将会是不利的（disadvantageous）。”一位专业记者（journalist）记录下了她的这番话。考虑到这一点，研究团队便通过记录植物发出（emit）的声音开始（initiate）了这项实验（experiment）。他们将烟草和番茄（tomato）植物放入隔音（soundproof）箱中，以隔绝（blockout）周围环境的（ambient）噪声（noise）。然后（then），在植物附近（near）放置了几台超声的（ultrasonic）麦克风，这些麦克风能够记录20至250千赫兹（kilohertz）之间的频率（frequency）声音。这些高频声音通常人耳（ear）是听不到的（inaudible）。成年人类的耳柔所能听到的（audible）最高的（maximum）频率大约（approximately）为16千赫兹。研究人员将这些植物进行了整理（arrange）并分（divide）成了三组（group）：一组五天不浇水，另一组的茎（stem）被剪掉，而最后一组则是原封不动（untouched）。麦克风捕捉（catch）到了前两组发出的40至80千赫兹的频率声音。这种声音在被转换（translate）成人类能够听到（hear）的频率后，与爆米花（popcorn）爆开时发出的声响相似（comparable）。在缺（shortage）水的五天里，这种声音变得越来越响。然后，随着植物逐渐干枯（dry out），声音开始减弱（decline）。研究表明，有压力的植物每（per）小时会发出约30至50次爆裂声，然而（whereas）原封未动的组的植物每小时仅发出约一次。研究者尚未发现（discover）这些声音是如何产生的。有一种理论（theory）认为，这些声音可能是在气泡破裂（cavitation）过程中产生的，而气泡破裂是一个植物内部气泡(bubble）在某种压力作用下发生破裂（collapse）的过程（(process)。实验结束后，研究团队收集（collect）了有关受压植物的数据（data），随后开发出了能够对植物的受压程度做出判断（judgement）的机器学习（machine-learning）软件。该软件能够区分（differentiate）无压力的（unstressed）植物、缺水的植物和被损坏的（damaged）植物，这对于农民监测他们的作物（crop）的状况非常有用。通过这种方式，农民可以采取及时的（timely）措施拯救它们。

sentences.en: even “shout" if you treat them badly. Although this is ane exaggeration, plants can make sounds when they are stressed, according to a recent paper published in Cell.
sentences.cn: 照顾好你的（your）植物（plant）吧！如果你对它们不好（badly），它们可能会“尖叫（scream）”甚至“呼喊（shout）"虽然这有些夸张（exaggeration），但根据最近发表在《细胞》杂志上的一篇论文（paper）所述，植物在有压力（stressed）时能够发出声音（sound）。

sentences.en: “Plants continuously have interactive relationships with insects and other animals, and many of these sound for communication, so it would organisms utilize be evolutionarily disadvantageous for plants not to use sound at all," Lilach Hadany, co-author of the study, said in an interview with the magazine Science Focus.
sentences.cn: 该研究的合著者（co-author）莉拉赫·哈达尼在接受《科学聚焦》期刊（magazine）采访（interview）时说道：“植物与昆虫（insect）和其他动物（animal）之间持续地（continuously）存在着互动的（interactive）关系，而这些生物中的许多都利用（utilize）声音来进行交流（communication），所以如果植物完全不使用声音，那在进化上（evolutionarily）将会是不利的（disadvantageous）。”

sentences.en: A professional journalist recorded her words.
sentences.cn: 一位专业记者（journalist）记录下了她的这番话。

sentences.en: With this in mind, the research team initiated the experiment by recording the sounds emitted by plants.
sentences.cn: 考虑到这一点，研究团队便通过记录植物发出（emit）的声音开始（initiate）了这项实验（experiment）。

sentences.en: They placed tobacco and tomato plants in soundproof boxes to block out ambient noise.
sentences.cn: 他们将烟草和番茄（tomato）植物放入隔音（soundproof）箱中，以隔绝（blockout）周围环境的（ambient）噪声（noise）。

sentences.en: Several ultrasonic microphones were then put near the plants, which can record at frequencies between 20 and 250 kilohertz. These high-frequency sounds are usually inaudible for human ears.
sentences.cn: 然后（then），在植物附近（near）放置了几台超声的（ultrasonic）麦克风，这些麦克风能够记录20至250千赫兹（kilohertz）之间的频率（frequency）声音。这些高频声音通常人耳（ear）是听不到的（inaudible）。

sentences.en: The maximum audible frequency for human adults'ears is approximately 16kilohertz.
sentences.cn: 成年人类的耳柔所能听到的（audible）最高的（maximum）频率大约（approximately）为16千赫兹。

sentences.en: The researchers arranged and divided the plants into three groups: one group wasn't watered for five days, another group had the stems cut off and the last group was untouched.
sentences.cn: 研究人员将这些植物进行了整理（arrange）并分（divide）成了三组（group）：一组五天不浇水，另一组的茎（stem）被剪掉，而最后一组则是原封不动（untouched）。

sentences.en: The microphones caught sounds at a frequency of 40 to 80 kilohertz from the first two groups.
sentences.cn: 麦克风捕捉（catch）到了前两组发出的40至80千赫兹的频率声音。

sentences.en: The sound, which was comparable to the noise of popcorn popping when “translated" into a frequency humans can hear, grew louder and louder during the five days of water shortage.
sentences.cn: 这种声音在被转换（translate）成人类能够听到（hear）的频率后，与爆米花（popcorn）爆开时发出的声响相似（comparable）。在缺（shortage）水的五天里，这种声音变得越来越响。

sentences.en: The sound then began to decline as the plants dried out.
sentences.cn: 然后，随着植物逐渐干枯（dry out），声音开始减弱（decline）。

sentences.en: A stressed plant produced the popping sound around 30 to 50 times per hour, whereas the untouched group only produced around once per hour, according to the study.
sentences.cn: 研究表明，有压力的植物每（per）小时会发出约30至50次爆裂声，然而（whereas）原封未动的组的植物每小时仅发出约一次。

sentences.en: The researchers haven't yet discovered how the sounds are made.
sentences.cn: 研究者尚未发现（discover）这些声音是如何产生的。

sentences.en: One theory is that they could be made during cavitation, which is a process of an air bubble in the plant collapsing under some kind of pressure.
sentences.cn: 有一种理论（theory）认为，这些声音可能是在气泡破裂（cavitation）过程中产生的，而气泡破裂是一个植物内部气泡(bubble）在某种压力作用下发生破裂（collapse）的过程（(process)。

sentences.en: After the experiment, the team collected the data on stressed plants and then developed machine-learning software capable of making judgements about plants stress levels.
sentences.cn: 实验结束后，研究团队收集（collect）了有关受压植物的数据（data），随后开发出了能够对植物的受压程度做出判断（judgement）的机器学习（machine-learning）软件。

sentences.en: It could differentiate between unstressed plants, thirsty plants and damaged plants, which can be useful for farmers in monitoring the conditions of their crops.
sentences.cn: 该软件能够区分（differentiate）无压力的（unstressed）植物、缺水的植物和被损坏的（damaged）植物，这对于农民监测他们的作物（crop）的状况非常有用。

sentences.en: In this way, farmers can take timely measures to save them.
sentences.cn: 通过这种方式，农民可以采取及时的（timely）措施拯救它们。

readings.title: English Market Towns to Visit in the UK
readings.text: market towns come in many shapes and English sizes. Each has a personality shaped by the goods and services produced and traded for centuries. But each town and village has more to do than shopping. There are five charming Englishmarket towns to visit. The first one is Hereford, Herefordshire. Hereford has remained a lively market town since 1189. Skirting the town square, you'll find appealing shops, eateries and the Black and White House Museum. Hereford Cathedral is the most impressive building intown. It's also home to an ancient library. The 17th- century books were so valuable that they were chained to library shelves. One of the four original copies of the Magna Carta is displayed there. The Castle House Hotel rooms and is Hereford's top lodging. The luxurious grounds were once the site of Hereford Castle. The second is Ludlow, Shropshire. Ludlow is known as the Foodie Center of England. Butcher shops, greengrocers, bakeries, cheese shops, and groceries line the towns square. Bordering the square, Ludlow Castle is a “must explore"medieval stronghold with a sizeable inner bailey. The three-day Ludlow Food Festival is held each September. The third is Shrewsbury, Shropshire. The route from London is somewhat complicated but definitely not in vain. The River Severn has a significant turn through town, almost making an island of Shrewsbury Town Centre. The shape creates a perfect market where goods can be shipped and received using the river as a highway. A visit to Shrewsbury Town Centre will include narrow, twisting streets. Flowers are everywhere-hanging baskets, window boxes, and planters just what you imagine in an attractive English market town. The fourth is Mevagissey, Cornwall. Even if you haven't been to the small fishing village Mevagissey, you've probably seen it in a movie or British television show. The operational harbour took shape in 1774. Fishermen sail out daily and sell their fish in harbour-side markets. One of the most moving experiences is attending a concert of the Mevagissey Male Choir. The choir is made up of male singers, performing classical music. Don't leave the harbour without a traditional Cornish pie, which tastes delicious. The last one is Padstow, Cornwall. Padstow, a fishing port in Cornwall, is famous for a large quantity of seafood. One of the most rewarding things to do here is to taste fresh seafood, which can satisfy your taste buds.
readings.translation: 英格兰的（English）集镇（market town）形态各异、规模不一。每个集镇的特色都是由几个世纪（century）以来其所生产及交易的商品（goods）和服务（service）塑造的。但每个城镇和村庄（village）所承载的活动远不止购物。这里有五个迷人的（charming）英格兰集镇值得您去参观（visit）。第一个是赫里福德，赫里福德郡。赫里福德自1189年以来一直是一个有活力的市场城镇。沿着（skirt）城镇广场（square）漫步，你会看到一些有吸引力的（appealing）商店、餐馆（eatery）以及黑白木屋博物馆（museum）。赫里福德大教堂是镇上最令人印象深刻的（impressive）建筑。它还是一座古老的图书馆（library）的所在地。17世纪的书籍因其珍贵而被锁（chain）在图书馆的书架上。《大宪章》四（four）份原件（original copy）之一就陈列在那里。城堡（castle）旅馆（hotel）是赫里福德最好的住宿（lodging）选择。其十分舒适的（luxurious）房间（room）和庭院曾是赫里福德城堡的所在地。第二个是勒德洛，什罗普郡。勒德洛被誉为英国（England）美食家（foodie）之都。肉铺（butcher shop）、果蔬店（greengrocer）、面包店（bakery）、奶酪（cheese）店和食品杂货店（grocery）沿街遍布城镇广场。毗邻广场，勒德洛城堡是一座“必须探索”的中世纪（medieval）堡垒（stronghold），其设有相当大的（sizeable）内堡区。每年九月都会举办为期三天的勒德洛美食节（festival）。第三个是什鲁斯伯里，什罗普郡。从伦敦（London）出发的路线（route）有点（somewhat）复杂（complicated），但肯定（definitely）不是徒劳无功（in Vain）。塞文河有一个显著的转弯处（turn）穿过城镇，几乎将什鲁斯伯里镇中心围成了一个岛屿。这种形状为利用这条河作为交通要道（highway）运输（ship）和接收货物创造了一个完美的市场。参观什鲁斯伯里镇中心时，会看到狭窄（narrow）而婉蜓的（twisting）街道。到处都是鲜花一一悬挂着的（hanging）花篮、窗台花箱和花盆（planter）一一这正是你想象（imagine）中一个迷人的英格兰小镇市场的样子。第四个是梅瓦吉西，康沃尔郡。即使你未曾造访过这个小小的渔村梅瓦吉西，你可能在电影或英国电视剧（television show）中见过它。这座运转的（operational）海港（harbour）于1774年建成。渔民们（fisherman）每天出海（sail out）捕鱼，并在码头边的市场售卖（sell）他们的鱼。最令人感动的（moving）经历（experience）之一是参加梅瓦吉西男声合唱团（choir）的音乐会（concert）。这个合唱团由男性歌手（singer）组成，演奏古典音乐（music）。离开海港时别忘了传统的康沃尔馅饼（pie），尝起来（taste）十分美味。最后一个是帕德斯托，康沃尔郡。帕德斯托是位于康沃尔郡的一个渔港（port），以数量（quantity）众多的海鲜（seafood）而闻名。在这里，最值得做的（rewarding）事情之一就是品尝新鲜的海鲜，这能让你大饱口福（satisfy your tastebuds）。

sentences.en: market towns come in many shapes and English sizes.
sentences.cn: 英格兰的（English）集镇（market town）形态各异、规模不一。

sentences.en: Each has a personality shaped by the goods and services produced and traded for centuries.
sentences.cn: 每个集镇的特色都是由几个世纪（century）以来其所生产及交易的商品（goods）和服务（service）塑造的。

sentences.en: But each town and village has more to do than shopping.
sentences.cn: 但每个城镇和村庄（village）所承载的活动远不止购物。

sentences.en: There are five charming Englishmarket towns to visit.
sentences.cn: 这里有五个迷人的（charming）英格兰集镇值得您去参观（visit）。

sentences.en: The first one is Hereford, Herefordshire.
sentences.cn: 第一个是赫里福德，赫里福德郡。

sentences.en: Hereford has remained a lively market town since 1189.
sentences.cn: 赫里福德自1189年以来一直是一个有活力的市场城镇。

sentences.en: Skirting the town square, you'll find appealing shops, eateries and the Black and White House Museum.
sentences.cn: 沿着（skirt）城镇广场（square）漫步，你会看到一些有吸引力的（appealing）商店、餐馆（eatery）以及黑白木屋博物馆（museum）。

sentences.en: Hereford Cathedral is the most impressive building intown.
sentences.cn: 赫里福德大教堂是镇上最令人印象深刻的（impressive）建筑。

sentences.en: It's also home to an ancient library.
sentences.cn: 它还是一座古老的图书馆（library）的所在地。

sentences.en: The 17th- century books were so valuable that they were chained to library shelves.
sentences.cn: 17世纪的书籍因其珍贵而被锁（chain）在图书馆的书架上。

sentences.en: One of the four original copies of the Magna Carta is displayed there.
sentences.cn: 《大宪章》四（four）份原件（original copy）之一就陈列在那里。

sentences.en: The Castle House Hotel rooms and is Hereford's top lodging.
sentences.cn: 城堡（castle）旅馆（hotel）是赫里福德最好的住宿（lodging）选择。

sentences.en: The luxurious grounds were once the site of Hereford Castle.
sentences.cn: 其十分舒适的（luxurious）房间（room）和庭院曾是赫里福德城堡的所在地。

sentences.en: The second is Ludlow, Shropshire.
sentences.cn: 第二个是勒德洛，什罗普郡。

sentences.en: Ludlow is known as the Foodie Center of England.
sentences.cn: 勒德洛被誉为英国（England）美食家（foodie）之都。

sentences.en: Butcher shops, greengrocers, bakeries, cheese shops, and groceries line the towns square.
sentences.cn: 肉铺（butcher shop）、果蔬店（greengrocer）、面包店（bakery）、奶酪（cheese）店和食品杂货店（grocery）沿街遍布城镇广场。

sentences.en: Bordering the square, Ludlow Castle is a “must explore"medieval stronghold with a sizeable inner bailey.
sentences.cn: 毗邻广场，勒德洛城堡是一座“必须探索”的中世纪（medieval）堡垒（stronghold），其设有相当大的（sizeable）内堡区。

sentences.en: The three-day Ludlow Food Festival is held each September.
sentences.cn: 每年九月都会举办为期三天的勒德洛美食节（festival）。

sentences.en: The third is Shrewsbury, Shropshire.
sentences.cn: 第三个是什鲁斯伯里，什罗普郡。

sentences.en: The route from London is somewhat complicated but definitely not in vain.
sentences.cn: 从伦敦（London）出发的路线（route）有点（somewhat）复杂（complicated），但肯定（definitely）不是徒劳无功（in Vain）。

sentences.en: The River Severn has a significant turn through town, almost making an island of Shrewsbury Town Centre.
sentences.cn: 塞文河有一个显著的转弯处（turn）穿过城镇，几乎将什鲁斯伯里镇中心围成了一个岛屿。

sentences.en: The shape creates a perfect market where goods can be shipped and received using the river as a highway.
sentences.cn: 这种形状为利用这条河作为交通要道（highway）运输（ship）和接收货物创造了一个完美的市场。

sentences.en: A visit to Shrewsbury Town Centre will include narrow, twisting streets.
sentences.cn: 参观什鲁斯伯里镇中心时，会看到狭窄（narrow）而婉蜓的（twisting）街道。

sentences.en: Flowers are everywhere-hanging baskets, window boxes, and planters just what you imagine in an attractive English market town.
sentences.cn: 到处都是鲜花一一悬挂着的（hanging）花篮、窗台花箱和花盆（planter）一一这正是你想象（imagine）中一个迷人的英格兰小镇市场的样子。

sentences.en: The fourth is Mevagissey, Cornwall.
sentences.cn: 第四个是梅瓦吉西，康沃尔郡。

sentences.en: Even if you haven't been to the small fishing village Mevagissey, you've probably seen it in a movie or British television show.
sentences.cn: 即使你未曾造访过这个小小的渔村梅瓦吉西，你可能在电影或英国电视剧（television show）中见过它。

sentences.en: The operational harbour took shape in 1774.
sentences.cn: 这座运转的（operational）海港（harbour）于1774年建成。

sentences.en: Fishermen sail out daily and sell their fish in harbour-side markets.
sentences.cn: 渔民们（fisherman）每天出海（sail out）捕鱼，并在码头边的市场售卖（sell）他们的鱼。

sentences.en: One of the most moving experiences is attending a concert of the Mevagissey Male Choir.
sentences.cn: 最令人感动的（moving）经历（experience）之一是参加梅瓦吉西男声合唱团（choir）的音乐会（concert）。

sentences.en: The choir is made up of male singers, performing classical music.
sentences.cn: 这个合唱团由男性歌手（singer）组成，演奏古典音乐（music）。

sentences.en: Don't leave the harbour without a traditional Cornish pie, which tastes delicious.
sentences.cn: 离开海港时别忘了传统的康沃尔馅饼（pie），尝起来（taste）十分美味。

sentences.en: The last one is Padstow, Cornwall.
sentences.cn: 最后一个是帕德斯托，康沃尔郡。

sentences.en: Padstow, a fishing port in Cornwall, is famous for a large quantity of seafood.
sentences.cn: 帕德斯托是位于康沃尔郡的一个渔港（port），以数量（quantity）众多的海鲜（seafood）而闻名。

sentences.en: One of the most rewarding things to do here is to taste fresh seafood, which can satisfy your taste buds.
sentences.cn: 在这里，最值得做的（rewarding）事情之一就是品尝新鲜的海鲜，这能让你大饱口福（satisfy your tastebuds）。

readings.title: The Lights of Aurora
readings.text: On the night of 2 September 1859, the dark sky over Europe and North America was unexpectedly illuminated by a light. It came from neither the sun nor the moon, and it had a strange colour. The light swept across the sky, coming and going, like clouds in a violent wind. In the US, a man in Boston was using the telegraph to converse with another man in Portland, 160 kilometres away. They both turned off the electricity for the telegraph, but their telegraph line kept running for the next two hours. The electricity was coming from the light in the sky. How was this possible? And what was the light in the sky? Known as the aurora, the phenomenon is normally land observable in the earth's extreme northern southern regions, where it is called Northern Lights and Southern Lights. But in 1859, a very large solar storm triggered abnormal activity on the sun, moving the aurora across middle latitudes. It was long thought to be a single historical occurrence, unmatched before and since. Why does the aurora happen? And why can we only see it near the earth's poles? The aurora is made by something called the “solar wind" (wind from the sun), which is invisible and untouchable. It is awind of particles constantly travelling away from the sun at about 400 kilometres a second, with most failing to reach the earth. The earth has a protective “wall" around it that wards off these particles. This wall is called the earth's magnetic field, and it pushes the particles away on either side. But the earth's magnetic field has two “windows": the magnetic north, and the magnetic south. At these places, the earth's magnetic field curves down toward the Earth. And some of the particles from the solar wind slip through these magnetic “windows. These solar particles crash into atoms within the earth's atmosphere. When this collision occurs, we see the luminous streaks or clouds of the aurora. Top spots for the Northern Lights include Alaska, Iceland, and Siberia, while the Southern Lights are viewable in southern Australia, Tasmania, and New Zealand. People travel thousands of kilometres to see the aurora, and they have no certainty of witnessing it. But whoever does see it says that it leaves an everlasting impression.
readings.translation: 在1859年9月2日的晚上，欧洲（Europe）和北美洲（America）黑暗的（dark）天空（sky）出乎意料地（unexpectedly）被光（light）照亮（illuminate）了。这道光既不（neither）是来自太阳（sun）也不是来自月亮，而且它有一种奇特的（strange）颜色。光掠过（sweep across）天空，来了又去，就像狂风（violent wind）中的云（cloud）。在美国，波士顿的一名男子正在使用电报（telegraph）与160千米（kilometre）外的波特兰的一名男子进行交谈（converse）。他们都关掉了电报的电（possible）？天空中的那道光又是什么呢？这种现象被称为“极光（aurora）”，通常（normally）在地球的极北（extreme northern）和极南地区（region）是能引发（trigger）了太阳上异常的（abnormal）活动，将极光移动（move）到了中（middle）纬度（latitude）地区。长期以来，人们一直认为这是唯一一次这样的历史（historical）事件（occurrence），在此之前和之后都是无与伦比的（unmatched）。为什么会出现极光现象？为什么我们只能在地球的两极（pole）附近（near）看见（see）它呢？极光是由一种叫做“太阳风”的东西造成的（来自太阳的风），它是看不见且无法接触的（untouchable）。这是一种由粒子（particle）组成的风，以大约（about）每秒40o千米的速度不断（constantly）远离太阳，其中大多数都无法到达（reach）地球。地球周围有一道保护的（protective）“屏障”，能抵挡（ward off）这些粒子。这道屏障被称为地球磁场（magnetic field），它将粒子推动（push）到两边（either side）。但地球的磁场有两个“窗户（window）”：磁北极和磁南极。在这些地方（place），地球的磁场沿着地球曲线移动（curve）。而一些来自太阳风的粒子会从这些磁“窗户”中悄悄溜进（slip）。这些太阳粒子会撞击（crash into）地球大气层（atmosphere）中的原子（atom）。当（when）这种碰撞（collision）发生（occur）时，我们就能看到极光那发光的（luminous）条纹（streak）或云状物。观赏北极光的最棒的（top）地点包括阿拉斯加、冰岛（Iceland）和西伯利亚，而南极光则在澳大利亚（Australia）南部、塔斯马尼亚以及新西兰可以看见（viewable）。人们会长途跋涉数千公里只为一赌极光的风采，然而他们却无法确定（certainty）一定能够看到（witness）它。但无论谁（whoever）看到它，都会说它留下了永恒的（everlasting）印象。

sentences.en: On the night of 2 September 1859, the dark sky over Europe and North America was unexpectedly illuminated by a light.
sentences.cn: 在1859年9月2日的晚上，欧洲（Europe）和北美洲（America）黑暗的（dark）天空（sky）出乎意料地（unexpectedly）被光（light）照亮（illuminate）了。

sentences.en: It came from neither the sun nor the moon, and it had a strange colour.
sentences.cn: 这道光既不（neither）是来自太阳（sun）也不是来自月亮，而且它有一种奇特的（strange）颜色。

sentences.en: The light swept across the sky, coming and going, like clouds in a violent wind.
sentences.cn: 光掠过（sweep across）天空，来了又去，就像狂风（violent wind）中的云（cloud）。

sentences.en: In the US, a man in Boston was using the telegraph to converse with another man in Portland, 160 kilometres away.
sentences.cn: 在美国，波士顿的一名男子正在使用电报（telegraph）与160千米（kilometre）外的波特兰的一名男子进行交谈（converse）。

sentences.en: They both turned off the electricity for the telegraph, but their telegraph line kept running for the next two hours. The electricity was coming from the light in the sky. How was this possible?
sentences.cn: 他们都关掉了电报的电（possible）？

sentences.en: And what was the light in the sky?
sentences.cn: 天空中的那道光又是什么呢？

sentences.en: Known as the aurora, the phenomenon is normally land observable in the earth's extreme northern southern regions, where it is called Northern Lights and Southern Lights. But in 1859, a very large solar storm triggered abnormal activity on the sun, moving the aurora across middle latitudes.
sentences.cn: 这种现象被称为“极光（aurora）”，通常（normally）在地球的极北（extreme northern）和极南地区（region）是能引发（trigger）了太阳上异常的（abnormal）活动，将极光移动（move）到了中（middle）纬度（latitude）地区。

sentences.en: It was long thought to be a single historical occurrence, unmatched before and since.
sentences.cn: 长期以来，人们一直认为这是唯一一次这样的历史（historical）事件（occurrence），在此之前和之后都是无与伦比的（unmatched）。

sentences.en: Why does the aurora happen?
sentences.cn: 为什么会出现极光现象？

sentences.en: And why can we only see it near the earth's poles?
sentences.cn: 为什么我们只能在地球的两极（pole）附近（near）看见（see）它呢？

sentences.en: The aurora is made by something called the “solar wind" (wind from the sun), which is invisible and untouchable.
sentences.cn: 极光是由一种叫做“太阳风”的东西造成的（来自太阳的风），它是看不见且无法接触的（untouchable）。

sentences.en: It is awind of particles constantly travelling away from the sun at about 400 kilometres a second, with most failing to reach the earth.
sentences.cn: 这是一种由粒子（particle）组成的风，以大约（about）每秒40o千米的速度不断（constantly）远离太阳，其中大多数都无法到达（reach）地球。

sentences.en: The earth has a protective “wall" around it that wards off these particles.
sentences.cn: 地球周围有一道保护的（protective）“屏障”，能抵挡（ward off）这些粒子。

sentences.en: This wall is called the earth's magnetic field, and it pushes the particles away on either side.
sentences.cn: 这道屏障被称为地球磁场（magnetic field），它将粒子推动（push）到两边（either side）。

sentences.en: But the earth's magnetic field has two “windows": the magnetic north, and the magnetic south.
sentences.cn: 但地球的磁场有两个“窗户（window）”：磁北极和磁南极。

sentences.en: At these places, the earth's magnetic field curves down toward the Earth.
sentences.cn: 在这些地方（place），地球的磁场沿着地球曲线移动（curve）。

sentences.en: And some of the particles from the solar wind slip through these magnetic “windows.
sentences.cn: 而一些来自太阳风的粒子会从这些磁“窗户”中悄悄溜进（slip）。

sentences.en: These solar particles crash into atoms within the earth's atmosphere.
sentences.cn: 这些太阳粒子会撞击（crash into）地球大气层（atmosphere）中的原子（atom）。

sentences.en: When this collision occurs, we see the luminous streaks or clouds of the aurora.
sentences.cn: 当（when）这种碰撞（collision）发生（occur）时，我们就能看到极光那发光的（luminous）条纹（streak）或云状物。

sentences.en: Top spots for the Northern Lights include Alaska, Iceland, and Siberia, while the Southern Lights are viewable in southern Australia, Tasmania, and New Zealand.
sentences.cn: 观赏北极光的最棒的（top）地点包括阿拉斯加、冰岛（Iceland）和西伯利亚，而南极光则在澳大利亚（Australia）南部、塔斯马尼亚以及新西兰可以看见（viewable）。

sentences.en: People travel thousands of kilometres to see the aurora, and they have no certainty of witnessing it.
sentences.cn: 人们会长途跋涉数千公里只为一赌极光的风采，然而他们却无法确定（certainty）一定能够看到（witness）它。

sentences.en: But whoever does see it says that it leaves an everlasting impression.
sentences.cn: 但无论谁（whoever）看到它，都会说它留下了永恒的（everlasting）印象。

readings.title: Old Things Are Earth's Treasures
readings.text: Today, we can buy all kinds of things easily. However, we often forget what we already possess. This leads not only to a waste of the things themselves, but also to a waste of the natural resources and energy used to produce them. March 2 is Old Stuff Day, which gives us a chance to rediscover those forgotten items and realize their real value. Olditems are far from being mere trash. They carry our memories and can still be functional. Just as good wine tastes better with time, old items can be more valuable too. At present, an increasing number of valuable people are discovering the charm of old stamps, toys, electric devices, books, and clothes. By reusing old things, we contribute to the conservation of the earth's resources, reduce waste and live a green life. There are many ways to bring old items back to life. First of all, you can give away things you no longer use to others or donate them to charity shops. Additionally, -what visiting second-hand stores is a great option seems old to someone else could become something new and practical for you! Another entertaining way is to transform old items into something new with a little imagination. This is not only enjoyable but also a wisely. way to use resources Old objects are Earth's treasures. Old Stuff Day is not just about remembering the past. It reminds us that cherishing and reusing what we already have is a waste. Let's begin by looking at the old things around us with a thankful heart. It matters to our world.
readings.translation: 如今（today），我们可以轻易地（easily）买到各种（kind）各样的东西。然而，我们常常（often）忘记（forget）自己已经拥有（possess）的物品。这不仅导致物品本身的浪费（waste），也导致用于生产它们的自然资源（resource）和能源的浪费。3月（March）2日是“旧物日（Old Stuff Day）”，它给了我们一个机会（chance）去重新发现（rediscover）那些被遗忘的物品（item）并意识到它们真正的（real）价值。旧物远非单纯的垃圾（trash）。它们承载着我们的记忆（memory），并且依然是实用的（functional）。正如好酒（wine）越陈越香，旧物也可能变得更有价值（valuable）。目前，越来越多的（an increasing number of）人正在发现旧邮票（stamp）旧玩具（toy）、旧电器（electric device）、旧书（book）和旧衣服（clothes）的魅力（charm）。通过重复使用（reuse）旧物，我们为保护（conservation）地球（earth）资源作出贡献、减少浪费以及过一种绿色生活（live agre enlife）。有很多方法可以让旧物重获新生。首先，你可以把自己不再使用的东西赠送给别人，或者捐赠（donate）给慈善（charity）商店（shop）。此外（additionally），连二手（second-hand）商店也是一个不错的选择（option）一一对别人来说似乎（seem）是旧的东西，对你来说可能变成新的且实用的（practical）！另一个有趣的（entertaining）方法是用一点想象力（imagination）把旧物品改变（transform）成新东西。这不仅是令人愉快的（enjoyable），也是一种明智地（wisely）利用资源的方式。旧物（object）是地球的宝藏。“旧物日”不仅仅（just）是为了记住（remember）过去。它提醒（remind）我们，珍爱（cherish）并重复使用我们已经拥有的物品，是一种保护地球、减少浪费的有意义的方式。让我们怀着一颗感恩的（thankful）心，开始看待（look at）我们身边的旧物吧。这对我们的世界至关重要。环境保护

readings.title: Guardians of the Coast
readings.text: Mangroves are regarded as unique types of forest that grow along coastlines. They look like tall green walls standing in the sea. Though they seem just like ordinary trees, they perform numerous vital functions for nature. First, mangroves are great “°coastal protectors"' They separate the land from the sea. This way, they can perfectly protector guard coasts from fierce winds and severe floods, keeping nearby residences and beaches safe. Their complex roots are like tiny “animal cities". Mangroves provide ideal habitats small fish swim among the roots, birds build nests on the branches, crabs hide in the muddy gaps, and shellfish cling to the roots, all living in this vibrant coastal ecosystem. What's more, mangroves are natural “water cleaners' They are capable of filtering harmful substances from seawater, making the ocean cleaner and healthier. Besides, mangroves absorb carbon dioxide to mitigate global warming. Moreover, they help hold back muddy soil along the shore, preventing coastal erosion and maintaining the stability of coastal land. In summary, mangroves are not only beautiful but also extremely valuable. So we must protect them well. But now, mangroves are endangered. People cut them down to build houses or farms. Human activities also produce lots of garbage and wastewater, which are harmful to mangroves too. Therefore, vast stretches of mangroves are shrinking gradually, and marine creatures are losing their homes. It's time for us to take action The encouraging news is that more people waking up to their importance. Not only do are volunteers plant new mangrove trees, but experts are also examining better ways to conserve them. We can help, too. For example, we should refrain from littering into the sea. After all, saving mangroves keeps nature healthy and that's good for every creature.
readings.translation: 红树林（mangrove）被视为沿海岸线（coastline）生长的独特的（unique）森林（forest）类型。它们看起来就像靠立在海里的高大的（tall）绿墙。尽管它们看似只是普通的树木（tree），但它们为大自然发挥着众多必不可少的（vital）作用。首先，红树林是出色的“海岸（coastal）保护者（protector）”。它们将陆地与海洋分隔（separate）。这样一来，它们就能完美地（perfectly）保卫（guard）海岸免受狂风（fierce winds）和特大洪水的侵袭，保障附近的住宅（residence）和海滩（beach）安全。它们复杂的根系就像小型的“动物城”。红树林提供了理想的（ideal）栖息地一小鱼在根系间游动（swim），鸟儿在树枝（branch）上筑巢，螃蟹（crab）躲在泥泞的（muddy）间隙（gap）中，贝类（shellfish）附着（cling to）在根部，它们都在这个充满活力的（vibrant）海岸生态系统（ecosystem）中繁衍生息。此外，红树林还是天然的“净水器（water cleaner）”。它们有能力（capable）从海水（seawater）中过滤（filter）有害物质（substance），使海洋（ocean）变得更洁净、更健康。不仅如此，红树林还能吸收二氧化碳（carbon dioxide），减缓全球变暖。而且，它们有助于牢牢固定住海岸（shore）边的泥泞土壤（soil），防止海岸侵蚀（erosion），维持海岸陆地的稳定性（stability）。总之，红树林不仅美丽，而且极其有价值。因此我们必须保护好（well）它们。但现在，红树林濒临灭绝（endangered）。人们砍伐它们来建造房屋或农场。人类活动还产生（produce）了大量的垃圾（garbage）和废水（wastewater），这对红树林也有害。因此，大片的（vast stretch of）红树林正在逐渐减少（shrink），海洋生物（marine creature）正在失去它们的家园。我们是时候采取行动了。环境保护振奋人心的（encouraging）消息（news）是，越来越多的人意识到了（wakeup to）它们的重要性。不仅志愿者们（volunteer）种植新的红树林树木，专家们也在研究（examine）更好的方法保护（conserve）它们。我们也能帮忙。比如，我们应当避免（refrain）向海里乱扔（litter）垃圾。毕竞，守护红树林能让自然界保持健康，这对每一个生物都有好处。

sentences.en: Mangroves are regarded as unique types of forest that grow along coastlines.
sentences.cn: 红树林（mangrove）被视为沿海岸线（coastline）生长的独特的（unique）森林（forest）类型。

sentences.en: They look like tall green walls standing in the sea.
sentences.cn: 它们看起来就像靠立在海里的高大的（tall）绿墙。

sentences.en: Though they seem just like ordinary trees, they perform numerous vital functions for nature.
sentences.cn: 尽管它们看似只是普通的树木（tree），但它们为大自然发挥着众多必不可少的（vital）作用。

sentences.en: First, mangroves are great “°coastal protectors"' They separate the land from the sea.
sentences.cn: 首先，红树林是出色的“海岸（coastal）保护者（protector）”。它们将陆地与海洋分隔（separate）。

sentences.en: This way, they can perfectly protector guard coasts from fierce winds and severe floods, keeping nearby residences and beaches safe.
sentences.cn: 这样一来，它们就能完美地（perfectly）保卫（guard）海岸免受狂风（fierce winds）和特大洪水的侵袭，保障附近的住宅（residence）和海滩（beach）安全。

sentences.en: Their complex roots are like tiny “animal cities".
sentences.cn: 它们复杂的根系就像小型的“动物城”。

sentences.en: Mangroves provide ideal habitats small fish swim among the roots, birds build nests on the branches, crabs hide in the muddy gaps, and shellfish cling to the roots, all living in this vibrant coastal ecosystem.
sentences.cn: 红树林提供了理想的（ideal）栖息地一小鱼在根系间游动（swim），鸟儿在树枝（branch）上筑巢，螃蟹（crab）躲在泥泞的（muddy）间隙（gap）中，贝类（shellfish）附着（cling to）在根部，它们都在这个充满活力的（vibrant）海岸生态系统（ecosystem）中繁衍生息。

sentences.en: What's more, mangroves are natural “water cleaners' They are capable of filtering harmful substances from seawater, making the ocean cleaner and healthier.
sentences.cn: 此外，红树林还是天然的“净水器（water cleaner）”。它们有能力（capable）从海水（seawater）中过滤（filter）有害物质（substance），使海洋（ocean）变得更洁净、更健康。

sentences.en: Besides, mangroves absorb carbon dioxide to mitigate global warming.
sentences.cn: 不仅如此，红树林还能吸收二氧化碳（carbon dioxide），减缓全球变暖。

sentences.en: Moreover, they help hold back muddy soil along the shore, preventing coastal erosion and maintaining the stability of coastal land.
sentences.cn: 而且，它们有助于牢牢固定住海岸（shore）边的泥泞土壤（soil），防止海岸侵蚀（erosion），维持海岸陆地的稳定性（stability）。

sentences.en: In summary, mangroves are not only beautiful but also extremely valuable.
sentences.cn: 总之，红树林不仅美丽，而且极其有价值。

sentences.en: So we must protect them well.
sentences.cn: 因此我们必须保护好（well）它们。

sentences.en: But now, mangroves are endangered.
sentences.cn: 但现在，红树林濒临灭绝（endangered）。

sentences.en: People cut them down to build houses or farms.
sentences.cn: 人们砍伐它们来建造房屋或农场。

sentences.en: Human activities also produce lots of garbage and wastewater, which are harmful to mangroves too.
sentences.cn: 人类活动还产生（produce）了大量的垃圾（garbage）和废水（wastewater），这对红树林也有害。

sentences.en: Therefore, vast stretches of mangroves are shrinking gradually, and marine creatures are losing their homes.
sentences.cn: 因此，大片的（vast stretch of）红树林正在逐渐减少（shrink），海洋生物（marine creature）正在失去它们的家园。

sentences.en: It's time for us to take action The encouraging news is that more people waking up to their importance.
sentences.cn: 我们是时候采取行动了。环境保护振奋人心的（encouraging）消息（news）是，越来越多的人意识到了（wakeup to）它们的重要性。

sentences.en: Not only do are volunteers plant new mangrove trees, but experts are also examining better ways to conserve them.
sentences.cn: 不仅志愿者们（volunteer）种植新的红树林树木，专家们也在研究（examine）更好的方法保护（conserve）它们。

sentences.en: We can help, too.
sentences.cn: 我们也能帮忙。

sentences.en: For example, we should refrain from littering into the sea.
sentences.cn: 比如，我们应当避免（refrain）向海里乱扔（litter）垃圾。

sentences.en: After all, saving mangroves keeps nature healthy and that's good for every creature.
sentences.cn: 毕竞，守护红树林能让自然界保持健康，这对每一个生物都有好处。

readings.title: Wetlandsthe Kidneys of the Earth
readings.text: Do you know that February 2nd is a special day for our planet? It is World Wetlands Day. Its purpose is to raise people's awareness of the core importance of wetlands to our planet. What is a wetland exactly? It refers to a tract of land that is covered by water most of the time. How do wetlands form? They form when water accumulates and can't flow away. This water can come from rainfall, lakes, rivers or the sea. There are many kinds of wetlands around the world. Some are as large as parks, while others are as small as garden pools. But no matter what their sizes are, wetlands need our protection. Why are wetlands important? Firstly, wetlands are home to forty percent of the world's plants and animals. They are not only important for wildlife, but also helpful in slowing down climate change and protecting surrounding areas from bad weather, thus earning themselves the reputation as the Earth's guardians. Furthermore, more than one billion people all over the world depend on wetlands to make a living. Wetland-related industries and tourism provide jobs. Unfortunately, wetlands are facing big threats. Since 1970, more than one third of the world's wetlands have vanished. Moreover, many people use wetlands for residential and industrial construction, which makes wetlands smaller. Also, plants and animals from somewhere else grow quickly and very crowd out the native species, which harms the local environment. How can we protect wetlands? Fortunately, many countries have collaborated to make some laws and regulations on protecting wetlands. In 197l, of countries signed an agreement called the group Convention on Wetlands, which proposed effective methods to conserve wetlands and use them correctly. Wetlands are so valuable. Remember that protecting wetlands is equivalent to protecting ourselves.
readings.translation: 你知道2月2日对我们地球来说是一个特殊的日子吗？它是世界湿地（wetland）日。其主要（core）目的（purpose）是提高人们对于湿地对地球重要性（importance）的意识（awareness）。湿地到底是什么？它指的是那种大部分（most）时间都被水覆盖的大片土地（tract）。湿地是如何形成（form）的呢？它们是在水积聚（accumulate）起来且无法流走（flow away）时形成的。这些水可能来自（come form）降雨（rainfall）、湖泊、河流或者海洋（sea）。世界上有许多（many）类型的湿地。有些像公园（park）那么大，而有些则像花园的水池（pool）那么小。但无论面积大小（size），湿地都需要我们的保护（protection）。为什么湿地很重要？首先，湿地是世界上百分之（percent）四十（forty）的植物（plant）和动物的家园（home）。它们不仅对野生生物很重要，而且有助于减缓气候变化（climate change），并保护周围的（surrounding）地区免受坏（bad）天气（weather）的影响，从而赢得了地球的保护者（guardian）的声誉（reputation）。此外（furthermore），全世界有超过十亿人依靠湿地谋生。与湿地相关的工业和旅游业（tourism）提供了工作（job）机会。不幸的是（unfortunately），湿地正面临着大的（big）威胁（threat）。自1970年以来，全球超过三分之一的湿地已经消失（vanish）。此外，许多人将湿地用于住宅（residential）和工业建设（construction），这使得湿地变得更小。而且，外来的（from somewhere else）的植物和动物生长得非常（very）迅速（quickly），还挤占了当地的（native）物种（的生存空间），这破坏了当地的自然环境（environment）。环境保护我们该如何保护湿地呢？幸好（fortunately），许多国家已经合作（collaborate）制定了一些保护湿地的法律（law）和法规（regulation）。1971年，一批（a group of）国家签署了一项名为《湿地公约（convention）》的协议（agreement），该协议提议（propose）了保护（conserve）湿地和正确（correctly）利用湿地的有效方法。湿地很宝责。请记住，保护湿地就等同于（is equivalent to）保护我们自己。

sentences.en: Do you know that February 2nd is a special day for our planet?
sentences.cn: 你知道2月2日对我们地球来说是一个特殊的日子吗？

sentences.en: It is World Wetlands Day.
sentences.cn: 它是世界湿地（wetland）日。

sentences.en: Its purpose is to raise people's awareness of the core importance of wetlands to our planet.
sentences.cn: 其主要（core）目的（purpose）是提高人们对于湿地对地球重要性（importance）的意识（awareness）。

sentences.en: What is a wetland exactly?
sentences.cn: 湿地到底是什么？

sentences.en: It refers to a tract of land that is covered by water most of the time.
sentences.cn: 它指的是那种大部分（most）时间都被水覆盖的大片土地（tract）。

sentences.en: How do wetlands form?
sentences.cn: 湿地是如何形成（form）的呢？

sentences.en: They form when water accumulates and can't flow away.
sentences.cn: 它们是在水积聚（accumulate）起来且无法流走（flow away）时形成的。

sentences.en: This water can come from rainfall, lakes, rivers or the sea.
sentences.cn: 这些水可能来自（come form）降雨（rainfall）、湖泊、河流或者海洋（sea）。

sentences.en: There are many kinds of wetlands around the world.
sentences.cn: 世界上有许多（many）类型的湿地。

sentences.en: Some are as large as parks, while others are as small as garden pools.
sentences.cn: 有些像公园（park）那么大，而有些则像花园的水池（pool）那么小。

sentences.en: But no matter what their sizes are, wetlands need our protection.
sentences.cn: 但无论面积大小（size），湿地都需要我们的保护（protection）。

sentences.en: Why are wetlands important?
sentences.cn: 为什么湿地很重要？

sentences.en: Firstly, wetlands are home to forty percent of the world's plants and animals.
sentences.cn: 首先，湿地是世界上百分之（percent）四十（forty）的植物（plant）和动物的家园（home）。

sentences.en: They are not only important for wildlife, but also helpful in slowing down climate change and protecting surrounding areas from bad weather, thus earning themselves the reputation as the Earth's guardians.
sentences.cn: 它们不仅对野生生物很重要，而且有助于减缓气候变化（climate change），并保护周围的（surrounding）地区免受坏（bad）天气（weather）的影响，从而赢得了地球的保护者（guardian）的声誉（reputation）。

sentences.en: Furthermore, more than one billion people all over the world depend on wetlands to make a living.
sentences.cn: 此外（furthermore），全世界有超过十亿人依靠湿地谋生。

sentences.en: Wetland-related industries and tourism provide jobs.
sentences.cn: 与湿地相关的工业和旅游业（tourism）提供了工作（job）机会。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, wetlands are facing big threats.
sentences.cn: 不幸的是（unfortunately），湿地正面临着大的（big）威胁（threat）。

sentences.en: Since 1970, more than one third of the world's wetlands have vanished.
sentences.cn: 自1970年以来，全球超过三分之一的湿地已经消失（vanish）。

sentences.en: Moreover, many people use wetlands for residential and industrial construction, which makes wetlands smaller.
sentences.cn: 此外，许多人将湿地用于住宅（residential）和工业建设（construction），这使得湿地变得更小。

sentences.en: Also, plants and animals from somewhere else grow quickly and very crowd out the native species, which harms the local environment.
sentences.cn: 而且，外来的（from somewhere else）的植物和动物生长得非常（very）迅速（quickly），还挤占了当地的（native）物种（的生存空间），这破坏了当地的自然环境（environment）。

sentences.en: How can we protect wetlands?
sentences.cn: 环境保护我们该如何保护湿地呢？

sentences.en: Fortunately, many countries have collaborated to make some laws and regulations on protecting wetlands.
sentences.cn: 幸好（fortunately），许多国家已经合作（collaborate）制定了一些保护湿地的法律（law）和法规（regulation）。

sentences.en: In 197l, of countries signed an agreement called the group Convention on Wetlands, which proposed effective methods to conserve wetlands and use them correctly.
sentences.cn: 1971年，一批（a group of）国家签署了一项名为《湿地公约（convention）》的协议（agreement），该协议提议（propose）了保护（conserve）湿地和正确（correctly）利用湿地的有效方法。

sentences.en: Wetlands are so valuable.
sentences.cn: 湿地很宝责。

sentences.en: Remember that protecting wetlands is equivalent to protecting ourselves.
sentences.cn: 请记住，保护湿地就等同于（is equivalent to）保护我们自己。

readings.title: Save the Poles, Cool the Earth
readings.text: According to data published by the China Meteorological Administration's National Climate Center, global average temperatures rose rapidly again in 2025. The three-year period from 2023 to 2025 is the hottest on record. This clear fact shows that global warming is continuing to accelerate. Can you believe it? The Arctic and Antarctic, which are known as the two coldest areas on our planet, are undergoing an alarmingly rapid loss of ice, which means that this is no longer a distant warning to human beings. Scientists have made a shocking discovery the polar regions are getting hotter faster than ever before. The Arctic's average temperature is 1.17 degrees above normal, while the Antarctic's is 0.43 degrees higher than usual. Besides, satellite images show that glaciers in the polar regions are melting much faster than before. The rising temperature is a big red flag Why does this happen? The main reason lies in human activities. We burn a large amount of coal and oil for energy, releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. These gases hold heat like a thick blanket around the Earth, making it warmer and warmer. Every small choice we make, such as leaving the lights on or using plastic bags, adds up to this serious environmental problem. What consequences will the loss of glaciers bring? First, polar animals are facing great difficulties. For example, polar bears depend on ice to hunt seals. Without enough ice, they may starve to death. Penguins are also in danger because their breeding grounds on the ice are disappearing. Meanwhile, glacial melting will cause sea levels to rise, which may affect coastal areas and people's homes. As a result, humans are facing a survival crisis. What can we do? We can save electricity and plant more trees to absorb harmful gases. Small actions can make a big difference. The future of the polar regions is the future of humans!
readings.translation: 根据中国气象局国家气候中心发布（publish）的数据，2025年全球（global）平均（average）气温（temperature）再次快速上升（rise）。2023年至2025年是有记录以来（on record）最热的三年。这一明确的事实表明全球变暖（global Warming）仍在持续加速（accelerate）。你能相信吗？北极和南极作为地球上两个最冷的地区，那里的冰层（ice）正在经历（undergo）惊人地（alarmingly）快速消融，这意味着这已不再是对人类（human beings）遥远的（distant）警告（warning）。科学家们有了一项令人震惊的（shocking）发现（discovery）一—极地（polar）地区（region）的温度上升速度比以往任何时候都要快。北极地区的平均温度高于（above）常态（normal）1.17摄氏度，而南极地区的温度则比平常的（usual）高出0.43摄氏度。此外，卫星（satellite）图像显示，极地地区的冰川（glacier）融化（melt）速度比以前快得多。气温的上升是一个危险信号（big red flag）。为什么会发生这种情况呢？主要原因在于（liein）人类的活动（activity）。我们燃烧（burn）大量煤（coal）和石油（oil）来获取能源，释放（release）温室气体（gas）到大气层（atmosphere）中。这些气体储存着热量（heat），像厚厚的毯子（blanket）一样包裹着地球，使得地球变得越来越暖。我们所做的每一个微小的选择，比如忘记关灯或者使用塑料袋（plastic bag），都会促成（add up to）这个严重的（serious）环境问题。冰川的消失将会带来什么样的后果（consequence）呢？首先，极地动物们正面临巨大的困难。例如，北极熊依靠（depend on）冰层来猎食（hunt）海豹。没有足够的冰层，它们可能会饿（starve）死。企鹅（penguin）也处于危险之中，因为它们在冰面上的繁殖地（breeding ground）正在消失（disappear）。同时（meanwhile），冰川融化会导致海平面上升，这可能会环境保护影响沿海（coastal）地区和人们的家园。因此，人类也正面临着生存（survival）危机（crisis）。我们能做些什么呢？我们可以节约用电（electricity），并且种植更多的树木来吸收（absorb）有害气体。小小的行动（action）也能产生巨大影响。极地地区的未来就是人类的未来！

sentences.en: According to data published by the China Meteorological Administration's National Climate Center, global average temperatures rose rapidly again in 2025.
sentences.cn: 根据中国气象局国家气候中心发布（publish）的数据，2025年全球（global）平均（average）气温（temperature）再次快速上升（rise）。

sentences.en: The three-year period from 2023 to 2025 is the hottest on record.
sentences.cn: 2023年至2025年是有记录以来（on record）最热的三年。

sentences.en: This clear fact shows that global warming is continuing to accelerate.
sentences.cn: 这一明确的事实表明全球变暖（global Warming）仍在持续加速（accelerate）。

sentences.en: Can you believe it?
sentences.cn: 你能相信吗？

sentences.en: The Arctic and Antarctic, which are known as the two coldest areas on our planet, are undergoing an alarmingly rapid loss of ice, which means that this is no longer a distant warning to human beings.
sentences.cn: 北极和南极作为地球上两个最冷的地区，那里的冰层（ice）正在经历（undergo）惊人地（alarmingly）快速消融，这意味着这已不再是对人类（human beings）遥远的（distant）警告（warning）。

sentences.en: Scientists have made a shocking discovery the polar regions are getting hotter faster than ever before.
sentences.cn: 科学家们有了一项令人震惊的（shocking）发现（discovery）一—极地（polar）地区（region）的温度上升速度比以往任何时候都要快。

sentences.en: The Arctic's average temperature is 1. 17 degrees above normal, while the Antarctic's is 0. 43 degrees higher than usual.
sentences.cn: 北极地区的平均温度高于（above）常态（normal）1.17摄氏度，而南极地区的温度则比平常的（usual）高出0.43摄氏度。

sentences.en: Besides, satellite images show that glaciers in the polar regions are melting much faster than before.
sentences.cn: 此外，卫星（satellite）图像显示，极地地区的冰川（glacier）融化（melt）速度比以前快得多。

sentences.en: The rising temperature is a big red flag Why does this happen?
sentences.cn: 气温的上升是一个危险信号（big red flag）。为什么会发生这种情况呢？

sentences.en: The main reason lies in human activities.
sentences.cn: 主要原因在于（liein）人类的活动（activity）。

sentences.en: We burn a large amount of coal and oil for energy, releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
sentences.cn: 我们燃烧（burn）大量煤（coal）和石油（oil）来获取能源，释放（release）温室气体（gas）到大气层（atmosphere）中。

sentences.en: These gases hold heat like a thick blanket around the Earth, making it warmer and warmer.
sentences.cn: 这些气体储存着热量（heat），像厚厚的毯子（blanket）一样包裹着地球，使得地球变得越来越暖。

sentences.en: Every small choice we make, such as leaving the lights on or using plastic bags, adds up to this serious environmental problem.
sentences.cn: 我们所做的每一个微小的选择，比如忘记关灯或者使用塑料袋（plastic bag），都会促成（add up to）这个严重的（serious）环境问题。

sentences.en: What consequences will the loss of glaciers bring?
sentences.cn: 冰川的消失将会带来什么样的后果（consequence）呢？

sentences.en: First, polar animals are facing great difficulties.
sentences.cn: 首先，极地动物们正面临巨大的困难。

sentences.en: For example, polar bears depend on ice to hunt seals.
sentences.cn: 例如，北极熊依靠（depend on）冰层来猎食（hunt）海豹。

sentences.en: Without enough ice, they may starve to death.
sentences.cn: 没有足够的冰层，它们可能会饿（starve）死。

sentences.en: Penguins are also in danger because their breeding grounds on the ice are disappearing.
sentences.cn: 企鹅（penguin）也处于危险之中，因为它们在冰面上的繁殖地（breeding ground）正在消失（disappear）。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, glacial melting will cause sea levels to rise, which may affect coastal areas and people's homes.
sentences.cn: 同时（meanwhile），冰川融化会导致海平面上升，这可能会环境保护影响沿海（coastal）地区和人们的家园。

sentences.en: As a result, humans are facing a survival crisis.
sentences.cn: 因此，人类也正面临着生存（survival）危机（crisis）。

sentences.en: What can we do?
sentences.cn: 我们能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: We can save electricity and plant more trees to absorb harmful gases.
sentences.cn: 我们可以节约用电（electricity），并且种植更多的树木来吸收（absorb）有害气体。

sentences.en: Small actions can make a big difference.
sentences.cn: 小小的行动（action）也能产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: The future of the polar regions is the future of humans!
sentences.cn: 极地地区的未来就是人类的未来！

readings.title: Water Reduces
readings.text: Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth-they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and fallen in pure Antarctic snow. They have even entered the human bodies. Now, new research suggests that a simple, cheap measure may greatly lower the level of microplastics in water from your tap-boiling and filtering it. In a study published Wednesday in Environmental Science & Technology Letters, researchers from China found that boiling tap water in a clean pot or glass for just five minutes then filtering it after it cools could get rid of a minimum of 80% of its microplastics. Crucially, this process relies on the water containing ample calcium carbonate to trap the plastics. In the study, boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate led to an almost 90 percent drop in plastics But in samples with medium calcium carbonate content, the removal rate became low. Scientists computed the removal rate and found that in samples with calcium below 60 milligrams, boiling reduced the carbonate level of plastics by just 25 percent. Furthermore, the research had its limitations as it did not take all types of plastics into account. The team focused only on three common types-polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene-and they excluded other chemicals previously found in water, such as vinyl chloride. Still, the findings display a promising path forward for reducing microplastic exposure a task that's becoming increasingly difficult. Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1, o00 times more microplastics than previously estimated. Scientists are still striving to make an evaluation of how harmful microplastics are-but what they do know has raised alarms. The new analysis implies g tap water could be a tool to limit intake. “The boiling way they verified how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice,”Caroline Gauchotte-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the evaluation, provided an explanation to New Scientist. “We should be looking into optimizing drinking water purification systems so they can remove microplastics." Future research should carry out a deeper evaluation of microplastics under various water conditions. It is a pivotal time to organize relevant groups to reach a consensus and work together to promote the restriction of plastic pollution and ensure safe drinking water for all.
readings.translation: 微塑料（microplastic）已成为全球普遍的污染来源（source）一一它们已沉降（settle）在深海里和喜马拉雅山脉之上，陷（stick）在火山（volcanic）岩石（rock）中，填满了海鸟（seabird）的胃（stomach），飘落到了纯净的（pure）南极（Antarctic）积雪中。它们甚至已经进入了人类的身体（body）。现在，新的研究显示，一种简单且便宜的（cheap）方法或许能大大地降低（lower）从水龙头（tap）里流出来的水（water）中的微塑料的含量（level）一—将水煮沸（boil）并过滤（filter）。在周三（Wednesday）发表于《环境科技快报》杂志的一项研究中，来自中国的研究人员发现，把自来水在干净的锅（pot）或玻璃杯（glass）中煮沸仅5（five）分钟，放凉后进行过滤，就能去除（get rid of）其中至少（amini mum of）80%的微塑料。至关重要的是（crucially），这一过程依赖（rely on）水中含有（contain）的足够的（ample）碳酸钙（calcium carbonate）来吸附（trap）塑料（plastic）。在研究中，将含有300毫克（milligram）碳酸钙的硬水煮沸，使水中塑料的含量几乎（almost）下降了近90%。但在碳酸钙含量中等的（medium）样本（sample）中，去除率就变低了。科学家计算（compute）出去除率后发现，在碳酸钙含量低于（below）60毫克的样本中，煮沸仅能将塑料含量降低25%。此外（furthermore），这项研究也有其局限性（limitation），因为它没有考虑到（take...into account）所有类型的塑料。研究团队只关注了三种常见的类型——聚苯乙烯、聚乙烯和聚丙烯—一而且他们排除（exclude）了先前（previously）在水中发现的其他化学物质，例如氯乙烯。尽管如此，这些发现为减少微塑料暴露（exposure）展示（display）了一条有希望的（promising）可行道路一一而这项任务正变得越来越（increasingly）困难。科学家们今年早些时候发现，即便是瓶装（bottled）水的微塑料含量也比先前估计（estimate）的要高出10到1000倍。科学家们仍在努力（strive）对微塑料的危害程度做出评估（evaluation）一但他们所了解的情况已经引起了人们的惊慌（alarm）。新的分析（analysis）表明（imply），将自来水煮沸或许可以作为一种限制（limit）摄取量（intake）的方法。“他们证明（verify）微塑料在煮沸过程中是如何被吸附的这一方式很好（nice），”苏格兰（Scotland）格拉斯哥大学的环境工程师（engineer）卡罗琳·戈肖特-林赛并未参与此次评估，她向《新科学家》杂志提供了解释（explanation）。“我们应该研环境保护究使饮用水（drinking Water）净化（purification）系统最优化（optimize），使其能够去除微塑料。”未来的研究应当对微塑料在各种水环境中的情况开展更深入的评估。这是一个关键性的（pivotal)时期，应当组织（organize）

sentences.en: Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth-they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and fallen in pure Antarctic snow.
sentences.cn: 微塑料（microplastic）已成为全球普遍的污染来源（source）一一它们已沉降（settle）在深海里和喜马拉雅山脉之上，陷（stick）在火山（volcanic）岩石（rock）中，填满了海鸟（seabird）的胃（stomach），飘落到了纯净的（pure）南极（Antarctic）积雪中。

sentences.en: They have even entered the human bodies.
sentences.cn: 它们甚至已经进入了人类的身体（body）。

sentences.en: Now, new research suggests that a simple, cheap measure may greatly lower the level of microplastics in water from your tap-boiling and filtering it.
sentences.cn: 现在，新的研究显示，一种简单且便宜的（cheap）方法或许能大大地降低（lower）从水龙头（tap）里流出来的水（water）中的微塑料的含量（level）一—将水煮沸（boil）并过滤（filter）。

sentences.en: In a study published Wednesday in Environmental Science & Technology Letters, researchers from China found that boiling tap water in a clean pot or glass for just five minutes then filtering it after it cools could get rid of a minimum of 80% of its microplastics. Crucially, this process relies on the water containing ample calcium carbonate to trap the plastics.
sentences.cn: 在周三（Wednesday）发表于《环境科技快报》杂志的一项研究中，来自中国的研究人员发现，把自来水在干净的锅（pot）或玻璃杯（glass）中煮沸仅5（five）分钟，放凉后进行过滤，就能去除（get rid of）其中至少（amini mum of）80%的微塑料。

sentences.en: In the study, boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate led to an almost 90 percent drop in plastics But in samples with medium calcium carbonate content, the removal rate became low.
sentences.cn: 至关重要的是（crucially），这一过程依赖（rely on）水中含有（contain）的足够的（ample）碳酸钙（calcium carbonate）来吸附（trap）塑料（plastic）。

sentences.en: Scientists computed the removal rate and found that in samples with calcium below 60 milligrams, boiling reduced the carbonate level of plastics by just 25 percent.
sentences.cn: 在研究中，将含有300毫克（milligram）碳酸钙的硬水煮沸，使水中塑料的含量几乎（almost）下降了近90%。但在碳酸钙含量中等的（medium）样本（sample）中，去除率就变低了。

sentences.en: Furthermore, the research had its limitations as it did not take all types of plastics into account.
sentences.cn: 科学家计算（compute）出去除率后发现，在碳酸钙含量低于（below）60毫克的样本中，煮沸仅能将塑料含量降低25%。

sentences.en: The team focused only on three common types-polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene-and they excluded other chemicals previously found in water, such as vinyl chloride.
sentences.cn: 此外（furthermore），这项研究也有其局限性（limitation），因为它没有考虑到（take...into account）所有类型的塑料。

sentences.en: Still, the findings display a promising path forward for reducing microplastic exposure a task that's becoming increasingly difficult.
sentences.cn: 研究团队只关注了三种常见的类型——聚苯乙烯、聚乙烯和聚丙烯—一而且他们排除（exclude）了先前（previously）在水中发现的其他化学物质，例如氯乙烯。

sentences.en: Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1, o00 times more microplastics than previously estimated.
sentences.cn: 尽管如此，这些发现为减少微塑料暴露（exposure）展示（display）了一条有希望的（promising）可行道路一一而这项任务正变得越来越（increasingly）困难。

sentences.en: Scientists are still striving to make an evaluation of how harmful microplastics are-but what they do know has raised alarms. The new analysis implies g tap water could be a tool to limit intake.
sentences.cn: 科学家们今年早些时候发现，即便是瓶装（bottled）水的微塑料含量也比先前估计（estimate）的要高出10到1000倍。

sentences.en: “The boiling way they verified how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice,”Caroline Gauchotte-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the evaluation, provided an explanation to New Scientist.
sentences.cn: 科学家们仍在努力（strive）对微塑料的危害程度做出评估（evaluation）一但他们所了解的情况已经引起了人们的惊慌（alarm）。新的分析（analysis）表明（imply），将自来水煮沸或许可以作为一种限制（limit）摄取量（intake）的方法。

sentences.en: “We should be looking into optimizing drinking water purification systems so they can remove microplastics." Future research should carry out a deeper evaluation of microplastics under various water conditions.
sentences.cn: “他们证明（verify）微塑料在煮沸过程中是如何被吸附的这一方式很好（nice），”苏格兰（Scotland）格拉斯哥大学的环境工程师（engineer）卡罗琳·戈肖特-林赛并未参与此次评估，她向《新科学家》杂志提供了解释（explanation）。

sentences.en: It is a pivotal time to organize relevant groups to reach a consensus and work together to promote the restriction of plastic pollution and ensure safe drinking water for all.
sentences.cn: “我们应该研环境保护究使饮用水（drinking Water）净化（purification）系统最优化（optimize），使其能够去除微塑料。”未来的研究应当对微塑料在各种水环境中的情况开展更深入的评估。

readings.title: SLEAP
readings.titleCn: SLEAP：深度学习动物姿态追踪
readings.text: AI Powers Climate-Friendly Plant Research Carbon removal plays a vital role in the fight against climate change. Researchers at the Salk Institute are taking advantage of plants' natural capacity to absorb carbon dioxide by enhancing their root systems. This optimization is designed to increase the total amount of carbon that plants can store and extend carbon storage duration so that the carbon can last longer. In order to cultivate these climate-saving plants, the scientists are using a research tool called SLEAPan AI software that tracks multiple features related to root growth. SLEAP was originally created by Salk Fellow Talmo Pereira to monitor animal movements inside laboratory settings. Now, Pereira has joined forces with plant scientist Professor Wolfgang Busch, and together they have adapted SLEAP for use with plants. A study published in the journal Plant Phenomics establishes a new procedure for using SLEAP to analyse plant root phenotypes in other words, physical characteristics such as how deep and wide the roots grow, how large and complex the root systems become, and other similar qualities. Before SLEAP became available, researchers who needed to track the physical traits of plants or animals had to rely heavily on manual labour, which significantly slowed down the entire scientific process. By contrast, SLEAP relies on computer vision (a technology enabling machines to interpret visual images) and deep learning, an AI approach that trains computers to imitate the human brain's way of thinking and operating. As a result, researchers can now process images much more quickly than before. The successful application of SLEAP to plant research has already allowed scientists to create the most extensive catalogue of plant root phenotypes to date. Furthermore, tracking these physical root system characteristics helps the research team locate the specific genes that are linked to these characteristics. It also enables them to find out whether multiple root traits are controlled by the same set enable of genes or by different genes acting independently. The knowledge lets the Salk team identify which genes are most useful for their work on designing improved plants. “Our partnership is truly proof of what makes Salk not simply borrowing ideas from different scientific fields. Instead, we are treating those fields as equal partners, which allows us to create something that is greater than the sum of its parts." -ture
readings.translation: 碳移除（removal）在与气候（climate）变化作斗争（fight against）中扮演着至关重要的（vital）角色。索尔克研究所（institute）的研究人员（researcher）正在通过改良它们的（their）根系（root system）来利用植物的天然能力（capacity）吸收二氧化碳。这一优化（optimization）旨在增加（increase）植物所能（can）储存的碳总量（amount），并延长碳的存储（storage）持续时间（duration），从而使碳能（在植物体内）持续（last）更久。为了培育（cultivate）这些（these）气候救星植物，科学家们正在使用一种名为SLEAP的研究工具一一这款人工智能软件（software）能追踪（track）根系生长相关的多种（multiple）特征（feature）。SLEAP起初（originally）由索尔克研究所研究员塔尔莫·佩雷拉开发，用于在实验室（laboratory）环境（setting）中监测动物的运动。如今，佩雷拉与植物科学家沃尔夫冈·布施教授合作，共同将SLEAP改造（adapt）用于植物研究。一项发表（publish）在《植物表型组学》刊物（jour mal）上的研究建立（establish）了一套使用SLEAP分析（analyse）植物根系表型（phenotype）的新程序（procedure）一—也就是说，分析根系生长（grow）的深度和广度、根系的庞大与复杂程度以及其他类似特征（quality）等物理学的（physical）特征（characteristic）。在SLEAP问世之前，需要追踪植物或动物物理学的特性（trait）的研究人员不得不严重依赖体力的（manual）劳动（labour），这极大地拖慢（slowdown）了整个科研进程（process）。相比之下（by contrast），SLEAP依赖于计算机（computer）视觉（vision）【一种使机器能够解读（interpret）视觉（visual）图像的技术】和深度学习，一种训练计算机模仿（imitate）人脑（brain）思维（thinking）与运作方式的人工智能方法（approach）。其结果是，研究人员现在能够比（than）以往更快地处理图像。SLEAP在植物研究中的成功应用（application），已经（already）允许（allow）科学家们创建出了迄今为止最全面的植物根系表型目录（catalogue）。此外（furthermore），追踪这些根系的物理学特性有助于研究团队定位与这些特征相关的特定（specific）基因。这也使他们能够（enable）查明（find out）：多种多样的根系特性是由相同的（same）一组基因控制（control），还是由独立（independently）发挥作用的不同基因所控制。这一知识（knowledge）让索尔克团队能够识别出哪些基因对于他们设计改良型植物的研究最为有用。“我们的合作（partnership）是索尔克的科学研究为何如此特别且有影响力（impactful）的有力证明（proof），”佩雷拉表示，“我们不仅仅是从不同科学领域借用想法。相反，我们将那些领域视为（treat...as..）平等的（equal）伙伴，这使我们能够创造出比各部分的总和（sum）更显著的成果。”

sentences.en: AI Powers Climate-Friendly Plant Research Carbon removal plays a vital role in the fight against climate change.
sentences.cn: 碳移除（removal）在与气候（climate）变化作斗争（fight against）中扮演着至关重要的（vital）角色。

sentences.en: Researchers at the Salk Institute are taking advantage of plants' natural capacity to absorb carbon dioxide by enhancing their root systems.
sentences.cn: 索尔克研究所（institute）的研究人员（researcher）正在通过改良它们的（their）根系（root system）来利用植物的天然能力（capacity）吸收二氧化碳。

sentences.en: This optimization is designed to increase the total amount of carbon that plants can store and extend carbon storage duration so that the carbon can last longer.
sentences.cn: 这一优化（optimization）旨在增加（increase）植物所能（can）储存的碳总量（amount），并延长碳的存储（storage）持续时间（duration），从而使碳能（在植物体内）持续（last）更久。

sentences.en: In order to cultivate these climate-saving plants, the scientists are using a research tool called SLEAPan AI software that tracks multiple features related to root growth.
sentences.cn: 为了培育（cultivate）这些（these）气候救星植物，科学家们正在使用一种名为SLEAP的研究工具一一这款人工智能软件（software）能追踪（track）根系生长相关的多种（multiple）特征（feature）。

sentences.en: SLEAP was originally created by Salk Fellow Talmo Pereira to monitor animal movements inside laboratory settings.
sentences.cn: SLEAP起初（originally）由索尔克研究所研究员塔尔莫·佩雷拉开发，用于在实验室（laboratory）环境（setting）中监测动物的运动。

sentences.en: Now, Pereira has joined forces with plant scientist Professor Wolfgang Busch, and together they have adapted SLEAP for use with plants.
sentences.cn: 如今，佩雷拉与植物科学家沃尔夫冈·布施教授合作，共同将SLEAP改造（adapt）用于植物研究。

sentences.en: A study published in the journal Plant Phenomics establishes a new procedure for using SLEAP to analyse plant root phenotypes in other words, physical characteristics such as how deep and wide the roots grow, how large and complex the root systems become, and other similar qualities.
sentences.cn: 一项发表（publish）在《植物表型组学》刊物（jour mal）上的研究建立（establish）了一套使用SLEAP分析（analyse）植物根系表型（phenotype）的新程序（procedure）一—也就是说，分析根系生长（grow）的深度和广度、根系的庞大与复杂程度以及其他类似特征（quality）等物理学的（physical）特征（characteristic）。

sentences.en: Before SLEAP became available, researchers who needed to track the physical traits of plants or animals had to rely heavily on manual labour, which significantly slowed down the entire scientific process.
sentences.cn: 在SLEAP问世之前，需要追踪植物或动物物理学的特性（trait）的研究人员不得不严重依赖体力的（manual）劳动（labour），这极大地拖慢（slowdown）了整个科研进程（process）。

sentences.en: By contrast, SLEAP relies on computer vision (a technology enabling machines to interpret visual images) and deep learning, an AI approach that trains computers to imitate the human brain's way of thinking and operating.
sentences.cn: 相比之下（by contrast），SLEAP依赖于计算机（computer）视觉（vision）【一种使机器能够解读（interpret）视觉（visual）图像的技术】和深度学习，一种训练计算机模仿（imitate）人脑（brain）思维（thinking）与运作方式的人工智能方法（approach）。

sentences.en: As a result, researchers can now process images much more quickly than before.
sentences.cn: 其结果是，研究人员现在能够比（than）以往更快地处理图像。

sentences.en: The successful application of SLEAP to plant research has already allowed scientists to create the most extensive catalogue of plant root phenotypes to date.
sentences.cn: SLEAP在植物研究中的成功应用（application），已经（already）允许（allow）科学家们创建出了迄今为止最全面的植物根系表型目录（catalogue）。

sentences.en: Furthermore, tracking these physical root system characteristics helps the research team locate the specific genes that are linked to these characteristics.
sentences.cn: 此外（furthermore），追踪这些根系的物理学特性有助于研究团队定位与这些特征相关的特定（specific）基因。

sentences.en: It also enables them to find out whether multiple root traits are controlled by the same set enable of genes or by different genes acting independently.
sentences.cn: 这也使他们能够（enable）查明（find out）：多种多样的根系特性是由相同的（same）一组基因控制（control），还是由独立（independently）发挥作用的不同基因所控制。

sentences.en: The knowledge lets the Salk team identify which genes are most useful for their work on designing improved plants.
sentences.cn: 这一知识（knowledge）让索尔克团队能够识别出哪些基因对于他们设计改良型植物的研究最为有用。

sentences.en: “Our partnership is truly proof of what makes Salk not simply borrowing ideas from different scientific fields.
sentences.cn: “我们的合作（partnership）是索尔克的科学研究为何如此特别且有影响力（impactful）的有力证明（proof），”佩雷拉表示，“我们不仅仅是从不同科学领域借用想法。

sentences.en: Instead, we are treating those fields as equal partners, which allows us to create something that is greater than the sum of its parts.
sentences.cn: 相反，我们将那些领域视为（treat...as..）平等的（equal）伙伴，这使我们能够创造出比各部分的总和（sum）更显著的成果。”

readings.title: Learn About Tornadoes
readings.text: column of air. Atornadoisaviolentlyrotating It can travel at over 200 miles per hour and result in great damage. When moving across the land, it can readily lift cars, lorries and other vehicles, and even houses, then throw them far away onto the ground or buildings. The wind raises dust, which easily enters your nose and mouth. So it's very important to find a hiding place when a tornado attacks. A safe place can be a basement or the lowest floor of a building. If your home has no basement, seek refuge in a first-floor bathroom or a small windowless room in the middle of the house. Once inside, you should crouch down, curl up into a ball and cover your head and neck with your hands. To learn more about tornadoes' characteristics and how they form, some scientists make a decisive move to get close to these hazardous natural phenomena. They use specialized equipment a tornado probe. It is an important instrument. It has precise sensors that can collect accurate data such as wind speed, temperature, atmospheric pressure and wind direction. Some types of it even have compact cameras to take real-time photographs of tornadoes. By evaluating the collected data, scientists forecast where a tornado will move next. Afterwards, they drive to the predicted place and put the probe in the right position. If their prediction is correct, the tornado will pass near or right over the probe, allowing it to collect data usefully. These data are used to refine predictive models for upcoming tornadoes. Besides, they can be used to make timely warning announcements and reduce the risks to people's lives and property. readings.translation: 龙卷风（tornado）是一种猛烈地（violently）旋转的（rotating）柱状（column）气流。它每小时可移动超过200英里并会导致（result in）巨大的损失（damage）。当它在陆地（land）上移动时，能够轻而易举地（readily）卷起小汽车（car）、卡车（lorry）以及其他车辆（vehicle），甚至房屋（house），然后将它们抛（throw）到远处的地面或建筑物（building）上面（onto）。狂风卷起尘土，尘土很容易进入你的鼻子（nose）和嘴巴（mouth）。因此，当遭遇龙卷风袭击（attack）时，找到一个躲避的地方是非常重要的。安全的地方可以是地下室（basement）或者建筑物的最底层。如果你的家没有地下室，那就到一楼的浴室（bathroom）或者房子中间一个无窗的（windowless）小房间里寻找避难所（refuge）。进入之后，你应该尊下（crouch down），蜷缩（curl up）成一团，并用双手护住（cover）头部和颈部（neck）。为了更深入地了解龙卷风的特征以及它们是怎样形成（form）的，一些科学家采取了果断的（decisive）行动去接近这些危险的（hazardous）自然现象。他们使用专门的（specialized）设备（equipment）一一龙卷风探测仪。这是一种重要的仪器。它配备了精确的传感器，能够收集诸如风速（wind speed）、温度（temperature）、大气压（atmospheric pressure）和风向（wind direction）等精确的（accurate）数据。有些型号的探测仪甚至还配有小型的照相机（camera），能够拍摄龙卷风实时的照片通过评估（evaluate）收集到的数据，科学家能够预测（forecast）龙卷风接下来会移动到何处。之后（afterwards），他们会开车前往（drive to）预测的地点，并将探测仪放置在正确的位置（position）。如果他们的预测（prediction）是准确的，那么龙卷风就会从探测仪附近或正上方经过（pass），从而使其能够有效地（usefully）收集数据。这些数据被用于改进（refine）对即将来临的（upcoming）龙卷风的预测（predictive）模型。此外，这些数据还可用于发布及时的（timely）预警通告（announcement），降低危及民众生命（life）和财产（property）的风险。
