readings.title: Future Dreams 未来的梦想
readings.text: On Monday, our school had a special day. Everybody could choose a future job and learn about it. “This is a great chance,” our teacher said. “Get ready and enjoy the experience.” My best friend Li Lei wanted to be a lawyer. “I like law,” he said. “I want to help people.” Another student wanted to work in a bank. “Money is not everything,” he said. “But a bank is a useful place.” I wanted to be an actor. “I love stories,” I said. “I want to play different roles on stage.” We visited a theatre. An old actor talked to us. “I have been an actor for fifteen years,” he said. “It is hard work. Sometimes the theatre is empty. Sometimes you must play the same role again and again. But I never give up.” He told us a strange story. “Once, I played a nurse in a play. I had to lock a door and hide under a chair. In the story, a snake came out of a hole! It was not a real snake, of course. But I acted so well that everybody believed it.” We laughed. “I seldom think about money,” he said. “Acting is my pleasure. Even though it is difficult, I love it.” That day, I learned a lot. “A good actor must be ready for any situation,” he said. He also gave us advice: “Turn off your phone. Catch up with your dreams. Prepare for your future every day.” I will never forget his words. “Every big dream starts with a small step,” my teacher said. “Take a little time every day, and you will improve a lot.” On my way home, I saw a banana tree. I thought of my cousin in the south. She wants to be a nurse. “We all have dreams,” I said to myself. “Let’s catch up with them!” One morning, my pen ran out of ink, and I felt a little sorry.

readings.title: The French Class 法语课
readings.text: It was Friday afternoon. The sun was high in the sky, and the classroom was warm. We sat in our seats, but nobody wanted to relax. Today we had a special French class. “Put your books on the desk,” our teacher, Mr White, said. “Today we will learn about French poetry.” He wrote a poem on the board with a piece of chalk. The poem was short but beautiful. “Listen carefully,” he said. “Poetry is like music. It is the secret language of the heart.” He read the poem slowly. His voice was soft and kind. Some words were new to us, but we could understand the feeling. “What is the poem about?” he asked. “It is about a garden,” Lily said. “There are flowers and a small basket.” “Very good!” Mr White said. “It is about spring. The beans are growing, and the fruit is sweet.” After the class, we went to the library. “You can find more French books here,” the librarian said. “We have books about history, science, and art.” I looked around and found a book of European stories. “I want to borrow this one,” I said. At the door, I met my elder sister. She was in a hurry. “I have to go to the market,” she said. “Mum wants some onions and a cucumber.” “Your trousers are nice,” I said. “Thank you!” she said. “I bought them last week.” On the way home, I thought about the French class. “Learning a language is like opening a window,” I said. “It shows you a new world.” Mr White was right: poetry is the secret language of the heart. I decided to learn French well. “Maybe one day I can visit Paris!” I said. My mother smiled. “That is a good dream,” she said. “But first, finish your homework!”
readings.translation: 星期五下午，太阳高挂，教室很暖和。我们坐在座位上，但没人想放松。今天有一节特别的法语课。“把书放在桌上。”我们的老师怀特先生说，“今天我们要学法语诗歌。”他用粉笔在黑板上写了一首诗。诗短而美。“仔细听。”他说，“诗歌就像音乐，它是心灵秘密的语言。”他慢慢朗读。他的声音温柔亲切。有些词对我们来说是新词，但我们能理解那种感受。“这首诗讲什么？”他问。“讲一个花园。”莉莉说，“里面有花和一个小篮子。”“很好！”怀特先生说，“它讲春天。豆子在生长，果子很甜。”下课后，我们去图书馆。“这里可以找到更多法语书。”图书管理员说，“我们有历史、科学和艺术的书。”我四处看看，找到一本欧洲故事书。“我想借这本。”我说。门口，我遇见姐姐，她正忙着：“我得去市场，妈妈要洋葱和黄瓜。”“你的裤子很漂亮。”我说。“谢谢！上周买的。”她说。回家路上，我想着法语课。“学语言就像打开一扇窗。”我说，“它让你看到新世界。”怀特先生说得对：诗歌是心灵秘密的语言。我决定学好法语。“也许有一天我能去巴黎！”我说。妈妈笑了：“好梦想。不过先完成作业！”

readings.title: A Day by the Sea 海边的一天
readings.text: Last September, my family went to a small town by the sea. “This is a wonderful place for a holiday,” my father said. We stayed in a little hotel near the beach. “Look at the sea!” my sister shouted. “It is so beautiful!” The water was clean and blue. We took off our shoes and ran on the sand. The sand was warm under our feet. “Let’s look for shells!” my sister said. We walked along the beach and found many pretty shells. “This one looks like a cup,” I said. “And this one looks like a small hill!” After lunch, we went to see an old lighthouse. “It was built one hundred years ago,” the guide said. “It helped ships find their way in the dark.” We climbed to the top. From there, we could see the whole town. “What a beautiful view!” my mother said. In the evening, we had fish soup in a small restaurant. “This soup is delicious!” I said. “The fish is fresh from the sea.” The restaurant owner told us about the town. “Many years ago, there was a big storm,” she said. “A ship hit the rocks. A brave engineer ran to help. He saved twenty people. The town built a statue for him.” “What a hero!” I said. “He is our treasure,” the owner said. “We will never forget him.” The next day, we visited a museum. It had old maps and pictures of the town. “Look! A picture of a bear!” my sister said. “Bears lived in the hills long ago.” I also saw a picture of an Indian elephant. “Elephants are big and strong,” the guide said. “They can carry heavy things.” On the last day, we went to a small market. “These apples are cheap!” my mother said. “Let’s buy some.” We bought apples, fish, and a little toy. “I will remember this holiday forever,” I said. “The sea, the shells, and the kind people.” My father smiled. “The best treasure is not gold,” he said. “It is the time we spend with the people we love.” Our class had a football match against another school.

readings.title: Sunday in the Kitchen 厨房里的星期日
readings.text: Every Sunday, my grandmother cooks a big dinner for the family. “Today, you are my special helper!” she said to me. “I want to teach you my secret recipes.” I was so happy. “Thank you, Granny!” I said. “What are we making?” “Corn soup and a big salad!” she said. First, we washed the vegetables. “Be careful with the knife,” Granny said. “Always cut away from your fingers.” I cut the tomatoes carefully. “You are a quick learner!” she said. Next, we cooked the corn. “This is my favourite season,” Granny said. “In autumn, everything is fresh and lovely.” While the soup was cooking, Granny told me about her childhood. “When I was young, I lived in the countryside,” she said. “Our house was small, but we had a big garden. We grew rice, vegetables, and flowers.” “Did you have a kitchen like this?” I asked. “No,” she laughed. “We cooked over a fire. There was no electricity. We had to carry water from the river.” “That sounds hard!” I said. “It was, but we were happy,” Granny said. “At night, we sat outside and watched the stars. We listened to the sounds of the forest.” She looked at me and smiled. “A few years ago, I went back to the countryside. Everything had changed. A factory now stands where our old house was. The river is not as clean as before.” She was quiet for a moment. “The world changes,” she said. “That is why we must remember the good things.” The soup was ready. It smelled wonderful. “This is the best soup I have ever had!” I said. “Wait until you taste my cookies!” Granny laughed. That day, I learned more than cooking. I learned about love, memories, and family. “Cooking is not just food,” Granny said. “It is a way to say ‘I love you’.” I hugged her. “I love you too, Granny.” It was a rainy day. The clouds were grey, and the streets were quiet.
readings.translation: 每个星期日，奶奶为全家做一顿大餐。“今天你是我的特别小帮手！”她对我说，“我要教你我的秘方。”我高兴极了：“谢谢奶奶！我们做什么？”“玉米汤和大沙拉！”她说。首先，我们洗蔬菜。“小心刀，切的时候手指离远点。”奶奶说。我小心地切西红柿。“你学得真快！”她说。接着，我们煮玉米。“这是我喜欢的季节。”奶奶说，“秋天一切都新鲜可爱。”煮汤时，奶奶给我讲她的童年：“我年轻时住在乡下。房子小，但有个大花园。我们种水稻、蔬菜和花。”“你们有这样的厨房吗？”我问。“没有。”她笑了，“我们在火上做饭。没有电，得从河里提水。”“听起来真辛苦！”我说。“辛苦，但我们很快乐。”奶奶说，“晚上我们坐在外面看星星，听森林的声音。”她看着我说：“几年前我回了一趟乡下。一切都变了。老房子那儿现在是一座工厂，河水也不如以前清了。”她沉默片刻：“世界会变，所以我们必须记住美好的东西。”汤好了，闻起来真香。“这是我喝过最好的汤！”我说。“等你尝尝我的饼干！”奶奶笑了。那天我学到的不仅是做饭，还有爱、记忆和家庭。“做饭不只是食物。”奶奶说，“它是说‘我爱你’的一种方式。”我拥抱她：“我也爱您，奶奶。”

readings.title: The Postcard 明信片
readings.text: The postcard came on a windy afternoon. It was from my uncle in London. “Dear Tom,” he wrote. “I hope you are well. I am having a great time in England. The weather is nice, and the people are friendly. I visited a big museum yesterday. There is so much to see! I also walked along the river and took many photos. My favourite place is a small park near my hotel. Every morning, I sit there and read. It is quiet and peaceful.” I read the postcard again and again. “I wish I could go to London,” I said. “Maybe one day!” my mother said. “You can see the world if you study hard.” That evening, I wrote a letter to my uncle. “Dear Uncle,” I wrote. “Thank you for the postcard. I am so happy to hear from you. I am doing well at school. Last week, I got a good mark in the English test. My teacher said my English is improving. I am also learning to play the guitar. It is hard, but I practise every day.” I put the letter in an envelope and wrote the address carefully. “I hope it reaches you soon,” I said. The next morning, my father took me to the post office. “This is the ninth letter I have sent this year,” I said. “I like writing letters,” I said. “It is better than sending a message on the phone. A letter is something you can keep.” My father nodded. “You are right,” he said. “In a world that changes so fast, a letter is a gift.” A week later, a parcel arrived. It was from my uncle! Inside, there was a book about London and a small model of the Big Ben. “For my favourite nephew,” the card said. I was so happy. “I will study hard,” I said. “One day, I will visit London and see everything with my own eyes!”

readings.title: Dumpling Day 饺子日
readings.text: It was a cold winter day. Snowflakes fell softly on the ground. “What a perfect day for dumplings!” my grandmother said. “Let’s make some together!” “Great!” I shouted. “Dumplings are my favourite!” We put on our aprons and washed our hands. “First, we make the filling,” Granny said. We cut up some meat and vegetables. “Add a little salt and some juice from the ginger,” she said. “That makes it taste better.” Then we made the wrappers. “Roll the dough into small pieces,” Granny said. I tried, but my pieces were all different sizes. “Yours look like small moons,” I laughed. “And mine look like rocks!” “That is fine,” Granny said. “The first time I made dumplings, they were terrible! But with practice, you will get better.” We filled the wrappers and closed them carefully. “Be careful not to break them,” Granny said. “Or the soup will come out.” When the water boiled, we put the dumplings in. “Now we wait,” Granny said. “When they float, they are ready.” We sat and watched the pot. “Dumplings are special,” Granny said. “They bring the family together. When we eat them, we are all one.” “Do people in other countries eat dumplings?” I asked. “Yes!” Granny said. “In Germany, they have their own dumplings. In Japan, they eat dumplings too. Food connects people all over the world.” At last, the dumplings were ready. They smelled wonderful. “Be careful, they are hot!” Granny warned. We sat around the table and ate. “Mmm! Delicious!” I said. “You are a good cook now!” Granny said. That evening, we called my cousin in London. “We are eating dumplings!” I said. “I miss you!” My cousin laughed. “I miss you too! I will come back in the spring, and we will make dumplings together!” “Great!” I said. “I will be ready!” After we finished, I helped clean the kitchen. “In the end, the best part of cooking is sharing,” Granny said. “Food tastes better when you eat it with the people you love.” I think she is right. That winter day was the warmest day of the year.

readings.title: The Chess Club 象棋俱乐部
readings.text: Every Thursday afternoon, our school holds a chess club. I joined it last year. “Why do you like chess?” my friend asked me. “Because it is like a war without guns,” I said. “You must think before you move.” Our teacher, Mr Wang, is a patient man. “Chess teaches you to be calm,” he said. “Never give up, even when you are losing.” Last month, we had a big competition. The winner would go to the city finals. “I am nervous,” I told Mr Wang. “What if I lose?” “It is not about winning,” he said. “It is about learning. Every game teaches you something new.” On the day of the competition, the hall was full of students. I sat at a small table and looked at my opponent. “Good luck,” he said. “Good luck to you too,” I said. We began to play. The first game was difficult. I made a mistake and lost a piece. “Stay calm,” I told myself. “Think slowly.” I took a deep breath and looked at the board again. Then I saw it! There was a way to win. I moved my piece and said, “Check!” My opponent looked surprised. He thought for a long time, but there was no way out. “I win!” I said. “Good game,” he said. “You played very well.” I won two more games. At last, I was the winner of our school! “You did it!” my friends cheered. I smiled. “I could not do it without your help,” I said. Mr Wang patted me on the shoulder. “I am proud of you,” he said. “You stayed calm and used your brain. That is the true spirit of chess.” That night, I told my parents the good news. “I am going to the city finals!” I said. “Wonderful!” my mother said. “We are so proud of you!” “Remember,” my father said, “win or lose, we love you.” I nodded. “I know,” I said. “And I will try my best.”

readings.title: Strict Grandma 严格的奶奶
readings.text: My grandmother is strict, but she loves us very much. “Rules are important,” she often says. “They keep us safe.” Every morning, she wakes us up early. “Get up! The sun is already up!” she shouts. “We must not waste the day.” She has many rules. We must make our beds. We must finish our homework before dinner. We must not throw rubbish on the floor. “A clean house is a happy house,” she says. One day, my little brother broke a cup. “It was an accident!” he cried. “It is all right,” Grandma said. “Accidents happen. The important thing is to learn from them.” She gave him a small broom. “Now, sweep the floor,” she said. “That is how we take responsibility.” My grandmother also teaches us good manners. “When you meet someone, say ‘hello’ politely,” she says. “Do not interrupt when others are speaking.” “Why do we need so many rules?” I once asked. She smiled. “Because rules are like the rails of a railway,” she said. “They show you the way. Without them, the train cannot run safely.” Last week, I had an important exam. I was very nervous. “Do not worry,” Grandma said. “You have studied hard. You are ready.” She made me a cup of tea and said, “Drink this. It will calm your nerves.” I took the exam and did very well. “Thank you, Grandma!” I said. “Your words helped me a lot.” She smiled. “I knew you could do it,” she said. “You are stronger than you think.” I am lucky to have such a grandmother. She is strict, but her strictness comes from love. “One day, you will thank me,” she often says. I think she is right. Thanks to her rules, I am becoming a better person every day. “Discipline is a gift,” she says. “It helps you grow.”

readings.title: The Zoo Trip 动物园之行
readings.text: On Saturday, our class went to the zoo. “This is going to be a great day!” my friend said. “I can’t wait to see the animals!” We got on the bus early in the morning. The bus was full of excited children. “Sit down, please!” our teacher said. “We will be there soon.” When we arrived, the first thing we saw was a big gate. “Welcome to the zoo!” the sign said. We walked in and saw many animals. First, we visited the monkeys. “Look! The monkeys are playing!” a girl shouted. “They are so funny!” The monkeys jumped from tree to tree. One small monkey made a face at us. We all laughed. Next, we saw the tigers. “Tigers are strong and beautiful,” the guide said. “But they are in danger. We must protect them.” “Why are they in danger?” I asked. “Because people cut down forests,” the guide said. “And some people hunt them for their fur.” I felt sad. “That is terrible,” I said. “We must help them.” We also saw giraffes. “Look at their long necks!” my friend said. “They can eat leaves from tall trees.” The giraffes were eating quietly. “They are so gentle,” I said. At noon, we had lunch in the park. “I brought a hamburger and some salad,” my friend said. “My mother made it for me.” “Mine is rice and some fruit,” I said. We shared our food and talked about the animals. “What is your favourite animal?” I asked. “The panda!” my friend said. “It is so cute!” After lunch, we watched a dolphin show. The dolphins jumped high and played with the trainers. “They are so smart!” everyone said. “Dolphins can learn many things,” the trainer said. “They are one of the most intelligent animals.” At the end of the day, our teacher asked, “What did you learn today?” “Animals are our friends!” we said. “We must take care of them and their homes.” The teacher smiled. “I am proud of you,” she said. “Now, let’s go home and share what we learned with our families.” We got on the bus, tired but happy. “This was the best day!” I said. “I will never forget it.” My teacher, Miss Li, is very kind.
readings.translation: 星期六，我们班去动物园。“这将是美好的一天！”朋友说，“我等不及看动物了！”清晨我们上了大巴。车上满是兴奋的孩子。“请坐下！”老师说，“很快就到。”到达时，我们首先看到一扇大门。“欢迎来到动物园！”牌子上写着。我们走进去，看到许多动物。首先看猴子。“看！猴子在玩！”一个女孩喊道，“太有趣了！”猴子在树间跳来跳去。一只小猴子对我们做鬼脸，我们都笑了。接着看老虎。“老虎又壮又美。”导游说，“但它们处于危险中，我们必须保护它们。”“为什么危险？”我问。“因为人们砍伐森林，还有人为了皮毛猎杀它们。”导游说。我很难过：“太可怕了，我们必须帮助它们。”我们还看了长颈鹿。“看它们的长脖子！”朋友说，“它们能吃高树上的叶子。”长颈鹿安静地吃着。“它们真温和。”我说。中午我们在园里吃午饭。“我带了汉堡和沙拉，妈妈给我做的。”朋友说。“我带的是米饭和水果。”我说。我们分享食物，聊动物。“你最喜欢什么动物？”我问。“熊猫！太可爱了！”朋友说。午饭后，我们看海豚表演。海豚跳得高高的，和训练员玩耍。“它们真聪明！”大家说。“海豚能学很多东西，是最聪明的动物之一。”训练员说。一天结束时，老师问：“今天学到了什么？”“动物是我们的朋友，要爱护它们和它们的家园！”我们说。老师笑了：“我为你们骄傲。现在回家，把学到的分享给家人吧。”我们上了车，累但快乐。“这是最棒的一天！”我说，“我永远不会忘记。”

readings.title: The Dirty River 变脏的河
readings.text: There is a river near our town. Long ago, it was clean and beautiful. People swam in it in summer and fished in it in spring. “The river was our friend,” my grandfather said. “It gave us water and food.” But now, the river is dirty. “What happened?” I asked my teacher. “A factory opened near the river,” she said. “It puts waste water into the river every day. The waste water has harmful things in it. That is why the water is dirty and the fish are dying.” I felt very sad. “Can we do something?” I asked. “Yes!” my teacher said. “We can help. Let’s start a project to clean the river.” Our class made a plan. First, we wrote letters to the factory. “Please stop polluting the river,” we wrote. “The river is our home too.” Then, we cleaned the riverbank. We wore gloves and picked up rubbish. “Look at all this plastic!” my friend said. “People threw it into the river. That is so bad.” We also planted trees along the river. “Trees help keep the water clean,” our teacher said. “Their roots hold the soil.” We told our families and friends about the river. “Do not throw rubbish into the water,” we said. “Do not waste water.” My parents were proud of us. “You are doing a great thing,” they said. “Protecting the environment is protecting our future.” After two months, the river looked better. The water was cleaner, and we saw some small fish again. “Look! A fish!” I shouted. “The river is coming back to life!” Everyone cheered. “But we must keep working,” my teacher said. “It takes time for the river to become clean again. We must not give up.” I learned an important lesson that year. “We should never pollute our rivers,” I told my little sister. “Clean water is a gift.” She nodded. “I will help too,” she said. Now, our class still takes care of the river. We visit it every month and keep it clean. “Small actions can make a big difference,” my teacher says. She is right. Our little project is making our town a better place.

readings.title: The Guitar Contest 吉他比赛
readings.text: At the age of twelve, I fell in love with music. “I want to learn the guitar!” I told my mother. “Are you sure?” she asked. “You must practise every day. It is not easy.” “I am sure!” I said. My mother bought me a blue guitar. It was not expensive, but it was beautiful. “This is my treasure,” I said. I practised every day after school. At first, my fingers hurt. The strings were hard, and my hands were weak. “I will never learn this,” I said sadly. “Do not give up,” my mother said. “Everything is difficult at first. With time, you will improve.” I kept practising. After a few months, I could play simple songs. “Listen! I can play!” I shouted. My mother smiled. “You see? Hard work pays off.” One day, my teacher told me about a guitar contest. “There is a music contest next month,” she said. “Why don’t you enter?” “Me?” I said. “I am not good enough!” “You are better than you think,” she said. “Believe in yourself.” I decided to try. I practised for hours every day. I played in my room until my fingers were sore. “Take a break,” my mother said. “Rest is also important.” On the day of the contest, the hall was full of people. My heart beat fast. “What if I make a mistake?” I thought. I looked at my mother in the crowd. She smiled and nodded. I took a deep breath and began to play. The music filled the room. I forgot about the crowd and played with my heart. When I finished, everyone clapped. “Well done!” people shouted. I did not win the first prize, but I was happy. “I am proud of you,” my mother said. “You were brave.” “I learned something today,” I said. “It is not about winning. It is about trying your best.” My teacher was proud too. “Next year, you will do even better,” she said. I smiled. “I will keep practising,” I said. “Music is my dream.”

wordExamples: Last month, our class went to a science museum.
“This is going to be a great trip!” my friend said.
We saw many amazing things.
“Look at this old clock!” I said.
“It is three hundred years old!”
We also learned about the history of printing.
“People used to print books by hand,” the guide said.
“It was very slow.”
“How did they print pictures?” I asked.
“They used wood and ink,” the guide said.
“It was a common method long ago.” I thought about the guide’s words.
“Printing changed the world,” I said.
“Without it, we could not have books or newspapers.”
My friend nodded.
“That is true,” he said.
“We should be thankful for all the inventions that make our life easier.”

readings.title: Winter Video Call 冬日视频通话
readings.text: A month ago, my cousin moved to the north with his family. “I will miss you,” he said when we said goodbye. “But we can video call every week!” I said. “Promise?” he asked. “I promise!” I said. Last Saturday, we had our first video call. “Hello! Can you hear me?” he shouted. “Yes!” I laughed. “You look different. Did you cut your hair?” “Yes! I got a new haircut,” he said. He showed me his new room. “It is small, but I like it,” he said. “Look! I have a pet fish!” “Cute!” I said. “What is your school like?” “It is good,” he said. “The teachers are kind. We learn English, maths, and science. My favourite lesson is grammar. It is like solving puzzles.” “Grammar? Really?” I said. “Most people think it is boring!” “Well, I think it is interesting,” he said. “It helps me understand how language works.” He told me about the winter there. “It snows a lot,” he said. “Last week, we had a big snowstorm. The school was closed for two days!” “Lucky you!” I said. “We played in the snow and made a snowman. We also went skating on the lake.” “That sounds like fun!” I said. “What do you eat in winter?” “Hot pot and dumplings!” he said. “And my mother makes the best hot soup. It keeps us warm.” I smiled. “I miss your dumplings,” I said. “Next year, you must come back and visit.” “I will!” he said. “Maybe in the summer, when the weather is warm.” We talked for an hour. “I have to go now,” he said at last. “It is late, and I have homework.” “OK!” I said. “Let’s call again next week!” “Sure!” he said. “Take care!” “You too!” After the call, I felt happy. “Even though he is far away, we are still close,” I thought. “Thanks to technology, we can stay connected.” My mother smiled. “Friendship is a treasure,” she said. “No matter how far apart you are, keep in touch.” I nodded. “I will,” I said.

readings.title: The Swimming Club 游泳俱乐部
readings.text: Last summer, I joined the school swimming club. “Why do you want to learn swimming?” the coach asked me. “Because I want to be strong and healthy,” I said. “And I want to swim in the sea one day.” “Good!” he said. “Let’s begin.” The first lesson was difficult. I was afraid of the water. “Do not be afraid,” the coach said. “The water is your friend. Relax your body and trust it.” I held the side of the pool and kicked my legs. “Good!” the coach said. “Now, try to float.” At first, I sank. “I can’t do it!” I said. “Yes, you can!” the coach said. “Everyone can learn. Take your time.” I practised every day. After two weeks, I could swim a little. “Look! I am swimming!” I shouted. “Well done!” my friends cheered. My friend Li Hua was also in the club. “How are you doing?” I asked her. “I am getting better,” she said. “But I still need to practise my breathing.” “Me too,” I said. “Let’s practise together after school.” “Great idea!” she said. We practised together every day. “You are improving so fast,” the coach said. “I am proud of you.” In July, the club held a swimming competition. “Do you want to enter?” the coach asked me. “I am not sure,” I said. “What if I lose?” “It does not matter,” he said. “What matters is that you try.” I decided to enter. On the day of the competition, I was nervous. “Take a deep breath,” Li Hua said. “You can do it!” I stood at the edge of the pool and waited for the signal. When the whistle blew, I jumped into the water. I swam as fast as I could. “Come on! Come on!” my friends shouted. I touched the wall and looked up. I was the third! “I did it!” I shouted. “You were amazing!” Li Hua said. That day, I learned an important lesson. “If you believe in yourself, you can do anything,” the coach said. I smiled. “Next year, I want to be the first!” I said.

wordExamples: My mother is a nurse.
She works very hard.
“I help sick people get better,” she says.
“That is my job and my joy.”
One day, I asked her, “Is it difficult to be a nurse?” She smiled.
“Sometimes,” she said.
“But I love it. When a patient smiles at me, I feel happy.” I thought about her words.
“You are a hero,” I said.
“You save people’s lives.” She laughed.
“I am just an ordinary person,” she said.
“But I try my best every day.”

That evening, I wrote in my diary: “My mother is the best nurse in the world. She is kind, patient, and brave. I want to be like her when I grow up. I want to help others and make the world a better place.”

readings.title: The Birthday Surprise 生日惊喜
readings.text: Last Saturday was my mother’s birthday. “What should we do?” my father asked me. “Let’s give her a surprise!” I said. “A big one!” “Great idea!” my father said. We made a plan. First, we cleaned the house and put up balloons. Then, we bought a big cake and some flowers. “We need candles too,” I said. “How old is she?” “Forty,” my father said. “But let’s not put forty candles on the cake!” We laughed. “Let’s use a special candle instead,” I said. In the afternoon, my mother went out to visit my grandmother. “Perfect!” I said. “Now we can get everything ready.” We put the cake on the table and turned off the lights. “Be quiet!” my father said. “She is coming!” The door opened. My mother walked in. “Surprise!” we shouted. She was so surprised. “What is this?” she said. “Happy birthday!” we sang. Her eyes were full of tears. “Thank you, my dear family!” she said. “You are the best gift in the world.” She blew out the candles and made a wish. “What did you wish for?” I asked. “If I tell you, it won’t come true!” she laughed. We ate the cake and talked. “This is the best birthday I have ever had,” she said. “It is not about the presents. It is about being together.” “Mum,” I said, “thank you for everything you do for us. You work so hard.” She smiled. “I work hard because I love you,” she said. “And you are my greatest joy.” That night, I thought about my mother. She is always busy, always caring. She never complains. “I want to be a good daughter,” I said to myself. “I want to make her proud.” The next day, I helped her with the housework. “You don’t have to,” she said. “I want to!” I said. “You are growing up so fast,” she said. “Soon you will be a young lady.” I hugged her. “No matter how old I get,” I said, “I will always be your little girl.”

readings.title: The Old Church 老教堂
readings.text: Once upon a time, there was a small town with an old church. The church was very beautiful, with tall walls and colourful windows. It had stood there for more than three hundred years. “The church is the heart of our town,” my grandmother always said. One Saturday, my family and I visited the church. “Look at the windows!” my little sister said. “They are like pictures!” “They tell stories from the Bible,” my father said. “Long ago, people could not read. So they learned stories from the pictures on the windows.” “That is clever!” I said. We walked around the church quietly. “Be quiet, please,” my mother said. “People are praying.” I looked up at the high ceiling. Sunlight came through the windows and made colourful patterns on the floor. It was so beautiful that I could hardly breathe. “It feels like heaven,” I whispered. After a while, we went outside and sat in the garden. “Tell us a story about the church, Grandpa,” my sister said. My grandfather smiled and nodded. “When I was young,” he began, “there was a famous singer who came to our town. She sang in the church, and the whole town came to listen. Her voice was so beautiful that people cried.” “Really?” I said. “Yes!” he said. “And there is another story. During the war, the church was almost destroyed. But the brave people of our town protected it. They hid the precious things underground and guarded the doors day and night.” “They were heroes,” I said. “Yes,” my grandfather said. “We must never forget our history. It teaches us who we are.” I looked at the old church and felt proud. “One day, I will tell these stories to my children,” I said. My grandfather smiled. “That is the best way to keep history alive,” he said. My father bought me a new bike for my birthday. “This is the best gift!” I said.

readings.title: Trip to Canada 加拿大之旅
readings.text: Last summer, my parents took me to Canada. “This is a dream come true!” I said. “I have always wanted to see the world!” We flew from Beijing to Toronto. The flight was long, but I was too excited to sleep. “Look out of the window!” my mother said. “The clouds look like mountains of cotton!” When we arrived, a kind lady met us at the airport. She was my father’s old classmate. “Welcome to Canada!” she said with a big smile. “I will show you around.” We stayed in her beautiful house. It had a big garden with red and yellow flowers. “Can I help with anything?” I asked. “No, you are our guest!” she laughed. The next day, we went to see Niagara Falls. “Wow! It is so big!” I shouted. “The water falls from a great height. It is one of the most famous waterfalls in the world.” We took a boat ride near the falls. “Put on your raincoat!” my father said. “You will get wet!” We got very wet, but we laughed and laughed. “This is the best day of my life!” I said. We also visited a museum about the First Nations people. “They lived here for thousands of years,” the guide said. “They were the first people in Canada.” I learned that Canada has two official languages: English and French. “People here speak both languages,” my mother said. “That is why it is so special.” On our last day, we went shopping. “I want to buy a gift for my best friend,” I said. I bought a small model of a maple leaf. “The maple leaf is the symbol of Canada,” the shopkeeper said. “It is on our flag.” At the airport, I felt sad. “I don’t want to leave,” I said. “But we will come back,” my mother said. “The world is big. There is so much to see.” I nodded. “I want to see it all!” I said. On the plane home, I wrote in my diary: “Today I saw a new world. I will never forget Canada.”

readings.title: Uncle’s Restaurant 叔叔的餐馆
readings.text: My uncle has a small restaurant in the city. “Come and visit me!” he said on the phone. “I will cook you something special!” Last Sunday, my family went to see him. The restaurant was on a busy street. “Uncle! We are here!” I shouted. My uncle came out to meet us. “Welcome, my dear nephew!” he said. “Come in, come in!” The restaurant was warm and clean. There were many customers inside. “Your restaurant is very popular!” I said. “Yes,” my uncle said. “We are open every day from morning to night. We serve fresh food and friendly service.” “What is your most popular dish?” I asked. “Our dumplings!” he said. “And our roast duck. Many people come for them.” We sat at a table and ordered some food. “I want to try everything!” I said. “You can’t eat everything!” my mother laughed. We had dumplings, noodles, and a delicious soup. “This is the best food I have ever eaten!” I said. After lunch, my uncle showed me the kitchen. “This is where the magic happens,” he said. The kitchen was hot and busy. “How do you manage a restaurant?” I asked. “It is hard work,” he said. “I get up at five in the morning to buy fresh food. I work until ten at night. There is always something to do.” “Do you ever feel tired?” I asked. “Sometimes,” he said. “But when I see my customers smile, I feel happy. Cooking for people is my dream.” “I want to be like you one day,” I said. My uncle smiled. “Whatever you do, do it with love,” he said. “Then you will be successful.” That evening, my uncle gave us a box of mooncakes. “It is almost Mid-Autumn Festival,” he said. “Enjoy these!” “Thank you, Uncle!” I said. “Thank you for a wonderful day!” On the way home, I thought about my uncle. He works hard and never complains. “Success is not luck,” I said to myself. “It is hard work and a kind heart.” Last winter, we had a big snowstorm.

readings.title: The Airport 机场
readings.text: The airport was full of people. Some were laughing, and some were crying. “This is a place of goodbyes,” my mother said. “And hellos.” We were there to say goodbye to my cousin Anna. She was going to study in Canada. “I can’t believe this day has come,” she said. “I am so excited, but also a little afraid.” “You will be fine,” I said. “You are brave and smart.” Anna laughed. “Thank you,” she said. “I will miss you all so much.” We helped her check in her bags. “Did you bring your passport?” my aunt asked. “Yes, it is in my handbag,” Anna said. “And your ticket?” “Here it is!” We walked to the gate together. “Remember to call us when you arrive,” my grandmother said. “I will!” Anna said. “I promise to call every week.” “Study hard,” my uncle said. “But also take care of yourself. Eat well and sleep well.” “I will,” she said. “Don’t worry about me.” I gave her a small gift. “What is it?” she asked. “Open it on the plane,” I said. “It is a little something to remember us by.” Anna hugged me. “Thank you,” she said. “I will treasure it.” The loudspeaker announced our flight. “This is the final call for Flight CA1088 to Toronto.” “It is time,” Anna said. We hugged one last time. “Goodbye!” we all said. “Goodbye!” she said. “I love you all!” She walked through the gate and waved. We waved back until we could not see her anymore. On the way home, nobody said much. I looked at the sky and thought about Anna. “She is flying over the clouds now,” I said. “She is starting a new life.” My mother took my hand. “It is hard to say goodbye,” she said. “But goodbye is not the end. It is a new beginning.” I nodded. “She will come back,” I said. “And we will have so much to talk about!”

wordExamples: My grandfather is a very old man.
He is eighty years old.
“I have seen many things in my life,” he says.
“I have seen the world change.”
He tells me stories about the past.
“When I was young, there were no computers,” he says.
“We wrote letters by hand.”
“Was it difficult?”
I ask.
“No,” he says.
“We were happy. We talked to each other face to face. We shared our lives.”
I think about his words.
“Maybe we should do that too,” I say.
“Put down our phones and talk to people.”
My grandfather smiles.
“That is a wise idea,” he says.
“The best things in life are the simple ones.”

readings.title: A Wedding Day 婚礼日
readings.text: Last month, my big sister got married. It was a beautiful day. “I can’t believe my sister is getting married!” I said. “Neither can I!” my mother said, with tears in her eyes. My sister looked so beautiful in her white dress. “You look like a princess!” I told her. “Thank you, little brother,” she said. “I am so happy.” The wedding was held in a beautiful garden. There were flowers everywhere. The sun shone brightly, and the air smelled sweet. “This is like a dream,” my sister said. The music began to play, and my sister walked down the path with my father. My father looked proud but a little sad. “Take good care of her,” he said to the groom. “I promise,” the groom said. “I will love her forever.” They exchanged rings and made their promises. “I now pronounce you husband and wife!” the officiant said. Everyone cheered and threw flowers. After the ceremony, we had a big dinner. “This cake is delicious!” I said. “It has five floors!” “Don’t eat too much!” my mother laughed. “You will be sick!” During the dinner, my sister told me a secret. “You are my favourite brother,” she said. “I will always love you.” “I love you too,” I said. “Even though you are married now, you will always be my sister.” She smiled. “And you will always be my little brother.” That night, I could not sleep. I thought about all the good times we had together. “When we were young, we shared everything,” I said to myself. “Our toys, our secrets, our dreams.” My sister is far away now, but I know she is happy. “Love is not about being together every day,” my mother said. “It is about caring for each other, no matter where you are.” She is right. My sister is married, but our family will always be one. “I can’t wait to see her again!” I said. “We will,” my mother said. “Family is forever.” Last Christmas, I got a special gift: a robot!

readings.title: The Magic Show 魔法表演
readings.text: One evening, a magic show came to our town. “I love magic!” my little brother said. “Can we go?” “Of course!” my father said. “Let’s all go together!” We arrived at the hall early. There were many people waiting outside. “Look at that big poster!” my brother said. “The Great Wang! World-famous magician!” The show began at seven. The lights went down, and the music started. A man in a black suit walked onto the stage. “Good evening, ladies and gentlemen!” he said. “Welcome to the world of magic!” First, he pulled a rabbit out of an empty hat. “Wow!” everyone shouted. Then, he made a coin disappear. “Where did it go?” my brother asked. “Nobody knows!” I laughed. “It is magic!” The magician asked for a helper from the audience. “Who wants to come on stage?” he asked. My brother raised his hand. “You! Come here!” the magician said. My brother walked onto the stage, a little nervous. “What is your name?” “Ming,” my brother said. “Well, Ming,” the magician said, “I am going to make you float in the air!” “Really?” my brother said, his eyes wide. The magician waved his hands and said some magic words. Then, slowly, my brother began to rise! “I am flying!” he shouted. The whole hall clapped and cheered. When the show was over, my brother could not stop talking. “How did he do it?” he asked. “It is a secret,” I said. “A magician never tells his secrets.” “But I want to know!” he said. My father laughed. “Magic is about wonder,” he said. “It is more fun to believe than to know.” That night, my brother tried to do magic at home. “Watch! I can make this apple disappear!” he said. He hid it behind his back. “Where is it?” he asked. “I don’t know!” I said. “You are a great magician!” He laughed and laughed. “One day, I will be a real magician,” he said. “And I will show the whole world my magic!” On a dry summer day, we went to the beach.

readings.title: A Second Chance 第二次机会
readings.text: Hey, do you know him? Tom was a young man in an urban area, but his life was full of debt. In fact, he owed money to everyone, and his web bills were a real dilemma. One wet evening, he sat on the soft sofa in his small flat, wearing a worn sweater. A chart on the wall showed his debts, and it was not funny at all. “This life is boring,” he said to himself. He wanted to hold onto his old dream: to recite poems on a big stage. But fear was a barrier. His sister, a talented tailor, said, “Don’t worry about anything. You have a gift. As long as you try, you can change.” She taught him to punctuate his writing and pronounce words clearly. That night, he watched an opera about the orbit of the moon. The glare of the city lights made him think about the future. He opened his laptop and began to download a document about the Olympic Games. “Admission is free, and the stadium is near the station,” it said. A picture showed a field all over with flowers. Tom felt excited. He wrote a revision of his old poem and practised attentively. “I am proud of you,” his sister said. “Every good deed counts. Even a little effort is an advantage.” Tom smiled. He even wrote an artificial poem about mid autumn and his motherland. He was no longer a worm in a hive of worries. He picked up a recorder and began to sing. “Look out! Don’t knock over the bathtub!” his sister laughed. He laughed too. He had found his way back to life.

readings.title: The Brave Adventure 勇敢的冒险
readings.text: As she opened the door, her way was blocked by a big hole in the floor. “Who dug this?” she asked. His only answer was a smile. It was a hot day, and the air was dry. “Let’s clean the soil and fix it,” she said. He nodded. They worked hard, but the work was not easy. “Don’t cheat yourself,” she warned. “If you cheat, the floor will be unsafe.” He listened and began to expand the repair plan. They used a tablet to look up recipes for making strong cement. “This is like cooking,” she laughed. “You need the right order and the right fruit juice to make it tasty!” Soon, their neighbour came to help. She was a lively woman who liked to talk about her garden. “You can borrow my tools,” she said. “I keep them in my workshop.” They picked up the tools and went on. The work went on for hours. “I feel like a snake after all this effort!” he joked. “Don’t be upset,” she said. “Hard work is good for the soul.” In the evening, they finished the repair. “What a bargain!” she said. “We did it ourselves and saved a great deal of money.” He smiled. “Neither pride nor laziness can stop us now,” he said. They were out of breath but happy. This simple adventure taught them: teamwork can beat any chaos. Their friendship grew stronger that day, and they both improved a lot. It was a truly admirable day.

readings.title: The Green Dream 绿色的梦
readings.text: At the age of six, she was hit by a strange idea: why not make the desert green? “Ouch!” she cried when a thorn scratched her hand. “That hurts!” But she did not give up. “Once you have a dream, you must work for it,” her grandmother said. She yawned but kept reading books about plants. Soon, she learned about botany. She studied how liquid moves through leaves and how roots grip the soil. Her teacher was impressed. “You have a sharp mind,” he said. “You can escape the limits of this small town.” In high school, she joined a reform project. The target was a dry area near the mountains. She refused to give up even when the winter was vague and bitter. She planted young trees and watered them every day. Some villagers laughed at her. “This is a waste of time,” they said. But she did not care. A sponsor provided money, and a famous professor became her supporter. “Your idea is wonderful,” he said. “Add up to a thousand trees, and you will see a miracle.” She smiled and worked harder. She was energetic, and her energy impressed everyone. Soon, the district government noticed her. A reporter came to interview her. “Appreciate every small step,” she said. “As well as planting trees, we must protect the soil.” She even ate melon seeds while talking to them. As a result, more people joined her. Her brotherhood with the farmers grew strong. With great willingness and patience, she continued. Today, the once barren hills are green. Her life became a model for the whole neighbourhood. Her pronunciation of the word “hope” is still full of power.

readings.title: The Silent Hero 无声的英雄
readings.text: Before the war, he was a teacher in a small town. He was not a bishop or a famous expert, but the children loved him. “Obey the rules, work hard, and help others,” he often said. One snowy winter, the war came. Bombs fell, and the world seemed dark. His school was destroyed. He lost his hearing in an explosion, but he did not stop helping people. He hid food in his bedroom and shared it with the hungry. “We must look after each other,” he said. His courage inspired the whole village. A young officer came to him. “Sir, we need your help. Our soldiers are tired and hungry.” He nodded and opened his storage room. He gave them bread and soup. “Be careful,” the officer warned. “The enemy is everywhere.” He smiled. “Fear is our real enemy,” he said. One day, a spy was caught near the church. The villagers wanted to punish him. But the teacher stood up. “No,” he said. “We must not become like them. Show mercy.” His words touched everyone. After the war, the town was liberated. A monument was built in his honour. “He was like a teapot full of warmth, always giving,” an old man said. His initial teaching became a legend. “Although the war took his hearing, it could not take his heart,” people said. His story resembles a candle in the dark. He died out? No, his spirit lives on in every child he taught. They remember his face and his kind words. He is a true hero, a symbol of hope.

readings.title: A London Diary 伦敦日记
readings.text: Be careful when you travel to London, and you will have fun. Last summer, I flew there with my aunt. “Don’t be nervous,” she said. “Just look ahead.” At the airport, we showed our passports and took a taxi to the city. “How do you like London?” the driver asked. “It’s wonderful!” I said. We visited a temple and a palace. On the balcony of a museum, I saw a model of a beehive. “How do bees make honey?” I asked. My aunt laughed. “That’s a long story.” In the afternoon, we went to a park. The sky was clear, and the air was fresh. We saw a diamond exhibition and had dumplings with lemonade. “This is man made magic!” I said. We also visited a science museum. There was a huge telescope and many computers. “Perhaps one day you will discover something new,” my aunt said. She gave me a notebook. “Write down your ideas. Research is a journey.” On Saturday, we went shopping. My aunt bought a sweater and some postcards. “Don’t waste money,” she said, but she bought me a gift anyway. In the evening, we watched the sunset from a hill. The whole city lay below us. “What a view!” I said. “Look at the lights. They are like stars on earth.” My aunt smiled. “Above all, remember this feeling. The world is full of beauty.” Before we left, we visited a school. The students were very friendly. “Come again!” they shouted. I waved and said goodbye. That trip was more than a holiday. It taught me to see the world with new eyes. I will always treasure those days in London.
readings.translation: 去伦敦旅行时要小心，你会玩得很开心。去年夏天，我和阿姨飞去那里。“别紧张。”她说，“向前看就好。”在机场，我们出示护照，打车去市区。“你觉得伦敦怎么样？”司机问。“太棒了！”我说。我们参观了寺庙和宫殿。在博物馆的阳台上，我看到一个蜂巢模型。“蜜蜂怎么做蜂蜜？”我问。阿姨笑了：“那是个很长的故事。”下午，我们去了公园。天空晴朗，空气清新。我们看了钻石展，吃了饺子和柠檬水。“这是人造的魔法！”我说。我们还参观了科学博物馆，那里有巨大的望远镜和许多电脑。“也许有一天你会有所发现。”阿姨说。她送我一个笔记本：“把你的想法写下来。研究是一场旅程。”星期六，我们去购物。阿姨买了一件毛衣和一些明信片。“别乱花钱。”她说，但还是给我买了礼物。晚上，我们从山上观看日落，整座城市在我们脚下。“多美的景色！”我说，“看那些灯光，就像地上的星星。”阿姨笑了：“最重要的是记住这种感觉。世界充满美好。”离开前，我们参观了一所学校。学生们非常友好：“再来啊！”他们喊道。我挥手告别。那次旅行不仅仅是一次假期，它教会我用新的眼光看世界。我会永远珍藏伦敦的那些日子。

readings.title: The Marathon Runner 马拉松跑者
readings.text: By the time she was twenty, she had run many races. Her name was Maria, and she came from Belgium. “How did you get into running?” a reporter asked. “I began as a hobby,” she said. “One day, I watched a marathon on TV. I was so impressed that I decided to try.” Her training was hard. Every dawn, she got up and ran before breakfast. “Don’t let loneliness stop you,” her coach said. “You must be patient.” She kept a diary and wrote down her progress. “The body is like a machine. If you feed it well, it will serve you,” she said. She ate fruit and vegetables, and she never touched junk food. “A balanced diet is the key,” she explained. Sometimes she felt tired and wanted to give up. But she remembered her dream. “Success is a journey, not a destination,” she told herself. She also learned to listen to her body. “If you push too hard, you will get hurt,” her doctor warned. In the race, the weather was bad. Rain fell, and the wind was strong. But she did not stop. “I will run with my heart,” she said. After all, she had trained for years. She crossed the finish line and collapsed, out of breath but happy. “You did it!” her friends shouted. They hugged her and took photos. That night, there was a celebration. Maria smiled. “This medal is for everyone who believes in dreams,” she said. Her story inspired many young people. They learned that with hard work and courage, anything is possible. Even a simple girl can become a champion.

readings.title: The Boxer’s Heart 拳击手的心
readings.text: The boxer stood in the gym, his chest rising and falling. “Come on! One more round!” his coach shouted. He wiped the sweat from his face and nodded. “You must not betray your own dream,” the coach said. “Fighting is not only about strength. It is also about the soul.” The young man listened. He had started boxing as a child. At that time, he was thin and often bullied. “I want to be strong,” he said. His father, a former soldier, supported him. “Never give up, no matter how hard it is,” his father said. Training was painful. He ran every morning, even in the rain. He practised boxing until his hands hurt. “Your body must be solid, and your mind must be calm,” his coach taught him. “Don’t be afraid of losing. Be afraid of not trying.” Slowly, he improved. One day, he was chosen for an important match. The audience was huge. He felt nervous, but he remembered his father’s words. The match was fierce. In the third round, he was hit hard. For a moment, he felt like giving up. But he saw his coach’s eyes and heard the crowd. “I will fight for my family,” he said. He stood up and fought back. In the end, he won! The crowd cheered. His father cried with joy. “I am so proud of you,” he said. The young boxer smiled. “This victory belongs to everyone who believed in me,” he said. He became a record holder. But he stayed modest. “A true champion never stops learning,” he said. His story teaches us: with courage and hard work, we can overcome any difficulty.

readings.title: The Nurse’s Choice 护士的选择
readings.text: Do you know why she became a nurse? It started with a small accident. One afternoon, her younger brother cut his hand. “Don’t cry,” she said. “I will help you.” She cleaned the wound and put on a bandage. “You are so careful,” her mother said. From that day on, she wanted to help sick people. After high school, she entered a medical school. The lessons were hard, but she studied day and night. “A nurse must be patient and kind,” her teacher said. “You must treat every patient as your own family.” She remembered those words. During her training, she worked in a hospital. She helped the nurses and learned many skills. “You have a talent for this,” a doctor said. She smiled. One night, there was an emergency. A man had a heart attack. “Quick! Bring the equipment!” the doctor shouted. She ran and brought everything. The man was saved. His wife cried and thanked her. “You are an angel,” she said. That night, she felt proud. But her work was not always easy. Some patients were angry and difficult. “Don’t take it personally,” her senior nurse said. “They are in pain.” She learned to be calm and kind. Years later, she became the head nurse of the hospital. “Nursing is not just a job,” she often said. “It is a way to show love.” Her story spread far and wide. Many young people wanted to be like her. She taught them that true success is not about money. It is about making a difference in others’ lives.

readings.title: The Voice of the Sea 大海的声音
readings.text: Dr Lin was a scientist who studied the ocean. “The sea is not silent,” he often said. “It has a voice. Listen carefully.” He spent his life listening to whales and dolphins. “Zoom in on this sound,” he told his assistant. “Can you hear it? It is a song.” His love for the sea began when he was a child. He lived near the coast and loved to collect seashells. “One day, I will protect the ocean,” he said. His family laughed. “That is just a child’s dream.” But he did not give up. He studied biology and became an expert. His research was important. He discovered that noise from ships disturbs whales. “We must reduce the noise,” he said. “Otherwise, the whales cannot communicate.” He wrote many articles and gave lectures. “The ocean is in danger,” he warned. “Pollution is killing it.” Some people did not believe him. “The sea is so big,” they said. “How can we hurt it?” But Dr Lin did not stop. He worked with fishermen and taught them to protect the sea. “If we take care of the ocean, it will take care of us,” he said. One day, he received an important award. “This is not my award,” he said. “It belongs to the sea and all the people who love it.” He gave the money to build a nature reserve. Today, his work helps many sea animals. His story shows us: one person can make a big difference. We should always follow our dreams and protect our planet.
readings.translation: 林博士是一位研究海洋的科学家。“大海并不沉默。”他常说，“它有声音，仔细听。”他一生都在倾听鲸鱼和海豚。“放大这个声音。”他对助手说，“你能听到吗？这是一首歌。”他对大海的热爱始于童年。他住在海边，喜欢收集贝壳。“总有一天，我要保护海洋。”他说。家人笑了：“那只是孩子的梦。”但他没有放弃。他学习生物学，成为专家。他的研究很重要。他发现船只的噪音干扰鲸鱼。“我们必须减少噪音，否则鲸鱼无法交流。”他说。他写了许多文章，举办讲座。“海洋正处在危险中，污染正在杀死它。”他警告。有些人不相信他：“海那么大，我们怎么会伤害它？”但林博士没有停止。他与渔民合作，教他们保护大海。“如果我们爱护海洋，海洋也会爱护我们。”他说。一天，他获得了一项重要奖项。“这不是我的奖，它属于大海和所有爱它的人。”他说。他把奖金用于建立自然保护区。今天，他的工作帮助了许多海洋动物。他的故事告诉我们：一个人也能带来巨大的改变。我们应该永远追随梦想，保护我们的星球。

readings.title: The Internet Age 网络时代
readings.text: Go and look around you. The internet has changed our lives. “It is like a huge zoo of information,” my teacher said. “You can find anything if you know how to search.” I love the internet, but I also know its dangers. Last month, my friend Jack had a bad experience. He received a strange message from a website. It said he had won a prize. He clicked the link and entered his personal information. The next day, his bank account was empty! “Don’t panic,” his father said. “Let’s call the police.” They reported the crime, and the police caught the thieves. “Be careful online,” the police officer warned. “Never share your passwords.” Jack learned a valuable lesson. “The internet is a tool,” he said. “We must use it wisely.” My sister has a different story. She is a journalist. She uses the internet to find news and write articles. “It makes my work faster,” she says. “But I always check the facts before I write.” She is very careful. “Fake news is dangerous,” she says. I also use the internet for my studies. I watch videos, read articles, and talk to friends. “It is amazing,” I say. “We can learn anything from anywhere.” But my mother worries about us. “Don’t spend too much time on your phone,” she says. “Go outside and play. The real world is beautiful too.” She is right. The internet is wonderful, but we must remember to live in the real world. Balance is the key to a happy life.

readings.title: The Dinosaur in the Cornfield 玉米地里的恐龙
readings.text: Ha! Have you heard about the dinosaur in our village? It all began one foggy morning in January. Old Mr Brown, a farmer, went to check his cornfield. “What is that?” he cried. A huge bone stuck out of the ground. “Is it a cow bone?” he wondered. He called the university. Soon, a group of scientists arrived with a truck and many tools. “This is amazing!” the leader said. “It is a dinosaur! We must be careful.” They dug slowly and carefully. Day after day, they found more bones. “It was a giant animal,” a young scientist explained. “It lived millions of years ago.” The villagers were excited. Children came to watch after class. “Can we help?” they asked. “Of course,” the scientist smiled. “You can carry the small pieces.” Even the postman and the peasant stopped to watch. A lawyer who was visiting his family came too. “This will attract many tourists,” he said. “It is a great chance for our village.” The mayor agreed. They decided to build a small museum. Soon, news spread far and wide. Reporters came to interview the scientists. “This discovery is very important,” one expert said. “It helps us understand the past.” The dinosaur became famous. Tourists came from everywhere to see it. The village changed. New shops opened, and the people became richer. Mr Brown smiled. “I always knew this land was special,” he said. The dinosaur not only taught us about history, but it also brought new life to our small village.

readings.title: The Dentist’s Diary 牙医日记
readings.text: He was a dentist, and he loved his job. “A smile is the best medicine,” he often said. His name was Dr Lee, and his clinic was near a busy street. Every day, patients came to see him. Some were afraid of the dentist. “It will not hurt,” he said gently. “Relax, and it will be over soon.” He remembered his first patient. It was a little girl with a bad toothache. She cried and refused to sit in the chair. “Look at this shiny mirror,” he said. “Can you see your tooth?” Slowly, she calmed down. He worked carefully and quickly. “All done!” he said. The girl smiled. “That was not so bad!” she said. From that day on, she was not afraid anymore. Dr Lee worked long hours. Sometimes he felt tired, but he never complained. “Helping people is my happiness,” he said. One winter, a young man came with a broken tooth. He had no money. “Don’t worry,” Dr Lee said. “Your health is more important than money. Come in.” He treated the young man for free. The young man was surprised and grateful. “Thank you, doctor. One day, I will pay you back,” he said. Years later, the young man became a successful businessman. He returned to thank Dr Lee and donated money to the clinic. “Kindness always comes back,” Dr Lee said. He taught his students that a good doctor needs both skill and a warm heart. “Always listen to your patients,” he said. “Sometimes they just need someone to talk to.” Dr Lee is retired now, but his story still inspires many young doctors.

readings.title: The Marathon for Love 为爱奔跑
readings.text: Hi, let me tell you about my father. He is an athlete, and he runs marathons for charity. “Why do you run so far?” people ask. He smiles. “Because some children need help.” Five years ago, my cousin was very ill. The medicine was expensive, and the hospital bill was huge. My family was worried. “How can we pay for it?” my mother sighed. Then my father had an idea. “I will run a marathon and ask people to donate,” he said. He trained for months. Every morning at dawn, he ran along the river. “Be careful,” my mother said. “Don’t hurt yourself.” “Don’t worry,” he said. “I am strong.” On the day of the race, thousands of people came. My father ran with all his heart. At the twentieth kilometre, his legs hurt, and he wanted to stop. But he thought of my cousin and continued. “You can do it!” the crowd shouted. He crossed the finish line and fell to the ground, exhausted. But he was smiling. The race raised a lot of money. My cousin got the treatment she needed and recovered. “Thank you, Uncle,” she said. “You saved my life.” My father hugged her. “No,” he said. “Love saved you. We are a family. We help each other.” Now my father runs every year. He has raised money for many children. “Running is not just a sport,” he says. “It is a way to show love.” I am proud of him. He taught me that one person’s effort can change the world. Even a small step forward is a step toward hope.

readings.title: The Old Biology Book 旧生物学书
readings.text: If you open an old book, you never know what you will find. Last week, I was cleaning my grandfather’s study. Under a pile of papers, I found a dusty book. Its cover was torn, but the title was clear: “The Biology of the Sea.” I opened it and began to read. It was full of wonderful pictures of fish and plants. “This book is a treasure,” I said. My grandfather smiled. “It was my favourite when I was young,” he said. “I wanted to be a scientist and study the ocean.” He told me about his dream. “But life took me in another direction,” he said. “I became a teacher instead.” He sighed. “Do you regret it?” I asked. “No,” he said. “I love teaching. Every student is like a seed. I plant hope in their hearts.” He showed me more old books and photos. “Look at this one. It was taken on my first day of teaching.” The photo showed a young man standing in front of a blackboard, smiling. “You look so happy,” I said. “I was,” he laughed. “Teaching is a noble job.” He told me stories about his students. Some became doctors, and some became engineers. “Every success makes me proud,” he said. That evening, I read the old book until midnight. I learned about whales, dolphins, and strange fish from the deep sea. “I want to protect the ocean,” I told my grandfather. He smiled. “Follow your dream,” he said. “And remember: knowledge is the greatest gift.” I will never forget that afternoon in his study. That old book changed my life.

readings.title: The Firefighter’s Night 消防员之夜
readings.text: In the middle of the night, the fire alarm rang. Firefighter Tom jumped out of bed. “There is a fire in the old building!” the captain shouted. Tom put on his helmet and rushed to the truck. The streets were dark, and the rain was falling. “Be careful, Tom,” his partner said. “The wind is strong tonight.” They arrived at the burning building. Smoke was everywhere. People were shouting and crying at the windows. “Help us!” a woman screamed. “My baby is inside!” Tom did not hesitate. He ran into the building. The fire was fierce, and the heat was terrible. He climbed the stairs and found the baby crying in a room. “Don’t be afraid,” he said softly. “I am here.” He wrapped the baby in a blanket and carried him out. The crowd cheered. “You are a hero!” they shouted. But the night was not over. There was another person trapped on the fifth floor. Tom went back into the fire. He searched the rooms and finally found an old man. “Hold on! I will save you!” he said. He carried the old man down the ladder. At last, everyone was safe. Tom was tired and covered in smoke, but he smiled. “That was a close call,” his captain said. “You were very brave.” Tom shook his head. “I just did my job,” he said. “Every life is precious.” The next day, the newspaper wrote about him. Tom became famous, but he stayed modest. “I am not a hero,” he said. “The real heroes are my team. We work together.” His story reminds us that courage is not the absence of fear. It is doing the right thing even when you are afraid.

readings.title: The Detective’s Case 侦探的案件
readings.text: It was a quiet evening, and the detective was reading in his office. Suddenly, the phone rang. “Detective! Someone has stolen my necklace!” a woman cried. “Don’t worry,” he said. “I will come right away.” He arrived at the house and began to investigate. The woman, Mrs Green, was very upset. “I put the necklace on my desk before dinner,” she said. “When I came back, it was gone.” The detective looked around carefully. He noticed a window open and some footprints on the floor. “Who else was in the house tonight?” he asked. “Only my niece and the cook,” she said. The detective talked to the cook first. “I was cooking in the kitchen all night,” the cook said. “I didn’t see anything.” Then he talked to the niece. “I was in my room reading,” she said. But the detective noticed that her hands were shaking. “Show me your room,” he said. In her room, he found the necklace hidden under a pile of clothes. “Why did you do it?” he asked quietly. The niece began to cry. “I needed money for my husband. He is ill,” she said. “I am so sorry.” The detective felt sad. “Stealing is wrong,” he said. “But I will tell Mrs Green the truth. Perhaps she will forgive you.” Mrs Green was shocked but kind. “I will help your husband,” she said. “But you must learn from this mistake.” The niece thanked her and promised to change. The detective smiled. “Justice is not only about punishment,” he said.

readings.title: The Journalist’s Journey 记者之旅
readings.text: Me? I am a journalist. “Jog to the newsroom!” my editor jokes every morning. I work for a small newspaper, and I love my job. One day, my editor gave me an important task. “There is a strange story in the east of the city,” he said. “People say a whale appeared near the river. Go and find out the truth.” I took my notebook and went there. The streets were quiet, and the weather was cold. I walked along the river and saw a crowd of people. “Look! A whale!” a boy shouted. I could not believe my eyes. A huge whale was swimming in the river! “How did it get here?” I asked. An old fisherman shook his head. “It must have lost its way,” he said. I called a scientist. “We must help it,” I said. “The water is too shallow for it.” Soon, a rescue team arrived. They worked carefully to guide the whale back to the sea. I took photos and wrote down every detail. “This will be a great story,” I thought. That evening, I wrote my article. I called it “The Lost Whale.” It was published the next day and became very popular. People thanked me for telling the story. “Your article helped us understand the whale,” a teacher said. “It is important to protect our rivers.” I felt proud. Being a journalist is not just about writing. It is about telling the truth and helping people. “Keep on learning, keep on asking,” my editor always says. “The world is full of stories.” He is right. Every day is a new adventure for me.

readings.text: Mm, this is a strange story, but it is true. Last month, a kangaroo escaped from the zoo and jumped into the city park! “Look! A kangaroo!” children shouted. The kangaroo was scared and did not know where to go. It hopped across the grass and knocked over a flower pot. “We must catch it carefully,” a policeman said. “Don’t frighten it.” A group of people followed the kangaroo. Some took photos, and some called the zoo. Soon, a keeper arrived with a net. “Come here, little one,” she said softly. The kangaroo stopped and looked at her. Slowly, she got close and put the net over it. “Got you!” she smiled. The children clapped. “Why did it escape?” a reporter asked. “Maybe it was bored or hungry,” the keeper said. “Kangaroos need space to jump.” The kangaroo was taken back to the zoo. The zoo decided to build a bigger home for it. “Animals are our friends,” the keeper said. “We must take good care of them.” The story spread quickly. People came from far away to see the famous kangaroo. They named it “Jumper.” The park became more popular, too. I learned an important lesson from this story: we should respect animals and give them a good life. “Every creature has feelings,” my teacher said. “If we treat them kindly, they will trust us.” She was right. Now I always try to be kind to animals. I even helped a bird that fell from its nest last week. Kindness makes the world a better place.

readings.title: The Physicist’s Dream 物理学家的梦
readings.text: Mr Li is a famous physicist, but he was not always a scientist. “Ten years ago, I was a clerk in a small office,” he said. “Every day, I did the same work. I felt bored and unhappy.” One winter, he visited his hometown. He saw old friends and remembered his childhood dreams. “I always loved science,” he said. “I wanted to understand how the universe works.” That night, he made a decision. “I will change my life,” he told his wife. She supported him. “Follow your dream,” she said. He quit his job and went back to university. The first year was hard. He had to learn mathematics and physics from the beginning. “Don’t give up,” his teacher said. “Science needs patience.” He studied day and night. Sometimes he felt like giving up, but he remembered his dream. After four years, he graduated with excellent results. He joined a research centre and began to study light and energy. His work was difficult, but he loved it. One day, he made an important discovery about how light moves. The news spread quickly. “This is a great achievement!” scientists said. Mr Li became famous. But he stayed humble. “Science is not about being famous,” he said. “It is about understanding the world and helping people.” He now teaches at a university and encourages young students. “Never stop asking questions,” he tells them. “The world is full of mysteries, and every question is a door to discovery.” His story shows us that it is never too late to follow our dreams.

readings.title: A Cultural Exchange 文化交流
readings.text: Ms Wang is a teacher at a language school. Last month, a group of Japanese students came to visit. “Welcome!” she said. “Today, you will learn about Chinese culture.” The students were excited. In the morning, they watched a movie about Chinese customs. “In China, we greet people with a smile and a nod,” Ms Wang explained. “We don’t kiss on the cheek like some westerners.” The students laughed. Then they learned to use chopsticks. “This is difficult!” one boy said. But he did not give up. “Practice makes perfect,” Ms Wang said. After lunch, they visited a famous monument in the city. “This building is very old,” the guide said. “It was built hundreds of years ago.” The students took many photos. “The architecture is amazing!” they said. In the evening, there was a welcome party. The students performed a traditional Japanese dance. Everyone clapped. Then the Chinese students sang a song. “Music is a universal language,” Ms Wang said. The next day, the students went shopping. They bought gifts for their families. “These chopsticks are beautiful,” one girl said. “My mother will love them.” Before they left, they wrote thank-you letters. “Thank you for your kindness,” they wrote. “We will never forget this trip.” Ms Wang smiled. “Culture is a bridge between people,” she said. “When we understand each other, the world becomes smaller and friendlier.” The exchange was a great success. Both sides learned a lot. “I want to visit Japan one day,” one Chinese student said. “And I want to learn more Chinese,” a Japanese student replied. They said goodbye and promised to write to each other.
readings.translation: 王老师是一所语言学校的老师。上个月，一群日本学生来参观。“欢迎！”她说，“今天你们将了解中国文化。”学生们很兴奋。上午，他们看了一部关于中国风俗的电影。“在中国，我们用微笑和点头打招呼，不像一些西方人那样亲脸颊。”王老师解释道。学生们笑了。然后他们学用筷子。“太难了！”一个男孩说。但他没有放弃。“熟能生巧。”王老师说。午饭后，他们参观了市里一座著名的纪念碑。“这座建筑很古老，建于几百年前。”导游说。学生们拍了许多照片：“建筑太神奇了！”晚上有欢迎会。学生们表演了日本传统舞蹈，大家鼓掌。然后中国学生唱了一首歌。“音乐是通用的语言。”王老师说。第二天，学生们去购物，给家人买礼物。“这些筷子真漂亮，我妈妈会喜欢的。”一个女孩说。离开前，他们写了感谢信：“谢谢你们的善意，我们永远不会忘记这次旅行。”王老师笑了：“文化是人与人之间的桥梁。当我们互相理解，世界就会变得更小、更友好。”这次交流非常成功。双方都学到了很多。“我想有一天去日本。”一个中国学生说。“我也想学更多中文。”一个日本学生回答。他们道别，承诺互相写信。

readings.title: My Aunt the Sculptor 我的雕塑家阿姨
readings.text: My aunt is a sculptor, and she has a small studio behind her house. “My job is to give life to stone,” she says. “But it is not easy. You must be patient.” She works with her hands every day. “Fix this piece of marble,” she tells her assistant. “Then we will shape it.” Her work is famous, but she is not proud. “I am merely a servant of beauty,” she says. Last July, she received a big order. A supermarket wanted a sculpture for its entrance. “This is a great chance,” she said. “But the deadline is short.” She worked day and night. Sometimes she forgot to eat. “Don’t stress yourself,” my uncle said. “Your health is more important.” “I know,” she said. “But this work means a lot to me.” She had a clear vision: a bird flying above a bamboo tree. “It will stand for freedom and hope,” she explained. She chose the stone carefully. “This piece is perfect,” she said. Day by day, the sculpture grew. She used a special tool to cut the stone. “Be careful with your fingers,” I warned. She laughed. “I have done this for twenty years.” Finally, the sculpture was finished. It was beautiful. The supermarket owner was delighted. “This is wonderful!” he said. “Everyone will love it.” He paid her well. My aunt smiled. “Art is my prayer,” she said. “Every piece is a piece of my heart.” Now, when I walk past the supermarket, I see her bird. It makes me feel hopeful. I am proud of my aunt. She taught me that if you work hard and follow your heart, you can create something beautiful. “Never give up your dream,” she tells me. “Even a small stone can become a treasure.”

readings.title: The Ballet Dancer 芭蕾舞演员
readings.text: No one believed that a girl from a small town could become a famous ballet dancer. But Lily did. “Fit your body and train your mind,” her teacher said. “Dance is not just about movement. It is about feeling.” Lily started ballet at the age of five. “Tap your feet lightly,” the teacher said. “Don’t be dull. Be light like a bird.” She practised every day, even after school. “My legs hurt, and my arms are tired,” she complained. “But I love dancing.” Her mother supported her. “If you want to swim in the sea of art, you must work hard,” she said. One day, a famous ballet company came to their town. They were looking for young dancers. Lily was nervous but excited. “Show me what you can do,” the director said. She danced with all her heart. The director was impressed. “You have talent,” he said. “Come to our school in the city.” Lily was overjoyed. In the city, life was different. The lessons were hard, and the teachers were strict. “Don’t be lazy,” her teacher warned. “A dancer’s life is full of pain.” But Lily never gave up. She practised until her feet bled. “Every step is a prayer,” she said. Years passed. Lily became the leading dancer of the company. The audience loved her. “She dances like an angel!” people said. Her dream came true. But she never forgot her hometown. She returned every year to teach children. “Dance is a gift,” she said. “It can change your life, just as it changed mine.” Her story is a wonderful example: with hard work and courage, dreams can come true.

readings.title: The Bakery on the Corner 街角的面包店
readings.text: Of the many shops in our town, the bakery on the corner is my favourite. It is a small shop, but it is always warm and full of good smells. The baker, Mr Chen, starts work before dawn. “A few minutes more in the oven makes all the difference,” he says. He makes bread, cakes, and the best biscuits in the region. One day, a strange thing happened. A tourist from Mexico came in. “Excuse me,” she said. “Can you help me? I am lost.” Mr Chen smiled. “Don’t worry. Where do you want to go?” “I want to see the old temple near the river,” she said. Mr Chen gave her directions and a free bun. “Enjoy your visit,” he said. The tourist was very grateful. “Thank you so much! The people here are so kind!” she said. That evening, Mr Chen closed the shop and went for a walk. He saw the old temple in the sunset and felt peaceful. “This town is my home,” he said. “I love its streets and its people.” Years ago, he had wanted to retire and move to the city. But he stayed. “I am happy here,” he said. “A simple life is a good life.” His bakery became famous. People came from far away to buy his bread. He hired a young helper and taught him everything. “Baking is an art,” Mr Chen said. “You must put your heart into it.” The young man learned quickly. One day, he made a cake by himself. “Not bad!” Mr Chen laughed. “You will be a great baker.” The bakery is still there today. Whenever I smell fresh bread, I think of Mr Chen and his kind smile. He taught me that even a small job can bring great happiness.
readings.translation: 在我们镇上的许多店铺中，街角的面包店是我最喜欢的。店面不大，但总是温暖，充满好闻的气味。面包师陈先生天亮前就开始工作。“在烤箱里多烤几分钟，结果就完全不同。”他说。他做面包、蛋糕，还有本地最好的饼干。一天，发生了一件奇怪的事。一位来自墨西哥的游客走进来。“打扰一下。”她说，“你能帮我吗？我迷路了。”陈先生笑了：“别担心，你想去哪里？”“我想看看河边那座老寺庙。”她说。陈先生告诉她路线，还送她一个免费小圆面包：“祝你玩得开心。”游客非常感激：“太谢谢了！这里的人真善良！”那天晚上，陈先生关店去散步。他看到夕阳下的老寺庙，感到宁静。“这个镇是我的家，我爱它的街道和人民。”他说。多年前，他曾想退休搬到城里，但他留下了。“我在这里很快乐，简单的生活就是好生活。”他的面包店出了名，人们从远方来买他的面包。他雇了一个年轻帮手，把一切都教给他。“烘焙是艺术，必须用心。”陈先生说。年轻人学得很快。一天，他独立做了一个蛋糕。“不错！”陈先生笑了，“你会成为好面包师的。”面包店至今还在。每当我闻到新鲜面包的味道，就会想起陈先生和他善良的微笑。他教会我：即使小工作也能带来大幸福。

readings.title: The Spy Next Door 隔壁的间谍
readings.text: Oh, what a strange summer that was! My family moved to a new apartment, and our neighbour was a spy. Well, at least that is what my little brother believed. “Look at that man!” he whispered. “He is always watching the street. He must be a spy!” “Don’t be silly,” I said. “He is just an old man.” But my brother would not listen. He decided to investigate. One afternoon, he followed the man to a park. The man sat on a bench and fed the birds. “See? He is sending secret messages!” my brother said. I laughed. “He is just feeding the birds.” The next day, my brother saw the man carrying a small black bag. “It must be a secret code machine!” he said. He told our mother, and she laughed too. “He is probably a retired teacher,” she said. But my brother would not give up. He wrote everything down in his diary. One day, the man knocked on our door. “Hello,” he said. “I am Mr White. I heard you are new here. Would you like to come to my house for tea?” We went to his house. It was full of books and photos. “I was a teacher for forty years,” he said. “Now I am retired. I like to watch the street because it is peaceful.” My brother’s face turned red. “I thought you were a spy,” he said quietly. Mr White laughed loudly. “That is the best joke I have heard in years!” From that day on, we became good friends with Mr White. “Never judge people by their appearance,” my mother said. My brother learned his lesson. “I will not be so quick to guess,” he said. What a funny summer that was!

readings.title: The Invention Fair 发明展
readings.text: Ok, let me tell you about the school invention fair. It was held in our schoolyard on a cold September morning. “Each class must show one invention,” the headmaster said. “The best one will win a prize.” My class decided to make a robot that could water plants. “That is a great idea,” our teacher said. “Let’s get started.” We worked after school every day. Tom designed the robot, and Lily made the posters. “Don’t forget the battery,” Tom said. “The robot needs power.” We tested it again and again. Sometimes it did not work, but we did not give up. “Be patient,” our teacher said. “Great inventions take time.” On the day of the fair, the schoolyard was full of people. Parents and students came to see the inventions. There were robots, model planes, and many other wonderful things. “Look at that poster!” a visitor said. “It is so colourful!” Our robot was in the corner. We were a little nervous. “What if it doesn’t work?” Lily whispered. Just then, a judge came to our table. “Can you show me how it works?” he asked. Tom pressed the button. The robot moved forward and watered a small flower. “Excellent!” the judge said. “Very creative!” In the end, our class won the first prize! We were so happy. “Hard work pays off,” our teacher said. “You should be proud of yourselves.” The fair taught us many things. We learned that invention needs imagination, patience, and teamwork. “Never stop creating,” the headmaster said. “The world needs your ideas.” That day, I decided to become an inventor. I want to create something that helps people and makes the world better.
