readings.title: The Night Porter 夜班行李员
readings.text: On a cold winter night, a young porter worked at a hotel. His name was Sam, and he was saving money for college. “This job is not easy,” he said, “but I need the money.” That night, a tired traveller came in. “I missed my flight,” he said. “Do you have a room?” “Yes, sir,” Sam said. “Welcome to our hotel.” The man thanked him and went to his room. At midnight, Sam heard a strange noise. He went to check. He saw a man trying to open a door. “Can I help you?” Sam asked. The man looked nervous. “I forgot my key,” he said. But Sam did not believe him. He remembered that the traveller had a valuable camera in his room. Sam called the police quietly. Soon, the police came and caught the thief. “Good job!” the policeman said. “You are very clever.” The traveller was grateful. “You saved my camera!” he said. “It was a gift from my father.” Sam smiled. “It is my duty to protect our guests,” he said. The traveller was so happy that he wrote a letter to the manager. “Your porter is a hero,” he wrote. The manager praised Sam and gave him a reward. “You have a bright future,” he said. Sam continued to work hard. He studied at night and worked during the day. Finally, he entered the college and became an excellent student. “Never look down on small jobs,” he often said. “Every job teaches you something. Be honest, be kind, and work hard. Good things will come.” Sam’s story spread in the town. Many young people were inspired by him. They learned that with courage and honesty, anyone can change their life.

readings.title: The Country Doctor 乡村医生
readings.text: Or maybe you have heard about Dr Sun, the country doctor. She works in a small village hospital. “There are only a few doctors here,” she says. “But we help many people.” Every morning, she gets up early and goes to work. “Good morning, Doctor!” the villagers greet her. She smiles and waves. Her day is always busy. She sees patients, checks their health, and gives them medicine. “Take this tablet three times a day,” she tells them. She also visits old people at home. “How is your back today?” she asks Mrs Wang. “Much better, Doctor. Thank you,” Mrs Wang says. One night, there was an emergency. A farmer had a heart attack. “Quick! We must go now!” Dr Sun shouted. She drove through the dark streets and saved the farmer’s life. “You are an angel,” his family said. Dr Sun shook her head. “I just did my job,” she said. But she was happy. She loves her work because she can help people. “Money is not everything,” she says. “Seeing patients get better is the best reward.” Her father was also a doctor. “He taught me that a doctor must be kind and patient,” she says. “He was my hero.” Now she is a hero to the villagers too. “We trust Dr Sun completely,” they say. “She is like family.” Dr Sun plans to stay in the village for many years. “The village needs me,” she says. “And I need the village. It is my home.” Her story teaches us: true happiness comes from helping others. A warm heart is more valuable than gold.

readings.title: The Astronaut’s Daughter 宇航员的女儿
readings.text: Ox or bull, it doesn’t matter. My father is an astronaut, and I am proud of him. “The sky is not the limit,” he always says. “The universe is our home.” When I was little, he told me stories about stars and planets. “One day, humans will travel to Mars,” he said. “Maybe you will go there!” I loved his stories. But being an astronaut’s daughter is not always easy. He is often away for months. “Don’t worry,” he says on the phone. “I will be home soon.” Last year, he went to space for six months. I missed him very much. “Be brave,” my mother said. “Your father is doing something great.” We watched the launch on television. The rocket rose into the sky with a loud noise. “That is my father!” I shouted. Tears came to my eyes. In space, my father sent us videos. He floated in the spaceship and showed us the earth. “Look! That is our home,” he said. “It is so beautiful from up here.” I felt proud and happy. When he came back, we had a big celebration. “Welcome home, Dad!” I said. He hugged me. “I missed you so much,” he said. He told us about his journey. “Space is wonderful, but there is no place like home,” he said. Now I am studying hard. I want to be an astronaut like my father. “Follow your dream,” he tells me. “Work hard, and anything is possible.” My father taught me to be brave and never give up. One day, I will fly to the stars. And when I look down at the earth, I will remember his words: “Home is where love is.”

readings.title: The Lost Necklace 丢失的项链
readings.text: So you want to know about the necklace? It is a long story. Last spring, my grandmother gave me a beautiful necklace. “It was my mother’s,” she said. “Now it is yours. Take good care of it.” I loved it at once. “It is so beautiful!” I said. I wore it to school every day. One windy afternoon, I went to the park with my friend. “Let’s fly a kite!” she said. We ran and played. Suddenly, I felt my neck. The necklace was gone! “Oh no!” I cried. “I lost it!” We looked everywhere. We searched under the trees and beside the lake. But we could not find it. “Don’t worry,” my friend said. “Let’s think. Where did we play last?” We walked back slowly. Then I saw something shiny near a bench. It was my necklace! “I found it!” I shouted with joy. I held it tightly and thanked my friend. That night, I told my grandmother the story. “You were lucky,” she said. “But next time, be more careful. Some things are too precious to lose.” I nodded. From that day on, I kept the necklace in a special box. I only wore it on important days. “A gift from your family is a treasure,” my grandmother said. “It carries their love and memories.” I understood. The necklace is not just a piece of gold. It is a symbol of my family’s love. When I wear it, I feel my grandmother’s warmth. I will pass it to my daughter one day. Some things are worth more than money. Love is one of them.

readings.title: The Farm in Summer 夏天的农场
readings.text: To understand the countryside, you should visit a farm in summer. Last July, my family spent two weeks on my uncle’s farm. “Welcome!” my uncle said. “You will work hard, but you will have fun.” Every morning, we got up at six. “Time to feed the animals!” my cousin shouted. We fed the chickens and the pigs. “Look at that fat pig!” my little brother laughed. The pigs were always hungry. After breakfast, we worked in the fields. We picked tomatoes and planted vegetables. “This is hard work,” I said. “But it is good for us.” At noon, my aunt cooked a big lunch. “Everything is fresh from the farm,” she said. The food was delicious! In the afternoon, we fed the sheep and collected eggs. “Be careful. The hen is protecting her babies,” my uncle warned. One day, we had a small accident. A sheep ran away, and we had to catch it. “Don’t worry,” my uncle said. “It happens. We must be patient.” We finally caught the sheep and brought it back. In the evening, we sat by the fire and talked. My uncle told us stories about his childhood. “I love this farm,” he said. “It is my whole life.” I learned a lot that summer. I learned where our food comes from. I learned to respect the farmers who work so hard. “Every grain is a gift of nature,” my uncle said. When we left, I was sad. “Come back next summer!” my cousin shouted. I waved and promised. That summer on the farm taught me the value of hard work and simple life. I will never forget it.

readings.title: The Bank on the Corner 街角的银行
readings.text: Up the street from our school, there is a small bank. Every day, people go there to save money or take out money. My aunt works there as a cashier. “It is a quiet job,” she says. “But you must be careful. Money is a big responsibility.” One Monday morning, an old man came in. He looked worried. “Can I help you, sir?” my aunt asked. “I received a strange phone call,” he said. “Someone asked me to send money to a stranger.” My aunt was alert. “That is a trick!” she said. “Don’t trust them. Never give your money to anyone you don’t know.” She explained the danger clearly. The old man thanked her. “You saved my money!” he said. “It is my life savings.” The manager heard the story and praised my aunt. “You are a careful and honest worker,” he said. That evening, my aunt told us the story. “There are many dishonest people in the world,” she said. “We must protect ourselves and our families.” I learned an important lesson that day. “Be careful with your money,” my aunt said. “Don’t be greedy. If something seems too good to be true, it usually is.” My aunt also helps students. “Open a savings account,” she tells them. “Save a little every week. Small savings can grow into big money.” Many students followed her advice. “Thank you for teaching us,” they said. My aunt smiles. “Helping people is my joy,” she says. “A bank is not just about money. It is about trust.” I am proud of my aunt. She is a small person, but she makes a big difference in our community.

readings.title: The Woman Scientist 女科学家
readings.text: We often say that science has no borders. Dr Anna is a perfect example. She is a woman scientist from Australia, and she studies plants. “Bare soil is a problem,” she says. “We must protect the earth.” Last year, she came to our school. “Can a scientist be a woman?” a student asked. She laughed. “Of course! I am living proof.” She told us about her work. “I study how plants grow in different conditions,” she said. “It is amazing how nature works.” She showed us photos of her lab. “This is my thermos for coffee, and this is my favourite bathrobe,” she joked. The students laughed. “What is your most important discovery?” another student asked. “I learned that we must work together,” she said. “No one can save the planet alone. We need teamwork.” She explained that farmers, scientists, and governments must cooperate. “In peace, we can achieve great things,” she said. She also told us about her childhood. “I loved plants from a young age. My grandmother had a garden, and I helped her every day.” Her eyes shone with happiness. “Follow your interests,” she said. “Even a small seed can grow into a big tree.” After the talk, many students wanted to be scientists. “I want to study biology!” one boy said. Dr Anna smiled. “Science needs curious minds,” she said. “The world is full of questions waiting for answers.” She left us a wonderful gift: the belief that we can change the world. I will never forget her words: “Never stop asking why. That is the beginning of all discoveries.”
readings.translation: 我们常说科学没有国界。安娜博士就是最好的例子。她是来自澳大利亚的女科学家，研究植物。“裸露的土壤是个问题，我们必须保护地球。”她说。去年，她来到我们学校。“科学家能是女性吗？”一个学生问。她笑了：“当然！我就是活生生的证明。”她给我们讲她的工作。“我研究植物在不同条件下的生长，大自然真神奇。”她说。她给我们看实验室的照片。“这是我的保温杯，装咖啡用的；这是我最喜欢的浴袍。”她开玩笑说。学生们笑了。“您最重要的发现是什么？”另一个学生问。“我明白了我们必须合作。”她说，“没有人能独自拯救地球，我们需要团队合作。”她解释说农民、科学家和政府必须协作。“在和平中，我们能成就伟大的事。”她说。她还讲了自己的童年：“我从小就爱植物。奶奶有个花园，我每天都帮她。”她的眼里闪着幸福的光。“追随你的兴趣，即使小种子也能长成大树。”她说。讲座后，许多学生想当科学家。“我想学生物！”一个男孩说。安娜博士笑了：“科学需要好奇心，世界充满等待答案的问题。”她留给我们一份美好的礼物：相信我们能改变世界。我永远不会忘记她的话：“永远不要停止问为什么，那是一切发现的开始。”

readings.title: A Trip to Tokyo 东京之旅
readings.text: Act wisely, and you will enjoy your trip. Last February, my family visited Tokyo. “This is a wonderful city!” my mother said. We arrived at the airport and took a train to the city centre. The streets were clean, and the buildings were tall. “Look at that tower!” my little sister shouted. We visited many famous places. We saw a beautiful temple and a big park. “Can we see the cherry blossoms?” I asked. “Not yet,” my father said. “They open in April.” We also went to a museum. There were old kites and paintings. “This kite is a hundred years old!” the guide said. “Amazing!” I said. In the evening, we ate at a small restaurant. “Try this steak,” my father said. “It is delicious!” I was hungry, so I ate a lot. “Don’t eat too much,” my mother laughed. “You will get a stomachache.” The next day, we went shopping. My mother bought a silk scarf, and I bought a small sword. “It is just a toy,” I said. “But it looks cool!” We also met a friendly old man in the park. He taught me how to say “hello” in Japanese. “Konnichiwa!” I said. He laughed. “Very good!” Before we left, we bought some gifts for our friends. “Don’t forget to send postcards,” my mother reminded me. I sent ten postcards to my classmates. That trip was wonderful. I learned about a new culture and made new friends. “Travel opens your eyes,” my father said. “The world is big and beautiful.” I agree. I want to travel to more places and learn more about the world.

readings.title: The Map and the Treasure 地图与宝藏
readings.text: Add a little imagination, and every map can lead to a treasure. Last weekend, my grandfather showed me an old map. “This map is from my father,” he said. “It shows the way to a hidden treasure.” I was excited. “Really? Let’s find it!” I said. “Not so fast,” he laughed. “First, we must read the map carefully.” The map was old and yellow. There were strange signs and lines on it. “This mark means a river,” my grandfather said. “And this one means a bridge.” We followed the map to a park. “The treasure is near the old tree,” he said. We walked around the tree. “Look! There is a box!” I shouted. I opened the box. Inside, there were old photos and letters. “This is the treasure?” I asked. My grandfather smiled. “Yes. These are letters from your great-grandfather. They are worth more than gold.” He told me about his father’s life. “He was a soldier, and he wrote these letters during the war,” he said. I read one letter. It was full of love and hope. “Dear family, I miss you. One day, we will be together again. Keep smiling,” it said. I felt tears in my eyes. “This is a real treasure,” I said. My grandfather nodded. “Family memories are the most precious treasure,” he said. “Never forget where you come from.” We took the letters home and put them in a safe box. That night, I thought about my great-grandfather. He was brave and kind. “I want to be like him,” I said. My grandfather smiled. “You already are,” he said. The map taught me that the greatest treasure is not gold or silver. It is love, family, and memory.

readings.title: Grandpa’s Medal 爷爷的奖章
readings.text: Age cannot stop a true hero. My grandfather is eighty years old, but he still tells us stories about his youth. “Look at this medal,” he says. “It is my greatest treasure.” The medal is old and a little dirty, but it shines in the light. “I got it during the war,” he says. “We fought bravely to protect our country.” He tells us about his friends. “Some of them never came back,” he says quietly. “They gave everything for peace.” His eyes become wet. “We must never forget them,” he says. My grandfather was a soldier. He was young then, full of energy and hope. “The war was terrible,” he says. “But we had to fight. Freedom is worth everything.” After the war, he became a teacher. “I wanted to build a better future,” he says. “Education is the key to peace.” He taught for forty years. Many of his students became doctors, teachers, and engineers. “They are my real medals,” he laughs. Every year, on a special day, he puts on his old uniform and wears his medal. “I am proud of my past,” he says. “But I am also proud of my country today.” He teaches us to love our country and help others. “Be kind, work hard, and never give up,” he says. “That is the best way to honour the past.” I love my grandfather. He is not famous, but he is a hero in my heart. His medal is small, but it carries a big story. One day, I will tell that story to my children. “Remember the past, treasure the present, and hope for the future,” my grandfather says. I will never forget his words.

readings.title: The Machine That Talks 会说话的机器
readings.text: Ago means “in the past.” Long ago, people dreamed of machines that could talk. Today, that dream has come true. Last month, our class visited a science museum. “Look! A robot!” my friend shouted. The robot was tall and silver. It waved at us. “Hello! Welcome to the museum!” it said. We were amazed. “It can talk!” I said. “How does it work?” “Inside the robot, there is a computer,” the guide explained. “It is full of information. The robot can understand our words and answer our questions.” We asked the robot many questions. “What is your name?” I asked. “My name is Robo,” it answered. “What is your favourite food?” my friend asked. “I don’t eat food. I need electricity!” the robot laughed. We all laughed too. The guide told us that robots can help people in many ways. “They can clean, cook, and even save lives,” she said. “In hospitals, robots help doctors do operations.” I was very interested. “I want to make robots one day,” I said. “That is a great dream,” the guide said. “Study science and maths, and you can do anything.” After the visit, I could not stop thinking about robots. “The future is full of machines,” I told my mother. She smiled. “But remember, machines are made by people,” she said. “The most important machine is the human brain. Use it well.” I understood. Technology is wonderful, but people are the real power. That visit changed my life. Now I study harder than before. I want to be an inventor and create machines that help the world. “Dream big,” the guide said. “And work hard to make your dream come true.” I will.

readings.title: A Small Act of Kindness 小小的善举
readings.text: Aid comes in many forms. Sometimes a small act of kindness can change a life. That is what happened to me last year. One rainy afternoon, I saw an old woman standing at the bus stop. She looked cold and tired. “Excuse me, are you okay?” I asked. “I missed my bus,” she said. “And I am very hungry.” I had a sandwich in my bag. “Please take this,” I said. She looked surprised. “Are you sure?” she asked. “Of course,” I said. She ate the sandwich and smiled. “Thank you, my child. You have a kind heart,” she said. We talked for a while. Her name was Mrs Chen, and she lived alone. “My children are far away,” she said. “I miss them very much.” I felt sorry for her. “I will visit you,” I said. From that day on, I visited Mrs Chen every week. We drank tea and talked. I helped her clean her house and water her plants. “You are like a granddaughter to me,” she said. One day, she gave me a small gift. “This is a birthday present,” she said. “It was my daughter’s. She gave it to me long ago.” It was a beautiful necklace. “I can’t take this,” I said. “Please,” she said. “I want you to have it.” I wore it and thanked her. That necklace reminds me of Mrs Chen every day. “Kindness is like a seed,” my mother says. “You never know how big it will grow.” She is right. A small sandwich became a beautiful friendship. I learned that helping others brings us happiness. “The world is full of people who need help,” my mother says. “Open your heart, and you will find love everywhere.”

readings.title: The Tortoise and the Marathon 乌龟与马拉松
readings.text: Aim high, but never forget the small steps. My school held a marathon last spring. “Every class must join,” the headmaster said. “It is not about winning. It is about trying your best.” My class chose Tom to run. Tom was not fast. In fact, he was slow, like a tortoise. “You will lose!” the other students laughed. But Tom did not care. “I will try my best,” he said. On the day of the race, the weather was perfect. The sun was warm, and the sky was blue. The runners gathered at the start line. “Ready? Go!” the teacher shouted. Everyone ran fast. But Tom ran slowly and steadily. “Come on, Tom!” we shouted. At first, he was far behind. “Don’t give up!” we cried. Tom smiled and continued. He ran one kilometre, then two. “My legs hurt,” he said. “But I must finish.” Meanwhile, other runners became tired. Some stopped to rest. Some gave up. But Tom kept going. “Slow and steady wins the race,” he said to himself. At the end, Tom crossed the finish line. He was not the first, but he finished! We cheered loudly. “You did it, Tom!” we shouted. Tom smiled and fell to the ground, tired but happy. “I did my best,” he said. The headmaster gave him a special prize. “This is for the bravest runner,” he said. Tom taught us a valuable lesson. “It doesn’t matter how fast you go,” he said. “What matters is that you never give up.” We learned that success is not about winning. It is about trying, learning, and growing. From that day on, we respect Tom even more. He is our hero.

readings.title: The Young Reporter 年轻记者
readings.text: Air is free, and so is a good story. My sister is a young reporter for a newspaper. “I love my job,” she says. “Every day, I meet new people and hear new stories.” Last month, she had an interesting experience. A hotel in our city was going to close. “The old hotel has a long history,” she said. “I want to write a story about it.” She visited the hotel and talked to the manager. “This hotel is fifty years old,” he said. “Many famous people have stayed here. Look at these photos on the wall.” The photos showed actors, singers, and politicians. “This is a treasure,” my sister said. She also talked to an old waitress. “I have worked here for thirty years,” the waitress said. “This hotel is my home.” Her eyes were full of tears. My sister wrote a beautiful story about the hotel. It was published on the front page. Many people read it and felt sad. “We must save this hotel!” they said. The city government decided to keep the hotel open. “Your article changed everything!” the manager told my sister. He thanked her again and again. My sister smiled. “I just told the truth,” she said. “Stories have power. They can change the world.” I am proud of my sister. She taught me that words are important. “Use your words carefully,” she says. “They can hurt or heal. Choose them with love.” From that day on, I also want to be a reporter. I want to tell stories that help people. “Follow your heart,” my sister tells me. “And never stop learning.”

readings.title: The Firefighter and the Cat 消防员与猫
readings.text: All of us were surprised that morning. A cat was stuck in a tree near our school! “Meow! Meow!” it cried. “Poor thing!” my friend said. “How can we help it?” We tried to reach the cat, but the tree was too tall. “We need help,” I said. We called the fire station. Soon, a fire truck arrived. “Don’t worry, little cat!” a firefighter shouted. He climbed the ladder carefully. The cat was scared and moved higher. “Come here, kitty,” the firefighter said softly. He held out his hand. Slowly, the cat came to him. “Got you!” he said. He carried the cat down. The crowd cheered! “Thank you!” a little girl said. “That is my cat, Mimi!” She hugged her cat and cried with joy. The firefighter smiled. “Be careful, Mimi,” he said. “Don’t climb trees anymore!” Everyone laughed. That afternoon, we watched the fire truck drive away. “Firefighters are heroes,” I said. “They save people and animals.” My teacher nodded. “They are brave and kind,” she said. “We should respect them.” The next day, I wrote a thank-you letter to the fire station. “Thank you for saving Mimi,” I wrote. “You are the best!” They wrote back and said, “We are happy to help. It is our job.” I learned something important that day: heroes are all around us. They are not just in movies. They are the people who help others every day. “Be kind. Be brave. Help where you can,” my mother says. I will always remember the kind firefighter and his smiling face.

readings.title: The Night of the Quake 地震之夜
readings.text: And then, the earth began to shake. It was a quiet night, and we were sleeping. Suddenly, the whole room moved. “Earthquake! Get under the table!” my father shouted. We were scared, but we remembered our training. We hid under the strong table and held on. The quake lasted for about a minute. Then everything became quiet. “Is everyone safe?” my mother asked. We checked each other. Nobody was hurt. “Thank goodness!” she said. But our house was damaged. The walls had cracks, and the windows were broken. “We must be careful,” my father said. “There may be more shakes.” We went outside. The streets were full of people. “Are you okay?” our neighbours asked. “Yes, we are fine,” we said. A young man brought us water. “Stay strong,” he said. “We will get through this together.” The next morning, soldiers came to help. They brought tents, food, and medicine. “Don’t worry. The government will help us rebuild our homes,” an officer said. “No one will be left alone.” We stayed in a tent for a week. It was not comfortable, but we felt safe. “We have each other,” my mother said. “That is the most important thing.” Slowly, our town recovered. Workers rebuilt the houses. Farmers returned to their fields. The shops opened again. “We are strong,” my father said. “This disaster taught us to value our life and love our neighbours.” I learned a lot from that night. In difficult times, people help each other. Kindness is the best medicine. “When we stand together, nothing can break us,” my mother said. She was right. Our town became stronger than before.

readings.title: The Big Storm 大风暴
readings.text: Ant or elephant, every life is precious. That was the lesson we learned during the big storm. It started on a summer afternoon. The sky turned dark, and the wind began to blow. “A storm is coming!” my grandfather said. “We must prepare.” We brought the animals inside and closed the windows. The storm arrived at night. The rain fell heavily, and the wind howled. “I am scared,” my little sister cried. “Don’t worry,” I said. “We are safe here.” We sat together and waited. Suddenly, we heard a loud noise. A tree had fallen on our roof! “We must move to the next room,” my father said. We stayed up all night, listening to the storm. In the morning, the storm stopped. We went outside and saw the damage. Trees were down, and the streets were full of leaves. “Look at the school!” my mother said. Part of the roof was gone. “We must help,” my father said. We went to the school and began to clean. Many neighbours came too. “Together, we can fix anything,” someone said. We worked all day. We collected the broken wood and carried the books inside. By evening, the school was clean again. “Thank you for your help!” the teacher said. “You are great neighbours.” That night, I thought about the storm. “Nature is powerful,” I said. “But people are stronger when they work together.” My father nodded. “Remember this,” he said. “In every difficulty, there is a chance to show kindness.” I will never forget that storm and the warm hearts of our neighbours.

readings.title: The Spaceship Dream 太空船之梦
readings.text: Any child can dream of space. Last year, our school held a science exhibition about space. “This is a model of a spaceship,” the teacher said. “It can travel to the moon and Mars.” We were amazed. “How does it work?” I asked. “It uses special fuel,” the teacher explained. “And it has a computer to guide it.” The exhibition was wonderful. We saw pictures of the moon and the stars. We learned about the sun and the planets. “Look! This is our earth from space,” my friend said. “It is so blue and beautiful.” I looked at the picture and felt proud. “We live on a wonderful planet,” I said. After the exhibition, I could not stop thinking about space. “I want to be an astronaut,” I told my mother. “That is a big dream,” she said. “But remember, even astronauts started as children. Study hard, and you can make your dream come true.” I began to read books about space. I learned about the stars and the planets. “The universe is so big,” I said. “And we are so small. But we can still reach for the stars.” My teacher encouraged me. “You have a curious mind,” she said. “Keep asking questions. That is how great scientists are born.” Now I study science and maths every day. “The sky is not the limit,” I tell myself. “The only limit is your imagination.” One day, I will build a real spaceship and travel to the stars. I will look back at the earth and remember this dream. “Never give up,” my mother says. “The stars are waiting for you.”

readings.title: The Night at the Opera House 歌剧院之夜
readings.text: Are you ready for a wonderful night? Last month, our school choir was invited to sing at the city opera house. It was a great honour! “This is a big chance,” our teacher said. “We must practise hard.” We practised for weeks. We sang the same song again and again. “Your voice is beautiful,” the teacher told us. “But you must sing together. One voice alone is not enough.” On the night of the concert, we were nervous. The opera house was huge and beautiful. “Look at the lights!” my friend whispered. “There are so many people!” I said. My heart was beating fast. “Don’t be afraid,” the teacher said. “Just sing from your heart.” We walked onto the stage. The audience became quiet. The music began. We opened our mouths and sang. Our voices filled the hall. It was like magic! When we finished, the audience clapped loudly. They stood up and cheered. “Bravo! Bravo!” they shouted. We bowed and smiled. Tears came to my eyes. “We did it!” I said. After the concert, many people came to congratulate us. “You were wonderful!” they said. “We will never forget this night.” That night taught me the power of teamwork. “Alone, we are just voices. Together, we are music,” our teacher said. I will never forget that night at the opera house. It showed me that with hard work and courage, we can do amazing things. “Dream big, and sing loud!” our teacher always says. I will.
readings.translation: 你准备好度过一个美妙的夜晚了吗？上个月，我们学校合唱团受邀在市歌剧院演唱。这是莫大的荣幸！“这是大好机会，我们必须努力练习。”老师说。我们练习了几周，一遍遍唱同一首歌。“你们的声音很美。”老师告诉我们，“但必须一起唱，一个人的声音不够。”音乐会当晚，我们很紧张。歌剧院又大又美。“看那些灯！”朋友低声说。“有这么多人！”我说。我的心跳得很快。“别怕，用心去唱。”老师说。我们走上舞台。观众安静下来。音乐响起。我们张开嘴唱歌，声音充满大厅。就像魔法一样！唱完时，观众热烈鼓掌，站起来欢呼。“好！好！”他们喊道。我们鞠躬微笑。我眼里涌出泪水：“我们做到了！”音乐会后，许多人来祝贺我们：“你们太棒了！我们永远不会忘记今晚。”那晚教会我团队合作的力量。“独自一人，我们只是声音；在一起，我们就是音乐。”老师说。我永远不会忘记歌剧院之夜。它让我明白：努力和勇气能让我们做出惊人的事。“大胆梦想，放声歌唱！”老师总是说。我会的。

readings.title: The Independent Farmer 自立的农民
readings.text: Arm yourself with knowledge, and you can face any challenge. My uncle is a farmer, but he is also a scientist. “Farming is not easy,” he says. “You must learn and try new things.” Ten years ago, his farm was small and poor. The soil was bad, and the crops were weak. “We cannot give up,” he said. “We must change.” He went to the city and studied at an agricultural school. He learned about new seeds and modern machines. “Knowledge is power,” he said. He returned to the farm with new ideas. He built a greenhouse and planted vegetables. He used new methods to save water. “Look at these tomatoes!” he said. “They are bigger than before!” His neighbours were surprised. “How did you do it?” they asked. “Come and learn,” he said. He taught them everything he knew. “If we help each other, we all succeed,” he said. The whole village improved. The farms became rich, and the people became happy. “You changed our lives,” the villagers said. My uncle smiled. “I just used my head,” he said. “And I never stopped learning.” Now my uncle is famous in our area. Students visit his farm to learn. “Agriculture is the future,” he tells them. “The world needs food, and it needs people who can grow food well.” My uncle taught me an important lesson: education can change our lives. “Never stop learning,” he says. “The more you know, the more you can do.” I want to be like him: a person who uses knowledge to help others.

readings.title: The Bookstore on the Corner 街角的书店
readings.text: Art is everywhere if you look carefully. My favourite place is a small bookstore near my school. It is old and a little dark, but it is full of treasures. The owner, Mr Gao, is a kind old man. “Welcome!” he always says. “Come in and look around.” I visit the bookstore every week. “I am looking for a good book,” I say. “What kind of books do you like?” he asks. “I love stories about adventures,” I say. He smiles and shows me a book. “This is a wonderful story,” he says. “A young man travels around the world and meets many people.” I read the book and love it. “Thank you, Mr Gao!” I say. One day, I found an old book in the bookstore. Its cover was broken, and the pages were yellow. “How much is this?” I asked. “It is not for sale,” Mr Gao said. “It was my father’s. He loved this book.” He showed me the book. It was a collection of poems. “Read this one,” he said. “It is about hope.” I read the poem and felt warm inside. “This is beautiful,” I said. Mr Gao smiled. “A good book is like a friend,” he said. “It is always there when you need it.” From that day on, I visit Mr Gao every week. We talk about books and life. He taught me that reading is a great gift. “Books open doors to new worlds,” he says. “Never stop reading.” I am grateful to Mr Gao. He is not just a bookstore owner. He is a teacher and a friend. Thanks to him, I love reading more than ever. I want to be like him one day: a person who shares the joy of books.
readings.translation: 只要仔细观察，艺术无处不在。我最喜欢的地方是学校附近的一家小书店。它又旧又有点暗，但满是珍宝。店主高先生是位善良的老人。“欢迎！”他总是说，“进来看看吧。”我每周都去书店。“我在找一本好书。”我说。“你喜欢什么类型的书？”他问。“我爱冒险故事。”我说。他笑着给我一本书：“这是个精彩的故事，一个年轻人环游世界，遇见许多人。”我读了那本书，非常喜欢。“谢谢您，高先生！”我说。一天，我在书店发现一本旧书。封面破了，纸页发黄。“这本多少钱？”我问。“这本不卖。”高先生说，“它是我父亲的，他爱这本书。”他给我看书，是一本诗集。“读读这首，是关于希望的。”他说。我读了诗，心里暖暖的。“真美。”我说。高先生笑了：“好书就像朋友，你需要时它总在那里。”从那天起，我每周都去看高先生，谈论书和生活。他教会我阅读是伟大的礼物。“书打开通往新世界的大门，永远不要停止阅读。”他说。我感激高先生。他不只是书店店主，还是老师和朋友。多亏他，我比以往更爱阅读。我想成为他那样的人：分享书的快乐。

readings.title: The Chemist’s Garden 化学家的花园
readings.text: Ash from the volcano made the soil rich. That is what my science teacher told us. “Nature is full of surprises,” she said. Last month, our class visited a chemist’s garden. It was not an ordinary garden. There were plants that could make medicine! “Look at this plant,” the chemist said. “It can help people with a headache.” We were amazed. “Can plants really be medicine?” I asked. “Of course,” he said. “Many medicines come from plants. For example, this one can stop pain.” He showed us many plants. “This one is for your stomach. This one is good for your eyes.” We took notes and asked questions. “How do you know which plant is useful?” my friend asked. “We study them carefully,” the chemist said. “It takes years of research. Sometimes we make mistakes, but we never give up.” He told us about his work. “I love my job,” he said. “Every day, I learn something new. Plants are amazing. They can feed us, heal us, and even clean the air.” He showed us a small laboratory. There were bottles, tubes, and many strange machines. “This is where we make medicine,” he said. “It is like cooking, but more careful!” We laughed. That visit opened my eyes. I learned that science is everywhere. “Look at the world with curious eyes,” the chemist said. “There is magic in every leaf.” Now I want to be a scientist. I want to discover new medicines and help people. “Follow your dream,” the chemist told me. “And never stop learning.” I will never forget his words.

readings.title: The Animal Hospital 动物医院
readings.text: Ask any vet, and they will tell you: animals need love too. My aunt is a vet. She works in a small animal hospital. “Every day is different,” she says. “I never know what will come through the door.” One morning, a farmer brought in a sick cow. “She will not eat,” he said. “She looks very weak.” My aunt examined the cow carefully. “Don’t worry. It is not serious,” she said. “She needs medicine and rest.” She gave the cow some medicine and told the farmer to take her home. “Bring her back next week,” she said. The farmer thanked her and left. That afternoon, a little boy came with a bird. “It fell from its nest,” he said. “Can you help it?” My aunt looked at the bird. Its wing was hurt. “We will take care of it,” she said. “Come back in a week.” The boy was happy. “Thank you, Doctor!” he said. My aunt worked all day. She treated a dog, a rabbit, and even a turtle. “I love my job,” she says. “But it is not easy. Sometimes animals are very sick, and we cannot save them. That makes me sad.” Her eyes became wet. “But we do our best,” she says. “That is all we can do.” My aunt also teaches people how to care for animals. “Give them good food and clean water,” she says. “Take them for walks. And most importantly, love them.” She is right. Animals are our friends. They give us so much joy. We should treat them with kindness. “Every life is precious,” my aunt says. “Big or small, every creature deserves love.” I am proud of my aunt. She is a hero to the animals and to me.

readings.title: The School After the Storm 风暴后的学校
readings.text: Bad days can make us stronger. Last autumn, a terrible storm hit our town. The wind was so strong that it blew off part of our school roof. “School will be closed for a week,” the headmaster announced. We were sad, but we knew we must help. “Let’s clean our school,” my teacher said. “We can do it together.” On Monday, we came to school with our parents. There were leaves and broken wood everywhere. “Be careful,” the teacher warned. “There may be broken glass.” We worked all morning. We collected the rubbish and carried the books inside. “Look at the classroom!” my friend said. The windows were broken, and the desks were wet. “Don’t worry,” my father said. “We can fix everything.” The workers came and repaired the roof. The parents cleaned the walls and floors. The students painted the desks. After three days, the school looked new again. “Welcome back!” the headmaster said. “Thank you for your hard work. You have shown us the power of teamwork.” We clapped and cheered. That experience taught me many things. I learned that we should never give up, even in difficult times. I learned that helping others makes us happy. “A small act can make a big difference,” my mother said. “Many small acts can change the world.” Now our school is stronger than before. We take better care of it. “This school is our home,” the headmaster says. “We should love it and protect it.” I will always remember that week. It showed me that when people work together, nothing is impossible. “Together, we can move mountains,” my teacher said. She was right.
readings.translation: 糟糕的日子能让我们更坚强。去年秋天，一场可怕的暴风雨袭击了我们镇。风大得吹掉了学校屋顶的一部分。“学校将停课一周。”校长宣布。我们很难过，但知道必须帮忙。“我们来打扫学校，一起努力。”老师说。周一，我们和父母来到学校。到处都是树叶和断木。“小心，可能有碎玻璃。”老师警告。我们干了一上午，清理垃圾，把书搬进屋里。“看教室！”朋友说。窗户破了，课桌湿了。“别担心。”爸爸说，“我们能修好一切。”工人们修好屋顶，家长们擦墙扫地，学生们刷课桌。三天后，学校焕然一新。“欢迎回来！”校长说，“谢谢你们的努力，你们展现了团队合作的力量。”我们鼓掌欢呼。那次经历教会我很多。我懂得了即使在困难时期也绝不放弃，懂得了帮助他人让我们快乐。“小举动能带来大不同，许多小举动能改变世界。”妈妈说。现在我们的学校比以前更坚固。我们更好地爱护它。“学校是我们的家，我们应该爱它、保护它。”校长说。我永远记得那一周。它让我明白：当人们团结时，没有什么是做不到的。“团结起来，我们能移山。”老师说。她说得对。

readings.title: The Dentist’s Promise 牙医的承诺
readings.text: Bag your worries and smile. That is what Dr Wang tells his patients. He is a dentist, and he is very kind. “The first time I saw a dentist, I was scared,” he says. “That is why I want to help children feel safe.” His clinic is warm and friendly. There are pictures on the walls and toys in the corner. “Look! A robot!” a little boy said. “It can move its arms!” Dr Wang smiled. “This is my helper,” he said. “It shows you how to brush your teeth.” The children loved it. “Open your mouth, please,” Dr Wang said softly. “This will not hurt.” He worked carefully and quickly. “All done! You are so brave!” he said. The boy smiled. “That was easy!” he said. “I am not scared anymore.” Dr Wang also visits schools. “Brush your teeth twice a day,” he tells the students. “Eat less sugar, and see the dentist twice a year.” The students listen carefully. “Why is it important?” a girl asked. “Because healthy teeth help you eat well and smile well,” he said. “A beautiful smile is a gift.” Dr Wang works long hours, but he never complains. “I love my job,” he says. “Seeing children smile makes me happy.” One day, a boy came to him with a bad tooth. He was very scared. “Don’t worry,” Dr Wang said. “I will be very careful. Hold my hand if you are afraid.” The boy held his hand and closed his eyes. After a few minutes, it was all over. “That was not bad!” the boy said. “Thank you, Doctor!” Dr Wang smiled. “You are very brave,” he said. That night, the boy told his mother: “I want to be a dentist like Dr Wang when I grow up!” Dr Wang heard about it and laughed. “That is the best reward,” he said.

readings.title: The Bookshop on a Sunny Day 阳光下的书店
readings.text: Ban the rush of daily life, and take a moment to read. That is the idea behind our little bookshop. Last Saturday, the weather was sunny, and I went there to buy a textbook. “Welcome!” the owner said. “Look around. You might find something interesting.” The bookshop was small but warm. Sunlight came through the window and fell on the shelves. I found a book about finance. “This is too difficult for me,” I thought. Then I saw a book of short stories. Its cover was colourful and cheerful. “This looks nice,” I said. I opened it and began to read. The stories were funny and interesting. “This is wonderful!” I said. I bought the book and went home. That evening, I sat in my room and read. The stories made me laugh and think. “Reading is like travelling,” my mother said. “Every book is a new world.” She was right. From that day on, I visit the bookshop every week. I have read many books now. I learned about history, science, and love. “A good book is a friend,” the owner says. “It never lets you down.” One day, I found an old book about the moon. “It was written a hundred years ago,” the owner said. “People used to dream about the moon. Now we have been there!” I was amazed. “How wonderful!” I said. “The world changes, but dreams never end.” The bookshop has taught me many things. It taught me to slow down and enjoy life. It taught me that knowledge is a treasure. “Never stop reading,” the owner says. “Books open the door to the world.” I will always love that little bookshop on the sunny street.

readings.title: The Café on the Corner 街角的咖啡馆
readings.text: Bar the door? No, the café is open! The little café on the corner is my favourite place. It is small and simple, but it is full of life. “Welcome!” the owner, Mrs Li, always says. “Sit down and relax. Would you like some coffee?” I go there every weekend. I sit by the window, drink coffee, and watch the street. “Life is like coffee,” Mrs Li says. “Sometimes it is sweet, and sometimes it is bitter. But it is always interesting.” She is a wise woman. She has worked in the café for twenty years. “I have seen many people come and go,” she says. “Students, workers, and old friends. Everyone has a story.” One day, a young man came in. He looked sad and tired. “What is wrong?” Mrs Li asked. “I lost my job,” he said. “I don’t know what to do.” Mrs Li gave him a cup of coffee. “Don’t give up,” she said. “Every cloud has a silver lining. Take your time. Something better will come.” The young man smiled a little. “Thank you,” he said. “Your words give me hope.” A few months later, he came back. “I found a new job!” he said happily. “And I want to thank you for your kindness.” Mrs Li smiled. “I didn’t do much,” she said. “I just gave you a cup of coffee and a few kind words.” “Sometimes that is all a person needs,” the young man said. The café taught me a lesson: small kindnesses can change a life. “Be kind to everyone you meet,” Mrs Li says. “You never know what they are going through.” I will never forget her words. I hope I can be as kind as Mrs Li.

readings.title: A Journey by Air 空中之旅
readings.text: Bat and owl, birds and planes — the sky is full of wonders. Last summer, I took my first flight. “Are you ready?” my father asked. “Yes!” I said, my heart beating fast. We arrived at the airport early. The terminal was huge and busy. “First, we must check in,” my father said. We showed our passports and got our tickets. Then we waited in the waiting room. “Look! A plane!” I shouted. The plane was big and white. “We will fly on that!” I said. When we got on the plane, a kind air hostess welcomed us. “Good morning! Welcome aboard!” she said. I sat by the window and looked out. The plane began to move. Faster and faster, it ran along the runway. Then it lifted into the air! “We are flying!” I shouted with joy. Below us, the city became small. The fields looked like a green carpet. The clouds were white and soft, like sheep. “This is amazing!” I said. “It is like a dream!” The flight was smooth. We had lunch on the plane. “Would you like chicken or fish?” the hostess asked. “Chicken, please!” I said. After two hours, the plane began to go down. “We are arriving,” my father said. I looked out of the window. I could see mountains and rivers below. “Our country is beautiful,” I said. The plane landed softly. “Thank you for flying with us,” the hostess said. That first flight was a wonderful experience. “The world is big,” my father said. “And now you have seen it from the sky!” I smiled. I will never forget that journey.

readings.title: The Beach in Summer 夏天的海滩
readings.text: Bay after bay, the coast stretches along the sea. Last August, my family spent a week at the beach. “This is the best holiday!” my little sister shouted. We stayed in a small hotel near the sea. Every morning, we got up early and ran to the beach. The sand was soft and warm under our feet. “Look! A shell!” my sister said. We collected shells and built sandcastles. “Let’s make a big castle!” I said. We worked together and made a beautiful castle. “It is like a palace!” my sister laughed. In the afternoon, we swam in the sea. The water was cool and clear. “Be careful!” my mother called. “Don’t go too far!” We also played beach volleyball. “You are a good player!” my father said to me. I smiled and felt proud. In the evening, we watched the sunset. The sky turned orange and pink. “What a beautiful view!” my mother said. We sat on the sand and ate ice cream. “This is the life!” my father said. One day, we went to a small fishing village. The fishermen were friendly and showed us their boats. “Would you like to go fishing?” one asked. “Yes!” we said. We went out on the sea and caught some fish. “This is so exciting!” I said. That week at the beach was wonderful. I learned to swim better and made new friends. “The sea is a gift,” my mother said. “We must protect it.” She was right. When we left, I was sad. “Can we come back next year?” I asked. “Of course!” my father said. I will always remember that happy week by the sea. The beach taught me that the simplest joys are often the greatest.

readings.title: The Museum of Light 光的博物馆
readings.text: Bed down in a city, and you will find art everywhere. Last week, I visited a special museum. It was called the Museum of Light. “This is a museum about light and colour,” the guide said. “Light is everywhere. It gives life to everything.” The museum was dark inside. “Look! Red light!” a child shouted. “Now it is blue!” The lights changed colours like magic. We walked through a room full of mirrors. “There are so many of me!” I laughed. In the next room, there were lasers. “Be careful,” the guide said. “Don’t look directly at the light.” We learned how light travels and how our eyes see. “Why is the sky blue?” I asked. “Because light bends in the air,” the guide explained. “That is a wonderful question!” There was also a room about the sun. “The sun is a giant ball of fire,” the guide said. “It gives us heat and light. Without it, there would be no life.” I looked at a model of the sun and felt small. “The universe is so big,” I said. At the end, we saw a beautiful rainbow. It was made by light passing through water. “Look! A rainbow!” everyone shouted. The guide smiled. “Nature is the greatest artist,” she said. “We just need to open our eyes.” That visit taught me to see the world differently. “Light is amazing,” I told my mother. “It is everywhere, but we rarely think about it.” She smiled. “That is true,” she said. “The most wonderful things are often the most common.” I will never forget the Museum of Light. It showed me that science is beautiful and full of magic.

readings.title: The Twin Cities 双子城
readings.text: Bee or butterfly, every creature has its own life. My uncle lives in a big city, and he told me a story about twin cities. “Long ago, there were two cities on the two sides of a river,” he said. “They were very different. The city on the east was rich, and the city on the west was poor.” The people in the rich city were proud. “We don’t need the poor city,” they said. They refused to help their neighbours. One year, a terrible flood came. The rich city was destroyed. “Help us!” the people cried. But the poor city had no boats. Just then, a brave young man from the poor city swam across the river with a rope. “Hold on to this!” he shouted. One by one, the people crossed the river. The poor city saved the rich city. “Thank you!” the rich people said. “We were wrong. We are one family.” From that day on, the two cities helped each other. They built a bridge and became one great city. “Teamwork makes us strong,” my uncle said. “When we work together, we can do anything.” I love that story. It taught me that we should help each other, no matter who we are. “Never look down on others,” my uncle said. “Everyone has value. Everyone can help.” He was right. In life, we all face difficulties. But if we stand together, nothing can stop us. “A friend in need is a friend indeed,” my grandmother always says. Now I try to help others as much as I can. I believe that kindness makes the world a better place.

readings.title: The Job Interview 求职面试
readings.text: Beg for nothing; work for everything. That is what my sister believes. Last month, she had a very important job interview. “This is my dream job,” she said. “I must do my best.” She prepared for a week. She read books about the company and practised her answers. “Be confident,” my mother said. “You are a good candidate.” On the day of the interview, she wore her best clothes. “Good luck!” I said. “Thank you!” she said. She arrived at the office early. The building was big and modern. “Please wait here,” the secretary said. My sister sat down and took a deep breath. “Don’t be nervous,” she told herself. “You can do this.” Finally, it was her turn. She walked into the office and smiled. “Good morning!” she said. The manager asked her many questions. “Why do you want this job?” he asked. “Because I love this work,” she said. “And I want to learn and grow.” She answered every question calmly and clearly. The manager nodded. “You have a good education and a warm heart,” he said. “Welcome to our team!” My sister could not believe her ears. “Really?” she said. “Really!” the manager laughed. “You are the best candidate we have seen.” My sister was so happy. She called us at once. “I got the job!” she shouted. We celebrated together that night. “Hard work pays off,” my mother said. My sister smiled. “I learned that preparation and confidence are the keys to success,” she said. I am proud of her. Her story teaches me: if you work hard and believe in yourself, you can achieve anything.

readings.title: The Lost Watch 丢失的手表
readings.text: Bid farewell to worry, and keep your patience. That is a lesson I learned from my grandfather. Last month, he lost his favourite watch. “It was a gift from my father,” he said. “I have worn it for forty years.” He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. “Don’t worry, Grandpa,” I said. “We will help you find it.” We searched his room. We looked under the bed and in the drawers. “It is not here,” my mother said. “Where did you put it last?” my father asked. My grandfather thought for a moment. “I remember! I wore it when I watered the garden,” he said. We went to the garden and looked carefully. The grass was long, and the flowers were bright. “Look! There it is!” I shouted. The watch was under a rose bush. My grandfather picked it up and smiled. “Thank you, my dear,” he said. “You are my lucky star.” He cleaned the watch and put it on. “It still works!” he said happily. That evening, he told me a story about the watch. “My father gave it to me when I was young,” he said. “He told me: ‘Time is precious. Use it well.’ I have never forgotten his words.” I looked at the watch. “Grandpa, will you give it to me one day?” I asked. He smiled. “Yes,” he said. “And I hope you will remember: time is the greatest gift. Never waste it.” I nodded. From that day on, I try to use my time well. “Time waits for no one,” my grandfather says. He is right. I will always remember that afternoon in the garden and the lesson about time.

readings.title: The Old Cathedral 老教堂
readings.text: Big or small, every building tells a story. Our town has a beautiful old cathedral. It was built three hundred years ago. “Look at the windows!” my friend said. “They are so colourful!” The windows were full of pictures made of glass. “They tell stories from the Bible,” my teacher explained. “People made them a long time ago.” We visited the cathedral with our class. “This is a treasure,” the guide said. “We must protect it.” Inside, it was quiet and peaceful. The sunlight came through the windows and made beautiful colours on the floor. “It is like magic!” I whispered. The guide told us about the history of the cathedral. “Many famous people have visited here,” she said. “Kings, queens, and presidents.” We walked around and looked at the old paintings. “This one is five hundred years old!” the guide said. “How do they keep it so clean?” I asked. “The cleaners work very carefully,” she said. “They use special tools and soft cloths.” I was impressed. “I want to be a cleaner here one day,” I joked. Everyone laughed. After the visit, I thought about the cathedral. “It is not just a building,” I said. “It is a piece of history.” My teacher nodded. “We must respect our history,” she said. “It teaches us where we come from.” That visit made me love history. I want to learn more about the past. “The past is a treasure,” my grandmother says. “Keep it safe, and it will teach you many things.” She is right. I will never forget the old cathedral and its beautiful windows.

readings.title: The Cook’s Little Helper 厨师的小帮手
readings.text: Bit by bit, the little girl learned to cook. Her name was Anna, and she loved helping her mother in the kitchen. “What are we making today?” she asked. “Cookies!” her mother said. “Do you want to help?” “Yes!” Anna said happily. She put on her apron and washed her hands. “First, we need flour and sugar,” her mother said. “Be careful with the cooker. It is hot!” Anna measured the flour carefully. “Now, add the butter and eggs,” her mother said. Anna mixed everything together. “It looks like mud!” she laughed. “That is normal,” her mother said. “Now we shape it into small balls.” Anna made little balls and put them on the tray. “Can I eat one now?” she asked. “Not yet!” her mother laughed. “We must bake them first.” They put the tray in the oven. “How long do we wait?” Anna asked. “Fifteen minutes,” her mother said. “Take your time. Good things take time.” Anna waited and waited. The kitchen began to smell wonderful. “I can smell the cookies!” she said. Finally, the cookies were ready. They were golden and warm. “They look delicious!” Anna said. She took one and bit into it. “Mmm! This is the best cookie in the world!” she said. Her mother smiled. “You are a good cook,” she said. From that day on, Anna helped in the kitchen every weekend. She learned to make cakes, bread, and soup. “Cooking is fun,” she said. “And it makes people happy.” One day, she cooked dinner for the whole family. “This is wonderful!” her father said. “Thank you, my little chef!” Anna smiled. “I love you all,” she said. Cooking taught Anna patience and love. “When you cook with love, everything tastes better,” her mother said. Anna never forgot those words.
readings.translation: 一点一点，小女孩学会了做饭。她叫安娜，喜欢在厨房帮妈妈。“今天做什么？”她问。“饼干！”妈妈说，“想帮忙吗？”“想！”安娜高兴地说。她系上围裙，洗了手。“首先，我们需要面粉和糖。”妈妈说，“小心炉子，很烫！”安娜仔细量面粉。“现在加黄油和鸡蛋。”妈妈说。安娜把一切混合起来。“看起来像泥！”她笑了。“这很正常。”妈妈说，“现在把它们揉成小球。”安娜做小球，放在烤盘上。“我能现在吃一个吗？”她问。“还不行！”妈妈笑了，“我们得先烤。”她们把烤盘放进烤箱。“要等多久？”安娜问。“十五分钟。”妈妈说，“慢慢来，好事需要时间。”安娜等啊等。厨房开始飘出美妙的香味。“我闻到饼干的香味了！”她说。终于，饼干好了，金黄温热。“看起来真好吃！”安娜说。她拿了一块咬一口：“嗯！这是世界上最好吃的饼干！”妈妈笑了：“你是好厨师。”从那天起，安娜每个周末都在厨房帮忙。她学会了做蛋糕、面包和汤。“做饭很有趣。”她说，“而且让人开心。”一天，她为全家人做了晚饭。“太棒了！”爸爸说，“谢谢你，我的小厨师！”安娜笑了：“我爱你们。”做饭教会安娜耐心和爱。“带着爱做饭，一切都更美味。”妈妈说。安娜永远不会忘记这些话。
